title: Jeremiyah Love's lingering ankle issue could keep him out Sunday
summary: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice on Wednesday due to a lingering ankle issue.
full_text: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice on Wednesday due to a lingering ankle issue. His availability for Sunday's game against the Rams is in question. Love's right ankle sprain from the preseason has healed, coach Mike LaFleur said, but the left ankle has bothered him the past two weeks. "We want to get this ankle right ," LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website. That could mean Love taking a week off. He played 36 of 73 snaps in the loss to the Lions on Sunday, with 12 rushes for only 22 yards. "I'm going to try to be as candid as possible knowing that everyone is listening to this too," LaFleur said. "He's a tough dude. But you see how he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL and putting your foot down and cutting the way that you are capable of. "We all agree that as much as he wants to battle, hey, let's give it a little bit of rest and see how it is as the week goes on." Safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) also did not practice. Safety Kitan Crawford (ankle) and wide receiver/returner Devin Duvernay (ribs) were limited. Crawford is in his 21-day return-to-practice window. Safety Budda Baker, outside linebacker Josh Sweat and left guard Isaac Seumalo had their usual rest day.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tyler Shough: We can't let Gayle Benson's comments affect our daily process
summary: Saints owner Gayle Benson's decision to publicly air her frustrations about the team's 1-4 start earlier this week drew a lot of attention because of how blunt she was about her disappointment and how rarely she shares her views about the state of the franchise.
full_text: Saints owner Gayle Benson's decision to publicly air her frustrations about the team's 1-4 start earlier this week drew a lot of attention because of how blunt she was about her disappointment and how rarely she shares her views about the state of the franchise. Quarterback Tyler Shough was among those who caught what Benson had to say and he said on Wednesday that Benson "wasn't saying anything that wasn't already known" about how things have unfolded so far this season. Shough said that the team shares Benson's desire for better results and that they are not going to change their approach to the job because she has gone public with them. "You obviously see it, it’s all over social media," Shough said. "It doesn’t affect our day-to-day process and we can't let it regardless. We win a game and you're the greatest people ever, and you lose some games and it's the worst thing ever. So I've said it before: We're going to have a really good chance to go on a run here. I think it starts with controlling what we can and all of a sudden the narrative changes, or not and we continue to slip and we've got to find a way to control that." A trip to New Jersey to face the Giants will be the Saints' first chance to shift the narrative with a trip to Paris to face the Steelers and a bye week on tap from there. If they can get to that bye at 3-4, things should feel a little less pressured in New Orleans but the alternative won't have anyone resting easy about what kind of changes could be in the franchise's future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Malik Willis doesn't think he has a tell despite Jordan Battle intercepting him twice
summary: Bengals safety Jordan Battle said before Sunday's game that he was going to time Willis's passes because of how willis pats the ball before throwing. Then Battle had two interceptions.
full_text: Bengals safety Jordan Battle said before Sunday's game that he had identified a tendency of Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis to pat the ball before throwing, and that he was going to use that tendency to time his breaks on Willis's passes. At the time, it seemed like a foolish thing to say out loud, but Battle backed up his talk and intercepted Willis twice as the Bengals won. Still, Willis doesn't believe he has a tell. Asked after the game about Battle's comments, Willis indicated that he wasn't even sure who Battle was, asking a reporter to clarify which Bengals player had said he had a tell. "Who said that?" Willis asked. A reporter answered, "Jordan Battle." Willis then asked, "What number?" A reporter told Willis that Battle wears No. 27, and Willis said he didn't even realize that Battle had caught both of his interceptions. Willis incorrectly thought No. 44, linebacker Demetrius Knight, had caught one of the interceptions. "I thought 44 caught one. I thought 44 caught a pick. Either way, you said he caught both? Let's come on," Willis said. Willis disputed that the interceptions had anything to do with a tell. On one of the picks, Willis's hand was hit as he was throwing the ball, and on the other one, Willis felt pressure to his left, scrambled to his right and threw directly to Battle. "That's not a tell, he caught tipped balls. Good for him, that's what defenses are supposed to do at this level," Willis said. "They battled a ball down and the second one was a scramble drill mishap. That has nothing to do with tells. I don't think I patted either one of those. I don't think those are correlated." Willis said he had been told what Battle said but didn't put any stock in it. "I didn't think much of it. Everybody pats the ball. That's funny. Really funny," Willis said. It was the Bengals who had something to laugh about after the game, as Battle backed up his talk.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Texans are 1-4, but Will Anderson is playing like a Defensive Player of the Year
summary: Anderson leads the NFL in sacks and tackles for loss and leads the betting odds for the Defensive Player of the Year Award.
full_text: On a Texans team that hasn't had much to celebrate this season, defensive end Will Anderson is the NFL's leading candidate for the Defensive Player of the Year award. Anderson leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks through five games, which puts him on a record pace of 25.5 sacks in a 17-game season. Anderson has had at least half a sack in every game this season, and he's coming off his best game of the season, with three sacks on Titans quarterback Cam Ward. Anderson, who also has 10 tackles for loss, is the first NFL player to have at least 7.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss in his team's first five games since 2012, when J.J. Watt did it, also for the Texans. Unlike the league MVP award, which almost always goes to the quarterback on one of the best teams in the league, the voters are willing to give the Defensive Player of the Year award to players on bad teams. Last year it was Myles Garrett on the 5-12 Browns, and this year it may go to Anderson even if the Texans don't turn things around. The current betting odds have Anderson as the overwhelming favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year, with +125 odds. He's followed by Pittsburgh's T.J. Watt and Minnesota's Dallas Turner, both at +850. Houston made a huge investment in Anderson, first trading two first-round picks, a second-round pick and a third-round pick to move up and draft him third overall in 2023, then signing him to a three-year, $150 million contract extension this year. On a team that has been a massive disappointment, Anderson has been a bright spot.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaguars are first team since the merger not to allow a 40-yard rusher in first five games
summary: Opposing running backs have 83 carries for 210 yards against the Jaguars this season, an average of just 2.5 yards per carry.
full_text: No one can run the ball on the Jaguars. Through five games this season, the most rushing yards any player has gained in a game against the Jaguars was 39, by Broncos running back Jonah Coleman.. That makes the Jaguars the first team since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger not to allow an opposing player to rush for 40 or more yards in the first five games of a season. The last team not to allow a 40-yard rusher in the first five games was the 1969 Cowboys. Last year, the most rushing yards any player gained in a game against the Jaguars was 74, by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The Jaguars have now gone 23 consecutive games, counting last year's playoff game, without allowing a 75-yard rusher. Opposing running backs have totaled 83 carries for 210 yards against the Jaguars this season, an average of just 2.5 yards per carry. That's by far the best defense against running backs in the NFL this season. On Sunday in London the Jaguars face the Texans, who rank 31st in the league with 395 rushing yards this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Al Michaels won't complain if Prime Video wants to move on
summary: The legendary Al Michaels continues to call the biggest of NFL games, four decades after making his debut on Monday Night Football.
full_text: '' The legendary Al Michaels continues to call the biggest of NFL games, four decades after making his debut on Monday Night Football . Now in his fifth year with Thursday Night Football on Prime Video, the 81-year-old broadcasting icon realizes that, at some point, it will end. Appearing on Wednesday's edition of The Dan Patrick Show , Michaels addressed the question of when he'll know the time has come. “Well, either the people that I work for will tell me, or I’ll know myself , a combination,” Michaels said, via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing . “Let’s put it this way. The folks at Amazon and Prime have been fantastic. Fantastic to me.” After his initial three-year deal, Prime Video has extended the arrangement on a one-year basis, twice. If they don't do it again, Michaels will be fine with that. “If they come to me and say, 'You know, it’s time for us to move on.' . . . 'You guys have been fantastic. You’ve been great.' I’ve done the NFL for 41 years, which is half my life. Love it. But you know what? At a certain time, it’s time. And if they feel it’s time, great. And if I feel it’s time, I’ll know it. And I’ll say, ‘You know what? Thanks for the memories.'" We're the ones who should be thanking him. As we've said before, many won't appreciate how much of our sports-watching lives he has influenced until he's no longer part of it. And while there are plenty of highly competent voices out there, Michaels is one of the very best to ever do it — possibly the best of all of the play-by-play announcers. He has been able to land in a high-profile spot after his tenure at NBC ended before he likely wanted it to. We've been able to listen to him call games for another four-plus years, thanks to the fact that Prime Video hired him. So either he'll walk away or he'll get a nudge. Either way, Michaels's long and distinguished journey has much greater meaning than however the road ends. For me and many others, it won't be the same to go through a football season without hearing him calling a game every week.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Hurts won't say much about "very unique" calf injury that was disclosed last Friday
summary: Last week's injury report for the Eagles included a curious designation on Friday.
full_text: Last week's injury report for the Eagles included a curious designation on Friday. And Wednesday's comments from the player at the center of the issue served only to make it more curious. Quarterback Jalen Hurts was listed as fully participating in Friday's practice before the game against the Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday's game in London, and he was never downgraded to questionable or doubtful. When the question came up during his midweek press conference, here's what Hurts said: "It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game." There's a lot there, in not that many words. What would be "very unique" about a calf injury that didn't impact his practice reps? And why would it be a big secret? The complicating factor is that the Eagles flew to London on Friday. Did he require medical care in London? Would it be something that the team doctors were able to provide? Did he have to visit a local hospital for it? He said he was "nicked up" during the Rams game, but he wasn't on the injury report for Wednesday or Thursday. Was is it that could have happened on Sunday that would have resulted in symptoms on Friday. (A condition like compartment syndrome typically surfaces much more quickly.) Regardless, plenty of questions flow from what seems to be very innocuous and basic on the surface. Hurts's words deepen the mystery. He remains on the Week 6 injury report, in advance of Sunday's game against the Panthers. Hurts was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice, due to the calf injury. Whatever the explanation is, there's clearly more to the story than what the team has disclosed. And the NFL doesn't require much more than the bare-bones contents of the injury report.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bradley Chubb explains his side of altercation with Alaric Jackson
summary: Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson had his suspension reduced to one game on appeal Wednesday.
full_text: Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson had his suspension reduced to one game on appeal Wednesday. He will be on unpaid leave Sunday when the Rams play the Cardinals. Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb, who took a punch from Jackson after the game Monday night, said he learned a valuable lesson from the incident. "Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or wear a helmet ," Chubb said, via Nick Suss of ESPN. Chubb admitted he initiated the conversation between the two men after the Bills' 37-34 overtime victory. "I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb said at the practice facility on UC Irvine's campus, where the Bills are practicing this week. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again, and when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom." Chubb, who hasn't heard from Jackson since the punch, said he was proud he didn't retaliate and draw a suspension of his own. If the teams play again this season, it will be in the Super Bowl back at SoFi Stadium in February.
author: Charean Williams

title: Four men arrested in shooting of 49ers DL Keion White in February
summary: Police have arrested four men in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White earlier this year, the Associated Press reports.
full_text: ' Police have arrested four men in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White earlier this year, the Associated Press reports. White was hosting a private Super Bowl party in a nightclub in San Francisco when the shooting occurred in the early morning hours of Feb. 9. White was treated at a local hospital for gunshot wounds to his ankle. Investigators used video footage and witness statements to identify the multiple suspects with firearms who confronted White. San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said authorities arrested the suspects over the past week with the help of law enforcement agencies in Atlanta; Stockton, California; Irvine, California and Los Angeles. Curtis Green, 35, was arrested in Irvine on Oct. 7, and two days later, authorities arrested 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, California. Walker will be charged with assault with a semiautomatic firearm -- which prosecutors say he fired -- as well as other charges for having a gun as a felon. Green faces misdemeanor charges of brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed and loaded gun in public. Two other men arrested in other jurisdictions are not yet in local custody. White has appeared in all five games for the 49ers this season and has three sacks.

title: Nick Caserio: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade was finalized on Friday
summary: Deal was done before initial half-reports that failed to name destination.
full_text: Yes, the trade that sent receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals to the Texans was fully in place before Sunday . As it turns out, it was fully in place before Saturday. Via Cole Thompson of USA Today , Texans G.M. Nick Caserio said in an appearance on 95.7 The Fan in Houston that the trade was finalized on Friday evening . Caserio said that the Cardinals wanted to wait until Sunday to announce it. Most importantly, Caserio pushed back against the theory that the deal hinged on the Texans beating the Titans on Sunday. "What happened in the game had zero bearing on the outcome," Caserio said. "Like, we're not going to agree to something and then see what happens in a game and then back out of it." Caserio's comments make the initial half-report from ESPNFL even more bizarre. It's possible, if not likely, that the folks who broke the news that the Cardinals would be trading Harrison but who didn't identify the destination knew damn well where Harrison was going, but agreed not to name the Texans as part of the dealmaking that often happens when, coincidentally, the #insiders trade discretion for future considerations. It didn't take much effort (which qualified me for the assignment) to get to the bottom of the question of where Harrison was being traded . Bottom line? Per Caserio, the deal was done on Friday night. By Saturday morning, only part of the story was reported as part of the first news that Harrison's time in Arizona had ended. It made no sense then, and it makes even less sense now.
author: Mike Florio

title: Hearing officer Derrick Brooks reduces Alaric Jackson's suspension to one game
summary: Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
full_text: Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson will be suspended for sucker punching Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. But Jackson won't miss two games. Hearing officer Derrick Brooks has reduced Jackson's suspension to one game on appeal. It's possible that Jackson's case included evidence regarding the provocation from Chubb that preceded the approach. Chubb may have said something that made the punch less unreasonable. Or not so unreasonable to support a two-game suspension. Jackson will still serve a one-game suspension, missing Sunday's game against the Cardinals. At a base salary of $16.822 million, he'll lose $934,555. That may have been a factor in the final decision. Apart from the time missed, Jackson was looking at losing nearly $2 million on a two-game suspension. Regardless, Jackson is fortunate to be missing only one game. He punched Chubb minutes after the game ended. Hot blood should have cooled by then. And Jackson likely would have been arrested if he'd done it in the parking lot instead of in the middle of the field.
author: Mike Florio

title: 8.1 million watched Eagles-Jaguars
summary: Same city.
full_text: Same city. Same stadium. Same day of the week. Same kickoff time. Different teams. Far different numbers. The Colts-Commanders game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London averaged fewer than five million viewers in Week 4. In Week 5, Eagles-Jaguars generated 8.1 million viewers . It was the second most-watched international game on NFL Network, with a 36-percent increase over the 2025 average of 6.2 million. The series continues this weekend, when the Texans face the Jaguars at Wembley Stadium in London. In Week 7, the Steelers face the Saints in Paris. Sunday's game lasted three hours and 42 minutes, trickling into the 1:00 p.m. ET window — and likely taking a major chunk out of the ratings for the pregame shows on ESPN, Fox, and CBS. If/when (when) the NFL secures the ability to stage 16 international games per season, the 9:30 a.m. ET window will become commonplace. At some point, it will be fair to ask whether the morning/afternoon pregame shows should go the way of the dodo bird. With so much more analysis and content available in advance of the Sunday games than ever before, the Sunday morning/afternoon pregame shows really don't add much. They add even less when, you know, a game is being televised at the time the pregame shows are on. Indeed, if/when (when) the NFL sells the Sunday morning European package to the highest bidder, whoever wins the rights may request that the NFL direct its other broadcast partners to stand down from 9:30 a.m. ET to 1:00 p.m. ET on every Sunday when a game is being played.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kellen Moore on Gayle Benson's comments: We all want the same thing
summary: Saints owner Gayle Benson didn't pull any punches in her assessment of the team's start to the season in a speech on Tuesday.
full_text: Saints owner Gayle Benson didn't pull any punches in her assessment of the team's start to the season in a speech on Tuesday. Benson said that the team's fans are right to be upset about their play during a 1-4 start and that she "will not accept this level of performance as our standard." Benson also said she is "committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team" and it was hard not to read those comments as a mandate for those currently in charge of the team to show that improvement or find new places to work. That group includes head coach Kellen Moore and his Wednesday press conference opened with several questions about Benson's speech. Moore said he did not feel an increased sense of urgency because he already understood that "we all want better results" and that everyone in the organization is doing all they can to create them. "It’s where we’re at . We’re 1-4, missed a few opportunities right there," Moore said. "We all want the same thing. We’re all shooting for that. We’ve all got the same objectives and we just gotta get better moving forward." Wanting the same things that Benson is talking about and achieving them are different things, which makes it all the more incumbent on Moore and the rest of the staff showing that they can do the latter before ownership decides that someone else will have a better chance of succeeding.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders open TE Carter Runyon's 21-day practice window
summary: The Raiders designated tight end Carter Runyon to return Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: '' The Raiders designated tight end Carter Runyon to return Wednesday, the team announced. It opens Runyon's 21-day practice window, and the team can activate him back to the active roster at any point in the next three weeks. Runyon went on injured reserve on Aug. 30 with an undisclosed injury after not playing in the preseason. He became eligible to return last week after missing four games. Runyon played 13 games last season, seeing action on 45 offensive snaps and 206 on special teams. He made two tackles and caught one pass for 3 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Buck, Troy Aikman reportedly have "tension" in what could be last year of their partnership
summary: The next time he "welcomes you into the broadcast booth" during a Monday night game, Joe Buck could be looking for backup.
full_text: The next time he "welcomes you into the broadcast booth" during a Monday night game, Joe Buck could be looking for backup. As reported by Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , " there has been tension " between long-time on-air partners Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. It comes at a time when Buck has gotten a new five-year deal to remain with ESPN/ABC and Aikman has not. Glasspiegel explains that, during Monday night's game between the Bills and Rams at SoFi Stadium in L.A., Buck "broke the ice" on the situation, prompting an argument between the duo. The situation de-escalated, and there was no sign of any issue during the actual broadcast. The situation suggests that ESPN/ABC will be looking (if they aren't already) to replace Aikman after the season ends. The fact that Buck did his deal without Aikman's deal being done implies that Buck has no qualms about making a change after a quarter of a century with the Hall of Fame quarterback.
author: Mike Florio

title: Colts list Daniel Jones as full practice participant with ankle injury
summary: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones landed on the team's injury report for the first time this season on Wednesday.
full_text: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones landed on the team's injury report for the first time this season on Wednesday. An ankle injury is given as the reason for Jones's presence on the list. He was listed as a full participant, so it does not appear it will impact his availability for the Titans unless his participation level drops in the coming days. Wide receiver Keenan Allen (rest), linebacker Jayden Carlies (ribs), wide receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring), offensive tackle Jalen Travis (ankle), and cornerback Charvarius Ward (rest) did not practice on Wednesday. Wide receiver Josh Downs (rest, hamstring), guard Matt Goncalves (concussion evaluation), running back Jonathan Taylor (rest), and defensive end J.T. Tuimoloau (concussion evaluation) were limited participants. Tight end Will Mallory (thumb) and wide receiver Darius Slayton (knee) were full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalen Ramsey out of Steelers practice, Jamel Dean limited
summary: Cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean were both on the Steelers' injury report to open Week 6.
full_text: Cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean were both on the Steelers' injury report to open Week 6. Ramsey did not practice due to a wrist injury. That was also the case in Week 5, but Ramsey returned for limited practices the rest of the week and had nine tackles in their win over the Colts. Dean was inactive for that game due to an ankle injury, but he was limited in Wednesday's practice and that could bode well for his chances of playing against the Buccaneers this week. Running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was also limited after missing last Sunday's game. Safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and linebacker T.J. Watt (rest) were the other Steelers in the limited category. Wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) did not practice and they've been ruled out for this week. Defensive linemen Keeanu Benton (ankle) and Cam Heyward (rest) were also out of practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: QB Bryce Young a full participant; RT Monroe Freeling and RB AJ Dillon did not practice
summary: The Panthers are returning from their off weeks, so they practiced Tuesday instead of Wednesday.
full_text: The Panthers are returning from their off weeks, so they practiced Tuesday instead of Wednesday. They released their first injury report of the week on Wednesday. Rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) and veteran running back AJ Dillon (ankle) were the only players listed as not practicing. Left guard Damien Lewis (elbow), outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), tight end Tommy Tremble (ribs) and tight end Darren Waller (toe) were limited. The other six players listed on the report were listed as full participants, including quarterback Bryce Young (knee), wide receiver Jalen Coker (quad) and linebacker Thomas Incoom (ribs). The other three players who fully participated — offensive tackle Taylor Moton (lungs, blood clot), defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton (neck) and running back Trevor Etienne (ankle) — are in their 21-day return-to-practice window. This is the second week Young is on the report, but he has fully participated in all four practices since injuring his knee.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lamar Jackson remains out of practice Wednesday
summary: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter called the quarterback day-to-day with an ankle injury.
full_text: A report on Wednesday indicated that there's a realistic chance of quarterback Lamar Jackson playing against the Browns on Sunday, but there was no change to his status when the Ravens took the practice field later in the day. Jackson missed practice all of last week due to an ankle injury and he remained off the field during the team's first practice of Week 6. Head coach Jesse Minter didn't make any guesses about when he will be back, but said that the quarterback is doing what's needed to return to action. "I think it’s definitely day-to-day ," Minter said. "I think a lot of times those things, right when they happen, you're not sure. You gather information, you look at stuff. To Lamar's credit, he's working his butt off. He's doing everything he can to be out here. When he's able to be, he will." Tyler Huntley started in place of Jackson last Sunday and helped the Ravens to an overtime win over the Falcons. Rookie Joe Fagnano is the team's third quarterback.
author: Josh Alper

title: KC Concepcion will practice on Wednesday, working through concussion protocol
summary: Browns receiver KC Concepcion will practice on Wednesday after suffering a concussion during Sunday’s loss to the Jets.
full_text: Browns receiver KC Concepcion will practice on Wednesday after suffering a concussion during Sunday’s loss to the Jets. Concepcion was hit hard by New York safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, staying down for a while before eventually standing up and heading to the locker room under his own power. The No. 24 overall pick of this year’s draft, Concepcion has caught 18 passes for 149 yards so far this season. He’s also returned four punts. While it’s unclear if Concepcion will clear concussion protocol in time to play on Sunday, head coach Todd Monken told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that the team isn’t ruling anyone out for this week at this point. Notably, running back Dylan Sampson will return to practice on Wednesday, opening up his 21-day window as he returns from injured reserve. But several Browns are not slated to practice, including running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), and defensive tackle Mason Graham (knee/ankle). Cleveland’s full Wednesday injury report will be released later in the day.

title: Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. breaks silence after missing Week 5 game and how much does he plan to play at Packers
summary: Porter Jr. began to feel sick on the day of Dallas' Thursday Night Football game in Week 5
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. knew he was in trouble on Thursday morning, the day of his new team's "Thursday Night Football" showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Porter Jr., who the Cowboys acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans. He and the team were ramping up for him to be a full-time starter after being on the roster for a week, but those plans changed quickly when he woke up that day.
He had an itchy throat in the morning, and that feeling stuck with him during morning walkthroughs with his Cowboys teammates. Porter Jr. reported feeling ill to the team, and they gave him cold medicine to deal with his symptoms. By the time it was time to drive down from Frisco, where Dallas' team facility is located, to Arlington, where AT&T Stadium is just over 35 miles down the road, Porter Jr. was ready to vomit. He told his Uber driver to floor it to the stadium, so that he could go ahead and vomit when he arrived. That's when he and the team knew he wouldn't be suiting up Thursday night.
"I really just couldn't hold anything down. I just kept throwing up," Porter Jr. said Wednesday after practice, his first media availability since the illness. "I tried to fight through it. I tried taking a nap before the game to shake it off, but I couldn't hold anything down. That's when they made the call to send me home. ... Throughout the day, it just kept getting worse and worse. On my way to the game when I was throwing up outside of my Uber on the way to the game, it was brutal. Not going to lie."
Week 5 was supposed to be Porter Jr.'s home opener against a winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers team starting Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie making his second career start. A happy coronation in front of his new home fans was all lined up. Instead, Porter Jr. ended up watching Dallas lose from home in a shocking 24-16 defeat.
"It was very frustrating. I was prepared to play all week. The mind was playing. The mindset was to get the dub," Porter Jr. said. "Obviously, I didn't get to do that, and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed in my couple days off."
Not that it excuses Dallas' poor performance, particularly on defense where they allowed a whopping 241 yards rushing, but Thursday was the Cowboys' third game in 12 days. That stretch also included two 10-hour flights from Dallas to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. They were all worn out. Energy is much higher around the locker room, especially from Porter Jr., with a 10-day gap between Thursday and their "Sunday Night Football" matchup at the Green Bay Packers (3-2) in Week 6. The layoff especially helped Porter, who will now have been a Cowboy for 17 days before he takes the field with a higher workload.
"I feel great. Those extra days definitely helped. Helped me lock in with the playbook too. It was win-win. I was mad I couldn't be out there with the guys on that Thursday night," Porter Jr. said. "I was beating myself up, and my dad was just telling me 'keep the main thing the main thing and focus on what we have ahead of us.' That's Green Bay."
With a higher comfort with the Cowboys' playbook, does that mean Porter Jr. will be a full-time starter on Sunday? Yes, yes, it does.
"Definitely," he said with a soft smile. "That's what I'm shooting for, and that's what they're [the coaching staff] shooting for as well, so that's what we're going to try to do."
His return is crucial for a Dallas secondary that has the highest opposing passer rating (120.5) in the entire league entering Week 6. Especially since the Green Bay Packers' passing attack is full steam ahead after a 31-7 Week 5 demolition of the Chicago Bears on Sunday. Quarterback Jordan Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, with much of his damage coming in explosive play chunks. He went big-game hunting over and over to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches). That made Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016.
Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006.
However, Porter Jr. sees Love's eagerness to let it rip downfield as an opportunity for him and a Cowboys defense that has gone three consecutive games without a takeaway, one game away from the longest streak in team history. Dallas is the only team in the NFL without an interception this season.
"I see that we have a lot of opportunities to make plays on the ball, so I know we're all excited for that," Porter Jr. said. "We really have to rally to the ball and make plays when they call on us to."
Cowboys edge rusher Rashan Gary, the Packers' 2019 first-round pick the year before Green Bay used their next one on Love in 2020, spent six of his seven seasons with the Packers practicing against Love every day. He's making sure his teammates have a healthy respect for the 27-year-old quarterback, now in his fourth year as an NFL starter.
"Swagger, confidence, his poise. Understanding defensive ID. Understanding the nickel's rotation. Understanding the coverage he is getting in the back. Able to find a way to get his playmakers the ball. A guy that is relentless," Gary said Wednesday. "A guy that wants to throw the ball, but if his lane is open, he will scramble. Just a true winner."
It will be interesting to see how much Love tries to go Porter Jr.'s way. In his Dallas debut against the Texans, Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud didn't target Porter Jr. during his 19 coverage snaps.
"It's a respect thing. That's how I look at it at the end of the day. If I'm not getting any work, that's the beautiful thing about defense," Porter Jr. "You can find your own work. If they're not looking toward you, that's when you need to get in the run game and show your presence. ... It can never be boring. There's always work out there. That's what I look forward to."
Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked total defense (395.4 total yards per game allowed), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. That's why they hired former Cleveland Browns head coach and Packers defensive coordinator Mike Pettine this week as a senior assistant to first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Porter Jr. sees that move and the decision to trade for him as investments in winning.
"It just shows that we're trying to get things done the right way, and we're trying to win. That's the main thing that everyone is focused on, to win," Porter Jr. said. "When you have guys all willing and able to put into the pile, that's when good things happen. That's what we're looking forward to."
So when will four steady quarters of action come for the Cowboys? They led the Buccaneers 10-7 before the meltdown occurred in the second half. Maybe Week 6 is the time.
"It's right there. We all watch the tape. We all know what we need to work on," Porter Jr. said. "It's a couple plays that are holding us back. If we just do what we need to do, those plays and those little miscues should be cleaned up."
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France as protests in Paris continue
summary: The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
full_text:
With protests on their third week in Paris and an NFL game scheduled to take place in the city in just 11 days, growing concern over fan and player safety has left some wondering if the league will alter any of its plans. But the NFL said on Wednesday that the game will go on as scheduled, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meeting on Oct. 25 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, located just north of Paris.
"We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25," the NFL said in a statement, via ESPN . "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."
The social unrest stems from demands for the government to change multiple aspects of the education system. Protestors are asking the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. Students say the schools are falling apart and rats are in the buildings.
The protests have sparked violence, with authorities using tear gas, stun grenades and various other means to attempt to stop the crowds. Protestors have reportedly set fires and caused damage. Police detained over 5,000 people in connection with protests, according to CBS News .
Local officials say they are investigating both the protests and the police response.
The French government is currently in a "political deadlock" as they approach the presidential elections in the spring. They have not responded to protestors with any plans or solutions for their complaints and demands.
If the situation in Paris escalates, the NFL could reconsider its stance, but right now, it is sticking with its original plan. The NFL has changed game locations in the past due to extreme weather or field conditions.
The Saints are considered the home team for the game, and their only listed event for the day in New Orleans is a private event where youth and amateur sports teams have the chance to play inside the stadium. It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. local time, so if needed, the game could seemingly be played at Caesar's Superdome. But that seems unlikely at the moment.
If the game does go on as planned, it will mark the first-ever NFL game played in France.
This will be the second straight year the Steelers play a game outside the United States, having played in Dublin last season against the Minnesota Vikings . The Saints last played an international game in 2022, visiting London to face the Vikings.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Shedeur Sanders just made a curious move that could signal a trade is coming in Cleveland
summary: Sanders' decision to hire an agent comes as Cleveland carries four healthy quarterbacks and speculation builds
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline coming up on Nov. 10, one of the most interesting names to watch in the trade rumor world is Shedeur Sanders .
The Browns quarterback made a curious move this week, and it's one that could possibly signify that he might be on his way out of Cleveland. Sanders hired an agent on Wednesday, according to ESPN , after spending the first part of his career without one. Sanders has signed on with Adie von Gontard (CEO of Young Money APAA Sports), who also represents Sanders' former college teammate, Travis Hunter .
The move was interesting for two big reasons:
1. As a player who was drafted in 2025, Sanders isn't allowed to start negotiating a new contract with his team until after the 2027 season, so it doesn't make a lot of sense for him hire an agent right now (If he's looking toward 2027, he could simply have waited until after the season to hire an agent).
2. The last notable player to hire an agent during the middle of the season was Marvin Harrison Jr . The former Cardinals receiver hired an agent for the first time on Oct. 9, and less than 24 hours later, Arizona leaked out news that he was being traded . By Oct. 11, the deal was done, and he was on his way to Houston.
The only reason it would make sense to hire an agent now is if you need some representation heading into the trade deadline. If you have an agent, they can sniff around and see if you're drawing any interest on the trade market, and if so, they could then try to convince your team that both sides would be better off if you moved on.
There's already been some speculation that the Browns are open to dealing a quarterback before the deadline. The team has four healthy quarterbacks in Sanders, Deshaun Watson , Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green .
Through the first four weeks of the season, Gabriel was on injured reserve, so it made sense to keep all four quarterbacks. Watson served as the starter while Sanders served as the backup with Green being a developmental project.
With Gabriel now healthy, there's no reason for the Browns to keep four quarterbacks, so it could certainly make a lot of sense to move on from either Sanders or Gabriel.
Before the season started, there was some speculation that Sanders might ultimately end up as the starting QB in Cleveland if Watson played poorly to start the year, but instead, he's got the Browns off to a 3-2 start, and he has three fourth-quarter comebacks. This is now Watson's team, which makes Sanders expendable.
Sanders did start seven games for the Browns last year, and new coach Todd Monken gave him a chance to win the job in training camp, but Watson ended up earning the starting spot. At this point, if another team shows any interest in Sanders, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Browns make a deal.
Here are a few teams that could make sense as a possible landing spot:
No one knows for sure if Shedeur is going to be traded, but he's certainly someone you're going to want to keep an eye on between now and the trade deadline.

title: Agent's Take: Making sense of Eagles' salary cap manipulation after Lane Johnson's retirement
summary: The Eagles kept Johnson on their 53-man roster after his abrupt Week 5 retirement. Here's a look at why and what they gain from it
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired due to personal reasons a couple of days after he was a surprise inactive for Week 4's contest against the Los Angeles Rams . The expectation was that the Eagles would put Johnson on the reserve/retired list because of his decision.
Instead, the Eagles, who have suffered a rash of injuries, are reportedly going to keep Johnson on the 53-man roster. The roster decision is for salary cap reasons and also allows Johnson to change his mind about playing at some point this season, which seems unlikely. Johnson cited focusing on his mental health as a primary reason for his retirement in a statement he posted on his Instagram page .
Johnson is making $23 million this year, consisting of a $1.3 million base salary and a $21.7 million option bonus. Half of the option bonus, or $10.85 million, has already been paid. The remaining $10.85 million is payable on December 1.
Option bonuses are prorated on a team's salary cap over the life of a contract (including the option years and up to a maximum of five years) beginning in the league year when the option is exercised. This means Johnson's $21.7 million is prorated on Philadelphia's salary cap at $4.34 million annually from 2026 through 2030.
I suspect the Eagles wouldn't have hesitated to put Johnson on the retired list if the entire $23 million had been base salary. In that case, Johnson would be forfeiting roughly $17.9 million (14/18ths of $23 million), which would have come as salary cap relief for the Eagles in 2026.
Retiring would typically put Johnson in breach of his contract, giving the Eagles the right to recoup money from him. Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement, an option bonus is only forfeitable if a breach occurs in the league year where the money is earned. Keeping Johnson on the 53-man roster means the Eagles won't be able to declare he is in breach and recover some of the 2026 option bonus. The Eagles don't have any recovery rights to Johnson's $18.79 million 2024 option bonus and $23.745 million 2025 option bonus because no breach occurred in either year.
The recoupment standard is different for signing bonuses. A team has a right to recover the prorated amount of a signing bonus in the current and future years of a contract when a player retires. The $18.835 million signing bonus Johnson received in 2023 still has $3.767 million prorated in 2026 and 2027 for salary cap purposes.
Some NFL teams are reluctant to enforce these rights, especially for a player with a Hall of Fame-worthy career like Johnson. (Though that didn't stop the San Francisco 49ers from getting money back from Hall of Fame linebacker Patrick Willis when he prematurely retired in 2015 after eight NFL seasons, according to a conversation I had with a 49ers front office executive a few years ago.)
If the Eagles processed Johnson's retirement in 2026 (when recoupment isn't pursued), they would have $42.89 million of 2027 dead money — a salary cap charge for a player no longer on a team's roster — from the bonus proration in Johnson's 2027 through 2030 contract years. Here's what the dead money would consist of:
The $42.89 million would be $18.06 million more than Johnson's listed 2027 cap of $24.83 million. Johnson would be off Philadelphia's books beginning in 2028.
The plan is for the Eagles to delay processing Johnson's retirement until next June 2 at the earliest. That's because only the current year's bonus proration counts toward the salary cap with players released, traded or retiring after June 1. The prorated bonus in future contract years is delayed until the following league year, which typically begins in early to mid-March.
By waiting so long to list Johnson as retired, this $42.89 million will be split into $16.614 million of dead money in 2027 and $26.276 million of dead money in 2028. That's likely what the Eagles were already planning for with Johnson previously stating 2026 would probably be his final season. In this scenario, Johnson's 2027 dead money is $8.216 million less than his current 2027 cap number.
The $16.614 million will be the 2027 prorated amount from Johnson's 2023 signing bonus and his three option bonuses from 2024, 2025 and 2026. The $26.276 million will be the prorated amount from the three option bonuses in the next three years of Johnson's contract.
Teams have delayed retirement processing before, but not quite to this extreme. For example, after Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees announced his retirement in March 2021, the New Orleans Saints kept him on the roster until June 11 because waiting was more advantageous from a salary cap standpoint.
There is speculation that the Eagles and Johnson's camp will work out how much of the 2026 option bonus will be retained, given his roster status. It wouldn't be surprising if the $10.85 million Johnson is due in December isn't paid.
The Saints and Derek Carr did something similar when the quarterback unexpectedly retired in May 2025 with an injured right shoulder. Carr kept the $10 million roster bonus for 2025 that he had already received. He forfeited the other $30 million he was scheduled to make in 2025, of which $28.745 million had been converted into a signing bonus for cap purposes. The Saints waived rights to $17.1 million of a 2023 signing bonus that was subject to recoupment due to his retirement.
For the Eagles, it remains to be seen how any potential savings from the 2026 option bonus would be treated under the salary cap. It's conceivable the savings would be applied proportionately. This would mean the 2026 through 2030 option bonus proration would be reduced by $2.17 million annually if the $10.85 million December payment isn't made. Under this scenario, there would be $34.21 million of 2027 dead money split into $14.444 million next year and $19.766 million in 2028.
