title: A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots opening up WR's practice window with return imminent
summary: Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in New England's season-opening loss to Seattle
full_text:
Help is on the way for the New England Patriots offense. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced that the team has opened up the practice window for receiver A.J. Brown , and he will be on the field on Wednesday. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks , which landed him on injured reserve.
Week 6 was the earliest that Brown could be activated from IR, so the fact that he's able to get back to practice at this juncture is a positive sign that the ankle has healed at a good pace.
"I don't know. He hasn't been out there," said Vrabel when asked what Brown's looming return means for the offense. "I can't tell you until we actually see it. He hadn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. If not, then 21-day window and we'll go from there."
New England will now have 21 days to move Brown onto the active roster, or else he'll revert back to injured reserve for the rest of the season. That said, it feels unlikely it'll take that long for him to eventually make his way back onto the 53-man roster and on the field.
"I think he's stayed engaged," Vrabel said of how Brown has dealt with being injured. "I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good. His ability to be around the guys in meetings and also focus on his rehab. Just treated everything as a pro and be where he's supposed to be and work hard to get back."
While it's unclear if Brown will be ready to go for the club's Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets , there is a wrinkle in the team's schedule worth pointing out. After this home matchup with the Jets, New England has a short week as they'll take on the Bears in Chicago on "Thursday Night Football" to begin Week 7. Given the tight turnaround, it's fair to wonder whether the Patriots will play it slow with Brown, with an eye for him to return for that game.
"We obviously know we have a shortened week next week," said Vrabel. "Can't impact our decisions to try and do everything we can to win this week, and then figure out where we are after that."
Brown was acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Eagles this offseason. New England shipped a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to Philadelphia in exchange for the star pass catcher. On top of giving the Patriots a top-tier weapon, the trade also reunited Brown with Vrabel, who coached him when he first entered the league as a second-round pick of the Tennessee Titans in 2019.
Last season for the Eagles, Brown caught 78 balls for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns. In his brief showing with the Patriots in Week 1, the 29-year-old caught three of his four targets for 26 yards.
One of the top stories throughout the NFL over the last two weeks has been the resurgence of Drake Maye . What's particularly stood out has been the return of the quarterback's deep ball efficiency. After being lauded as one of the best deep-ball throwers in the league during his runner-up MVP season in 2025, he fell off over the first three weeks of the year. Over these previous two games, however, it's returned in a big way .
Once Brown is officially reinserted into the offense, there's an argument to be made for these numbers to not only hold, but possibly even improve.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Could returning to Texas for 2027 finally make Arch Manning a top-five NFL Draft pick?
summary: From Jayden Daniels and Cam Ward to Garrett Nussmeier and Carson Beck, recent quarterbacks offer lessons about the benefits and risks of staying in school
full_text:
For most of his football career, the question surrounding Arch Manning was when he'd enter the NFL Draft , not whether he would be ready once he got there. But five games into the 2026 season, we're having the same conversation we had midway through 2025: should he spend another year at Texas?
Coach Steve Sarkisian said in June that he "wouldn't be surprised" if Manning returned for a fifth season in 2027. Earlier this month, uncle Eli Manning told Colin Cowherd that there's value in the college experience beyond simply preparing for the NFL , including opportunities to develop as a quarterback and leader.
There has been no formal announcement, but the possibility raises a question worth exploring (again): Could one more year in college transform Manning into the top-five pick we've been hearing about, this time in the 2028 NFL Draft?
He turns 23 in the spring, but despite four years in college, Manning has made just 20 career starts. He could finish 2026 with 27-30, and another season would push him toward 40. The question then becomes: would the additional games make a meaningful difference? History offers reasons for optimism, along with some warnings.
As discussed repeatedly, Manning's physical talent isn't the problem . He has a big arm, he navigates the pocket as well as anyone in the class, can excel off-platform and is an asset in the run game. And despite the uneven performances, he's quietly one of the better deep-ball throwers in this quarterback class.
Through five games, Manning has a 93.1 PFF passing grade on throws traveling at least 20 yards, with 10 big-time throws on 24 attempts. He's completed only nine, but drops and circumstances matter. The tape routinely shows a quarterback who can throw with touch, drive and accuracy downfield.
The problems pop up elsewhere, particularly when his first read isn't available.
Manning can play hurried, at times, in clean pockets. It affects his footwork, accuracy and field vision. He'll skip reads, and there are stretches when he appears to see only part of the field.
Saturday's 27-24 loss to Oklahoma again offered both versions of Manning. He looked like the best player on the field on his 41-yard touchdown throw to Cam Coleman.
ARCH MANNING 41-YARD TD TO CAM COLEMAN 😤🔥 (Via @TexasFootball ) pic.twitter.com/meYaDe9YRF
He had another big-boy touchdown toss to Ryan Wingo later in the game. And this laser to Coleman might be the best throw of his career:
#Texas QB Arch Manning with pressure in his face delivers a NUKE to Cam Coleman. Might just be the best throw of his career. pic.twitter.com/iRGLTLO5AO
But two fourth-quarter interceptions brought it all crashing back down to earth, again highlighting the decision-making and accuracy issues we've discussed for 14 months. It's why, even before the loss to Oklahoma, I had dropped Manning from my first mock draft of the fall . (Last year, I first dropped Manning from my mock draft in early November , a month before he announced his return to school.)
"He has not played up to being a first-round pick. Right now, I have 5 quarterbacks I would take before [Arch Manning] if the draft were tomorrow." 👀 @ryanwilsonCBS #scoreboard pic.twitter.com/KvPsBIawk5
The encouraging news is that quarterbacks have made substantial improvements when returning to school for Year 5.
Jayden Daniels entered his fifth season with more than 40 career starts. We all knew who he was athletically; he just needed to be more consistent as a passer. In his final season at LSU in 2023, his PFF passing grade jumped from 79.1 to 92.0, his big-time throw rate nearly tripled and his pressure-to-sack rate fell from 30.8% to 20.2%, suggesting better pocket awareness and decision-making under pressure.
Daniels won the Heisman Trophy, was the No. 2 overall pick in 2024 and immediately helped the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie.
Cam Ward perhaps offers the more relevant comparison.
At Washington State in 2023, Ward displayed the big arm and the ability to create outside the pocket. But he could also lock onto his first read, hold the ball too long, leave clean pockets and force unnecessary throws. Sound familiar?
After transferring to Miami for his fifth season, Ward was more comfortable working through reads, playing on time and managing pressure. His passing grade climbed from 77.5 to 91.7, while his pressure-to-sack rate improved by nine percentage points.
His First-Round Readiness Score (FRED), which measures how closely a quarterback's college resume resembles previous first-round picks, jumped from 6.8 before that season to 49.3 . For context, 50 represents the average first-round resume . Ward was the No. 1 overall pick in 2025.
But there's another side to his story. As I wrote recently about Ward and the Titans , through 22 NFL starts, he ranks tied for 51st in EPA per dropback among 56 first-round quarterbacks who had as many starts in their first three seasons. His 5.8 yards per attempt ranks 52nd.
The familiar concerns -- holding the ball and passing up easier throws -- have followed him to the NFL. It's a reminder that another college season can turn a player into QB1 without necessarily making him a successful NFL starter.
Bo Nix is another example. He entered his fifth season with 47 starts, improved his passing grade from 79.2 to 92.7 and went 12th overall in 2024. His first two NFL seasons were encouraging, although he's struggled to begin 2026.
PFF passing grade before → after
*Ward's total excludes earlier FCS experience. Penix Jr. returned for a sixth season.
Of course, returning to school guarantees nothing, as Garrett Nussmeier can attest. After throwing for more than 4,000 yards in 2024, he returned to LSU with just 14 career starts and legitimate first-round buzz. Instead, injuries and inconsistent play derailed his fifth season, and the quarterback once considered QB1 fell all the way to the seventh round, going 249th overall, eight picks from Mr. Irrelevant.
Spencer Rattler is another cautionary example. Like Manning, he had outstanding arm talent but struggled with the must-haves that separate franchise QBs from NFL backups. Rattler improved in some areas during his fifth season at South Carolina, and I had a third-round grade on him heading into the 2024 draft, but the league viewed him as a Day 3 pick and he wasn't selected until the fifth round.
Carson Beck is another example, but for a different reason. After a disappointing final season at Georgia in 2024, Beck transferred to Miami and was a much better quarterback in 2025. He was more confident, more decisive and had greater command of the offense. As I wrote following his pro day , he also became a better leader, helping Miami to the national title game while breathing new life into his NFL Draft stock. QB1 heading into that 2024 season, Beck was considered a Day 3 prospect months later, only to work himself back into the mix this spring, where he went 65th overall.
The takeaway? Another year in college can make a quarterback better – but it's a two-way street. Daniels and Beck made the most of their additional seasons, while Nussmeier watched his draft stock implode. And as we're seeing with Ward, just because you're the No. 1 overall pick doesn't promise success in the NFL.
At 22, with just 20 starts, Manning still has room to develop. And historical examples suggest there's no reason to assume development stops after four years of college.
But there's a difference between getting better and becoming the next great Manning. Arch can already make the spectacular throws – we watch it every week. But for NFL teams , it's about what it's always been about, and what former NFL quarterback and CBS Sports colleague Danny Kanell talked about recently :
"Ninety percent of playing quarterback is making boring decisions, but making the right decisions, making the right reads, getting in the right protection, getting the right run plays. And then the 10% is what makes guys super special," Kanell…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Joe Brady admits clock-management mistake despite overtime win over Rams
summary: Brady said Buffalo could have taken two knees before Tyler Bass' winning field goal, limiting the Rams' opportunity to answer if the kick missed
full_text:
In a week dominated by coaching gaffes and clock mismanagement , the victors are trying to learn from their counterparts' mistakes. There were some missteps that went unnoticed, however. Such as one from Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills .
Brady's Bills scored a massive, 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, but the first-year lead man identified one area where he could have been better. After Buffalo tipped Harrison Mevis ' 48-yard field goal attempt in the extra period, the Bills marched 35 yards down the field on five plays and set up Tyler Bass for a game-winning 45-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining on a second-and-10.
Brady now wishes he had called a couple of kneel-downs to take some time off the clock and cover his bases if Bass happened to miss his kick as Mevis did.
"I didn't want to run two QB sneaks with the thought process of putting the ball in harm's way, taking some shots on Josh, just to get — we knew we were already in line," Brady said. "So it's like, hey, do I just, hey, center the ball and just take two knees? You know, you go back two yards, but you don't give them, you know, they end up worse if you miss. They get 45 seconds to go 20 yards for the field goal. Big difference in two-minute, and the 45-yard field goal and a 47-yard field goal percentages, you should still be good to go.
"So if I had that opportunity again — look, I was conflicted about it. You know, T-Bass was good to go. The conversation we had in the huddle and upstairs was like, 'Let's just go win the game right now.' But to not give them that shot again if we do miss, the best thing would be is to take two knees and say, 'Hey, the 45 and the 47 is not of big difference.' Be a completely different story if the ball was a little further back. I'd be no indecision on taking knees if we were a little closer. We were just in that is a long field goal, we had just missed an extra point, but had the confidence in T-Bass, but that's one I do wish I probably took two knees and then we kick the game winner. And if anything, they'd have 45 seconds and not two minutes."
#Bills HC Joe Brady confirmed they probably should’ve taken two knees before attempting the game-winning FG last night to drain more time in case they missed and the #Rams got the ball back. Brady says a 45-yard FG and 47-yard FG isn't a big difference in that situation. https://t.co/CchyFnlXic pic.twitter.com/N1YCVWec3l
Running down the clock in overtime is something every NFL team needs to consider -- as long as you don't pull a Washington Commanders and run out the clock on yourself . But something else for NFL teams to consider is remaining aggressive in overtime. The Bills didn't have to kick a 45-yard field goal on second-and-10. They could have continued to gain yardage, run the clock and set up Bass for an easier field goal.
It would have been pretty embarrassing if Bass, who missed an extra point in the third quarter, had missed his 45-yard field goal on second down and allowed Matthew Stafford to engineer a game-winning drive with 1:50 remaining on the clock.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Tyreek Hill wants an NFL return, but these three obstacles could keep him off the field
summary: The eight-time Pro Bowler is working toward an immediate return, but big questions complicate his comeback after the recent ruling
full_text:
The latest buzz around eight-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Tyreek Hill is that he's nearing a return to the field. The Miami Dolphins released the 32-year-old this past offseason after he suffered a significant knee injury last September. Now that we are one year removed from the injury, The Athletic reports that Hill's former team, the Kansas City Chiefs, is very interested in a reunion, while his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, says he remains in discussion with multiple teams.
"He's continuing his rehab with the goal of being on a team in the immediate future," Rosenhaus told ESPN.
Rosenhaus said that Hill's situation is "very fluid" but that they are looking for the right situation d uring an interview with Josh Moser . That means the right financial compensation, the right quarterback and the right approach from a medical standpoint. That's fine, but it's also worth mentioning that Hill is currently under NFL investigation over allegations that could implicate the league's personal conduct policy.
This investigation comes after Hill's wife, Keeta Vaccaro, made allegations of domestic violence against the wide receiver, which could complicate his return to the field. In all, there are three factors that could hold Hill back from signing with an NFL team in the near future. Let's take a look at them.
On Tuesday, a jury returned a mixed verdict in Hill's assault and battery civil trial. They found the wideout liable for two counts of battery, but not liable for six other counts of battery, not liable for intentional infliction of emotional distress, and not liable for "continuing domestic violence," a ccording to ESPN .  Vaccaro was awarded $500,000 in compensatory damages but denied punitive damages.
One of the battery findings stemmed from a January 2024 incident that began with an argument over a postnuptial agreement. Vaccaro testified that Hill grabbed a necklace from her neck, put his hands around her neck, and grabbed and twisted her breasts. She presented photographs of markings on her chest and said the incident terrified her.
While the civil trial has concluded, the NFL's investigation has not. With domestic violence, the collective bargaining agreement allows for a suspension of six games. However, we've seen cases where players receive more severe punishments and less severe suspensions. It's all about what the league discovers during its independent investigation.
"We have been monitoring developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy," an NFL spokesperson told Pro Football Talk .
“I’m going into football terms, but I just think that after watching the film, there were a lot of areas I can improve in..” - Tyreek Hill, when asked if he was a good husband, pic.twitter.com/7aTCINog7h
If the NFL decides to suspend Hill for six games, that could mean he won't be eligible to play until Week 13 -- and Week 13 may be a best-case scenario.
We have no idea how long the NFL will take to wrap up its investigation. Think about Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs . He's still waiting to hear his fate from the league. And like Jacobs, Hill would probably be placed on the commissioner's exempt list if he were to sign with a team today -- barring him from practicing or playing.
Signing a player recently found liable for battery of his wife in a civil trial is not great from an optics standpoint, to say the least. But even if an NFL team doesn't care about optics, the timing of a potential suspension could complicate things. Why roll the dice and shell out millions of dollars if an older Hill coming off a major knee injury can't return until late December?
Even Hill's agent, Rosenhaus, said he doesn't know if Hill is 100% healthy right now. It appeared retirement was firmly on the table for Hill after what happened on the night of Sept. 29, 2025. Hill dislocated his knee and tore multiple ligaments, including his ACL. It's barely been a year since that happened.
After the injury occurred, it was fair to wonder if Hill's football career could be over. During an appearance on Terron Armstead's podcast, " The Set ," 11 months ago, Armstead asked Hill if he had a message for his doubters. Instead, the receiver offered a surprisingly honest answer.
"Well, at the end of the day, I feel like that decision is all based upon how I feel and where my mindset is at the moment," Hill said. "Like right now, I'm happy. I'm happy with being with my kids, I'm happy with the career that I've had. I love playing football. I love it, but it takes a lot. It takes a lot to be the best and to stay at the top and make a lot of money and help your team win games and stuff like that. It takes a lot. It takes a lot on you mentally, it takes a lot on you physically. I'm at the point now where I need to have a conversation with mom, family, everybody ... I don't want to make any rash decisions, obviously. I just want to be in the moment."
Hill is able to sprint at this point in his recovery, and still looks fast. But questions remain about acceleration, deceleration and route-running ability.
Those Red Cleats 🤔🤔🤔🤔🤔 pic.twitter.com/eEYjQrx2bH
There are several factors that could complicate an immediate return to the field for Hill, whether that be a suspension or questions about what kind of shape he's in and the contract he's looking for. Will a team like the Chiefs wait for the NFL to hand down a punishment, or will a club jump the gun and add Hill as soon as possible? All of that remains to be seen.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Mike Renner's 2027 NFL Draft Big Board: Ranking the top 150 prospects at college football midway point
summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith leads the way while Drew Mestemaker and CJ Carr emerge as early contenders to go No. 1 overall
full_text:
We're inching closer to the vaunted 2027 draft class with each passing day. Now, at the halfway point of the season, we're really starting to sift the wheat from the chaff. The big question everyone keeps asking, though, is how the quarterback class shakes out. Truthfully, it's a question I kept asking myself even after reviewing all of their tape. The class is obviously incredibly talented, as you can see by the 10 quarterbacks included below, but are any worthy of the No. 1 overall pick?
While this won't be the answer you want to hear, it's the honest truth: maybe. Two quarterbacks have started the early season on No. 1 pick trajectories, with a few others within realistic striking distance. The good news is that, with conference play now in full swing, the second half of the season through the playoffs is when the cupcakes fade away, and the real prospect evaluations start to heat up.
If you've seen him play, no explanation is necessary. If you haven't, no explanation will suffice. His current 12-game pace will put him in the single-season top-10 for both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. And with the very likely chance that Ohio State plays more than 12 games, Smith is a real threat to challenge both records.
Moore missed last weekend's game with a concussion, but prior to that, he picked up where he left off as the best corner in the country. In fact, he's giving up only a half a yard per coverage snap this season after giving up only a half a yard per coverage snap all last season. It doesn't matter what scheme you run, Moore's well-rounded skill set will fit your defense.
Stewart has not quite figured it all out yet, but has a tier-1 physical skill set when it comes to rushing the passer in the NFL . The latter matters far more than the former at defensive end. He doesn't need too many moves to be a high-end impact pass-rusher as we just saw against Florida .
After some hiccups in Week 1 against Tulsa, where Mestemaker was obviously a little juiced up, Mestemaker has been the best quarterback in college football the past five weeks. Over that span, he's averaged 11.1 yards per attempt with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions - burying a loaded Oregon defense in the process. His ability to deliver strikes downfield with defensive linemen bearing down on him is unparalleled in the draft class. While he hasn't played much football, that's a selling point, given how poised his tape already is.
Simmons is a speed rusher who wants to threaten the upfield shoulder of opposing offensive tackles. That juice has led to an FBS-leading 9.5 sacks this season. He may be undersized, but his tape against the run shows an every-down edge in the NFL.
Gilliam's breakout season reminds me a little of Byron Murphy's back in 2023. Not only because they share similar body types and athletic ability, but also because they went from unheralded prospects to superstars seemingly overnight. Gilliam has been an absolute handful this season - even in the past three weeks of SEC play. His low center of gravity combined with tremendous bend and explosiveness makes him nearly impossible to keep out of the backfield.
Hampton is one of those cornerbacks where you don't need to watch too many plays to realize he has the goods. 6-foot-2, 205-pound corners are not supposed to move as fluidly as he does. In five games this season, Hampton already has 10 forced incompletions - including two vs. Miami's Malachi Toney . That's the kind of ball production you want to see from a top-flight corner prospect.
Goosby started the season with a minor knee injury, although it hasn't altered his high level of play much. Goosby has yet to allow a sack all season with only seven pressures allowed on 181 pass-blocking snaps so far. At every bit of 6-foot-7, Goosby is a massive tackle to try to get around.
Becker is a special deep threat for three big reasons. The first is, as with any deep threat, his speed. He's a former state champion hurdler, and when he gets up to top speed, corners are left grasping for air. The second is his size at 6-foot-4, 208 pounds, which helps him go over the top of defensive backs. The final one is his ball-tracking, which is as good as any prospect in recent memory. In fact, it's very difficult to get better, as he's never dropped a pass in 65 career opportunities. Size, speed, and hands - sign me up.
While Carr has yet to face a real test on his schedule ( Notre Dame's highest-ranked opponent in FPI has been Wisconsin at 37th), the third-year quarterback has passed every test with flying colors. He just isn't missing throws, with a 70.8 completion percentage on the season and a 10.0 average depth of target. That's slinging it.
Seaton is one heck of an athlete who looks like it's only a matter of time before he becomes a shutdown pass-protector at the NFL level. With him, it's really all about when his play strength can improve to the point where he can consistently anchor against power, as that's been the biggest issue for him in SEC play.
Pieper is a stupidly good athlete who's been playing out of position his whole collegiate career at right guard. Even so, he's still getting the job done at a high level. In schemes that like to get their center out on the move, Pieper is the absolute perfect fit.
Ask LSU's offensive line about Echoles and they might tell you he should go #1 overall. The third-year defensive tackle took over that game earlier this year with seven pressures, flashing a pass-rushing skill set we've been waiting to see. Everyone knew him already as one of college football's best run defenders, but if he has more games like that in the SEC, he'll push his way into the top-10.
Johnson has not only been exceptional at guard this season, but he's also been the ultimate team player and kicked inside to center for the injured Ashton Beers . At 6-foot-6, that's definitely not going to be his best position in the NFL, but he's held his own there all the same. Johnson has allowed only one pressure on 201 pass-blocking snaps this season.
Thompkins has looked like a different player entirely this season at Alabama than he did at USC . His blend of power and agility at 6-foot-5 and nearly 300 pounds gives him a lot of ways to win as a pass-rusher. The crazy thing is, at that size, he's doing it off the edge. You don't see many ends that size in the league anymore, but he's looked far more comfortable there than he did playing primarily inside at USC before he transferred.
Cole is this year's version of Sonny Styles. An off-ball linebacker athlete almost too spectacular to believe. At 6-foot-3, 235 pounds, Cole moves in space like a cornerback. He's one of the most impressive linebackers I've ever seen closing to ball carriers in space. Heading into this season, I thought Cole's long frame belonged on the edge rushing the passer, but now I want him running the seams and shutting down screens.
Coleman has always teased high-end potential, but even after transferring from Auburn to Texas has still yet to put it all together as a full-tree route-runner. While that's usually worrying for a draft-eligible prospect, I'm willing to overlook it with Coleman for two big reasons. The first is that he only just turned 20 in August, as he's one of the youngest draft-eligible players in the country. The second is that there's nothing about him physically that says he can't run a full route tree; we just haven't seen it yet consistently.
Heldt is a relentless pass-rusher who only seems to keep improving week-to-week and year-to-year. He's racked up 16 pressures over the past three weeks, as he is outstanding at getting to edges on offensive linemen, then finishing through contact. I think the arrow is only pointed up for Heldt going forward.
Baugh has prototypical size and prototypical speed. That's a good combo for a running back. He is a load to bring down for opposing defenses, with already 38 broken tackles in six games this season.
Heard is the single biggest…
author: Mike Renner

title: Michael Penix Jr. injury update: Falcons QB likely to start this week vs. Bears, but status could change
summary: Penix suffered a rib injury during the Week 5 overtime loss to Baltimore
full_text:
After their quarterback couldn't finish Sunday night's overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens due to a rib injury, the Atlanta Falcons are getting some positive news relating to Michael Penix Jr.'s status for Week 6. On Wednesday, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Penix is "feeling better" and that, if "everything goes according to plan," he will start on Sunday against the Chicago Bears .
"Mike will practice," Stefanski said to begin his Wednesday press conference. "He'll be limited in some fashion. We'll see how he's feeling and have communication with him to see how many reps we'll take off, so that's to be determined."
When asked specifically if Penix will start on Sunday, Stefeanski said, "Yes, as long as everything goes according to plan."
Stefanski went on to say that he wants to see how Penix is feeling out on the field before making hard determinations on how the practice reps will be divvied up.
"With any injury like this, you want to make sure, as they move around, how they're feeling," he said. "It could be all, some, none. We shall see."
Penix suffered the injury after being sacked by Baltimore's Tavius Robinson with about 19 seconds left in regulation. He fumbled the ball after getting hit, but the Falcons recovered the football. Penix was forced to miss that next play, but did return one play later, throwing an incompletion before Atlanta punted the ball away. The game eventually went to overtime.
Despite that brief return, the former first-round pick did not go back onto the field during the overtime period, as Tua Tagovailoa relieved him the rest of the way. After the Ravens scored a touchdown on their opening possession, Tagovailoa tossed a game-clinching interception, with Atlanta falling 30-23.
It can't be overstated how much of a night-and-day difference Penix has made since returning as the starter in Week 3. After a 0-2 start with Cooper Rush as the starter, the Falcons are 2-1 under Penix, who was working his way back from a torn ACL last year. With Penix under center, the offense has averaged 34.3 points per game and 428.3 total yards per game, so likely having him back for this contest is a big development for their hopes of staying in the NFC South race.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Eagles facing NFL schedule disadvantage in Week 6 that no team has ever overcome
summary: The NFL didn't really think through this part of the schedule
full_text:
It's been a rough week for the Philadelphia Eagles , and things could get even worse on Sunday when they face the Carolina Panthers .
For their Week 6 game, the Eagles will be facing a scheduling disadvantage that no team has ever been able to overcome: They're coming off an international game and they have to face a team coming off a bye.
So, how bad of a disadvantage is this? It's only happened four times — so it's a small sample size — but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 against the team coming off a bye and 0-3-1 against the spread, which suggests this does put teams at a competitive disadvantage.
Over the past decade, the NFL has generally tried to avoid situations like this, but the league essentially gave up on that this year, with a total of five teams stuck in this exact situation.
Here's a brief look at the four games in which a team coming off an international game faced a team off a bye.
Here's where things get even uglier: The team coming off the international trip has averaged just 15.25 points per game. And to make things worse, the four international teams were outscored 70-30 over the first three quarters. Again, it's a small sample size, but those are eye-opening numbers.
One reason the sample size is so small is that this situation wasn't really possible for most of NFL history. The first London game was played in 2007, and for the first nine years of the series, any team playing Europe received a bye after its game. However, in 2016, the Colts decided they didn't WANT a bye after their London game because they didn't want their off week so early in the season. Since that point, the NFL has allowed teams to request a bye after playing abroad, but even if a team requests one, there's no guarantee they'll get it.
The 2021 Dolphins and 2025 Browns are the only two teams that played an international game in Europe before their matchup with a team coming off a bye. That's an important distinction, because they had to re-adjust to a massive time change heading into their next game.
After the NFL schedule came out in May, the league's vice president of broadcast planning, Mike North, explained why teams are no longer guaranteed a bye after an international game .
"I know it's not quite routine, but it's getting to the point where it's pretty routine," North said of international travel. "You play an afternoon (game) over there, it's morning over here, you're back in the facility by what? Midnight Sunday night? That's better than if it's played out in Seattle or Los Angeles … That's the new normal for us."
What North didn't mention is the impact of asking a team coming off an international trip to face a team coming off a bye in their next game. Yes, you might get back to your facility late Sunday night, but if your body is still on European time, there will be an adjustment period, and jet lag could last a day or two, which could impact practice for your next game.
The Eagles are coming off a brutal loss to the Jaguars. They're banged up, and now, they have to deal with this.
If the Eagles lose on Sunday, that will drop NFL teams to 0-5 all-time in this specific situation, and if that happens, the NFL is going to have to give some serious thought about whether it's fair to schedule a team coming off an international game to face a team coming off a bye.
author: John Breech

title: Here come the Patriots: What's changed for Drake Maye, New England as they look all the way back
summary: Drake Maye looks like his MVP self, and New England could be back in the Super Bowl conversation
full_text:
Don't look now, but the reigning AFC champions have started to look more like themselves lately. After a tumultuous first three weeks of the 2026 campaign, where it looked like Mike Vrabel's club was enduring a hangover from the success they had a year ago, they've stabilized over the past two games and sit at 3-2 on the year. More than that, they seem primed to once again vie for the conference crown and make a bid for the Super Bowl .
The biggest change, of course, has been Drake Maye . He was at the crux of New England's early-season struggles and has seen a night-and-day difference in his play over the past two weeks, especially when it comes to the turnover department. He's also coming off his first career back-to-back games with three-plus passing touchdowns.
If you dig a little deeper into what's changed with Maye over these past two games, it's been the return of his deep ball. Last year, Maye was arguably the best deep-ball thrower in the NFL , but that effectively vanished at the start of this season -- that sort of bled over from the offense's struggles last postseason.
From Week 1-3, Maye was just 9-of-23 passing (39%) on throws of 15-plus air yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions. More recently (Week 4-5), Maye is 11 of 18 (61%) on those throws with three touchdowns and no interceptions.
That efficiency has him right back to the range of where he was during the last regular season, where he completed 58% of such throws. If you remember, Maye finished second in MVP voting largely because of that prolific play down the field. If he's truly returned to that level, it makes his current odds to win MVP this season at +1700 quite tasty.
While Maye is the straw that stirs the drink of the entire organization, the Patriots ' climb back up to their ceiling goes beyond his improved play over the past couple of weeks.
Coming into the year, the Patriots were facing a gauntlet out of the gate. New England had the hardest Week 1-4 strength of schedule by any team entering a season in the last 40 years. When you zoom out and look at it from 10,000 feet, the fact that they emerged from that at 2-2 is pretty solid.
Of course, how they played in those games -- and losing to a Seattle team that lost Sam Darnold after the opening drive -- raised red flags, but from a record standpoint, it could've been much worse. They also picked up a key divisional win in Buffalo over that stretch, which is a valuable feather in their helmets as they look down the barrel of a schedule that does soften up.
at Chicago Bears (Thursday Night Football)
vs. Detroit Lions (in Munich, Germany)
vs. Minnesota Vikings (Thursday Night Football)
at Kansas City Chiefs (Monday Night Football)
This week, they take on a 2-3 New York Jets team at home and are a touchdown favorite. Then, the Patriots head to Chicago on a short week, where they'll face a Bears team that is currently depleted. Caleb Williams (hamstring) is still sidelined, but could be back for that contest. However, standout running back Kyle Monangai (toe) is on the shelf, and defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games (including the matchup against New England) for violating the league's performance-enhancing substance policy.
After their mini bye week, the Pats will visit the currently 0-5 Dolphins in Miami before a home matchup with a flawed Green Bay Packers team. Then, they will head off to Munich to face the Lions in Week 10. Detroit has one of the worst defenses in the NFL so far this season, so Drake Maye's affinity to chuck it deep could be on full display for the German fans.
Given that path, it's conceivable that the Patriots enter the Week 11 bye on a seven-game winning streak, putting them at 8-2. Even if they drop a game or two, sitting at 7-3 or 6-4 at the well-positioned bye gives them a strong chance at double-digit wins. That would put them well within range of Buffalo in the AFC East race.
For those wagering at home, the Patriots' win total currently sits at 10.5, with the Over priced at +120 on DraftKings . They're also +160 to win the AFC East and -370 to make the playoffs, so the oddsmakers are backing up what our eyes have been telling us these past two weeks. They're firmly in the mix.
Lost in the haze of Maye's resurgence is that he could be getting some massive reinforcements in the form of A.J. Brown . New England has yet to truly see any returns from their offseason prize after he suffered a high ankle sprain during the early portions of the team's Week 1 loss to Seattle. However, Brown is eligible to return from injured reserve as early as Week 6 against the New York Jets. Whenever he does come back, it adds a massive boost to an already emerging offense.
Throughout the summer, the Patriots seemed to make a concerted effort to build the chemistry between Maye and Brown. I would theorize some of the early-season struggles we saw from Maye were due to him not having the best rapport with his other pass catches (notably free agent signee Romeo Doubs ) because the team was focused on him working with Brown. Nevertheless, Brown brings a true No. 1 presence to the Patriots' passing attack, and the other weapons in the offense should now fit in quite well around him as he draws the eyeballs in coverage.
Even in that brief window in Week 1, you saw the big play potential of Maye and Brown, with the wideout breaking loose on a flea-flicker. Maye wasn't able to put it on a streaking Brown, but the receiver was able to draw the DPI penalty to set up their lone touchdown of the game.
The #Patriots get a 1st & GOAL after a flea flicker-deep pass to A.J. Brown draws a pass interference from the #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/5jUFcmhtG5
Given Maye's rekindled mastery of the deep ball, injecting Brown into the equation could be like hitting the NOS to the offense.
One of my biggest concerns for the Patriots entering the season was their perceived lack of high-caliber play off the edge. That was particularly true after losing K'Lavon Chaisson in free agency and Harold Landy III beginning the year on injured reserve, where he still sits. Those were the top two sack leaders on the team a year ago, so it was a legitimate question as to where that production would come from.
Well, through five weeks, the Patriots are ninth in the NFL in pressure rate thanks to the emergence of 2025 undrafted free agent Elijah Ponder and second-round rookie Gabe Jacas . Ponder has 4.5 sacks so far this season, which has him tied with T.J. Watt for the fifth-most in the NFL.
Meanwhile, Jacas, who was slowed through the offseason due to injury and contract issues, has steadily started to ramp up as a legit presence off the edge.
Their ability to pressure the quarterback has been instrumental in that unit arguably improving from the one we saw last year.
The elephant in the room when it comes to New England truly reestablishing itself as a player in the AFC is, of course, injuries. While A.J. Brown going down in the opener was the headliner to begin the season, the injury bug has continued to take bites out of the team. Top cornerback Christian Gonzalez has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury, while fellow corner Carlton Davis also missed time with a neck ailment.
On top of those hits to the secondary, the offense has had a number of injuries as well. Starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered what is believed to be a season-ending ankle injury in Week 2 against the Steelers . The Patriots also recently placed wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) and fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle, knee) on injured reserve.
Then, coming out of Week 5, starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury, and running back TreVeyon Henderson went down with an ankle injury. Campbell reportedly sprained his MCL and is expected to miss some time. As for Henderson, he's expected to miss multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain.
Those are some heavy hitters going down for New England, who will see its depth tested as it…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Lamar Jackson has 'realistic chance' to return vs. Browns in Week 6
summary: Baltimore expects to know more by midweek as Jackson pushes to return from the ankle injury that sidelined him against Atlanta
full_text:
Lamar Jackson has a "realistic chance" to return from his ankle injury suffered in Week 4 and start against the Browns in Week 6 on Sunday, ESPN reports.
Jackson sprained his ankle against the Titans on Oct. 4 and did not return in the second half. The Ravens , who were up by 17 points at halftime thanks to Jackson's red-hot start, held on for a 24-18 win with Tyler Huntley quarterbacking in the second half. In Week 5, Huntley led a game-tying touchdown drive late in regulation and a game-winning touchdown drive in overtime to lead the Ravens over the Falcons , 30-23. Baltimore is 4-1 this season.
"He is definitely doing better," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said on Monday. "Wednesday, I am not sure about exactly how that practice will look, but again, to Lamar's credit, he is doing everything he can to get back out there. ... I think we will know more definitely by the middle of the week."
Jackson did not practice at all last week.
Jackson battled several nagging issues last year. Officially, an early-season hamstring injury cost him three games, and a back bruise caused him to miss another game late in the year. Unofficially, Jackson rarely looked like his normal explosive self. He had just 67 carries for 349 yards, both career lows, and his 5.2 yards per carry was his lowest mark since his rookie year, when he took over as starter midseason. Jackson's pocket mobility evaporated, too, as he had a career-high sack rate.
But he had looked back to his old self early this season. He leads the NFL in yards per attempt, and his 7.6 yards per carry is on pace to be the highest of his career.
Should Jackson be unable to play, Huntley has proved to be a reliable backup. The Ravens have won all three of his starts since the start of last season.
If Jackson returns, he wouldn't be the only change to the lineup. The Ravens acquired center Cam Jurgens last week, and the two-time Pro Bowler is in line to make his Baltimore debut this weekend. Jurgens was in the concussion protocol last week, but Minter said Monday he was in the final stages of clearing the protocol. Baltimore is also opening the practice window for rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane , per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. Lane fractured his wrist in Week 1.

title: Predicting the full 14-team NFL playoff bracket entering Week 6: 49ers make Super Bowl run, NFC East gets ugly
summary: We just simulated the final 193 games of the NFL season and the 49ers are going to like how things ended up
full_text:
Apparently, no one wants to win the NFC East. At least that's how it looked after a wild Week 5 that saw all four teams go winless, which seems impossible when you consider that two NFC East teams actually faced each other.
So what happened in the division? The Cowboys lost to the previously winless Buccaneers . The Eagles blew a lead in the final eight seconds against Jacksonville, and then we had the Commanders and Giants , who somehow played to a tie.
At this point, you might be wondering who's going to win the division, and fortunately, we might have the answer for you here. To figure out who's going to win each division and who's going to make the playoffs, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season.
There are 193 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated ALL of them. Not only did he project the 14 teams that will end up making the playoffs, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion. And he also projected who the winner will be in the NFC East, since someone has to win that division.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
There are only four teams in the AFC with one loss or less, and to no one's surprise, all four of those teams are being projected to win their division.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Chiefs (4-0) -- AFC West champion 2. Bills (4-1) -- AFC East champion 3. Jaguars (4-1) -- AFC South champion 4. Ravens (4-1) -- AFC North champion 5. Broncos (3-2) 6. Bengals (3-2) 7. Patriots (3-2)
When it comes to the wild card teams, our projection model essentially has five teams battling for three spots, with the Broncos, Bengals and Patriots getting in over the Colts and Steelers . The computer has all five of those teams finishing with a winning record, but the Colts and Steelers are both on the outside looking in at 9-8.
The 49ers are officially the team to beat in the NFC, at least according to our projection. After watching them go on the road to beat the Seahawks on Sunday, the computer is now projecting that San Francisco is going to finish with the top seed in the NFC.
And then there's the NFC East. The computer has the Eagles falling backward into the division title with an 8-9 record. Yup, we have the NFC East winner finishing with a losing record.
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. 49ers (5-0) -- NFC West champion 2. Vikings (5-0) -- NFC North champion 3. Panthers (2-2) -- NFC South champion 4. Eagles (2-3) -- NFC East champion 5. Seahawks (3-2) 6. Lions (3-2) 7. Rams (2-3)
The biggest surprise here might be the fact that the BEARS are projected to miss the postseason. After losing to the Packers on Sunday, our projection has them finishing at 9-8, which will leave them one spot out of the wild card.
Speaking of the wild card, the Rams are still projected to make it despite their three losses because they're still viewed as a strong team. The three losses have come against three teams that have a combined 12-3 record. Not only that, but the Rams have the second-easiest remaining strength of schedule out of any team in the NFC, which should help them down the stretch. Five of the Rams' 12 remaining gams will come against teams that currently have one win or less.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Vikings) and two teams (49ers and Chiefs) that have faced each other in two of the past seven Super Bowls.
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at what the projected Super Bowl has been each week.
There's definitely been a Chiefs' theme in our projections so far.
Right now, the 49ers are on top of the football world, and things could stay that way for a while. Over the next five weeks, the 49ers are only scheduled to play one game against a team that currently has a winning record ( Raiders ), so this team could easily be 9-0 heading into their Week 11 showdown in Mexico against the currently undefeated Vikings.

title: How Bo Nix's strange, viral quote perfectly encapsulates his 2026 season
summary: Denver's offense ranks near the bottom of the NFL, but its history of wild second-half comebacks shows why Nix's strange comments hold some truth
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are off to a 3-2 start this season, but it's been a pretty rocky 3-2 start if we are being honest. The offense ranks third-worst in the entire NFL , averaging just 269.0 total yards per game, and Sean Payton has already yanked play-calling duties away from new offensive coordinator Davis Webb .
The play-calling change didn't help on Sunday, as the Broncos struggled against the winless Los Angeles Chargers . Denver did escape SoFi Stadium with a 23-17 victory, but the offense put up just 224 total yards and converted one of 12 third downs while quarterback Bo Nix threw for 123 yards and a touchdown.
Nix doesn't look like a quarterback on the cusp of leading the Broncos to the Super Bowl nine months ago. He's completed 59.9% of his passes, which ranks 26th in the NFL, and his 188.4 passing yards per game rank 25th. While Denver added a deep threat in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason, Nix's 5.2 air yards per attempt are the fewest by a qualifying quarterback through five games since C.J. Beathard's 5.1 in 2018.
But Nix doesn't seem overly worried about it. During Tuesday's press conference, Nix was asked how he handles stretches when he's playing well and when he's not. What's his process like when it comes to moving on from bad plays? He offered a pretty strange response.
"It's the same when I'm playing really good," Nix responded. "I think playing good and playing bad, it's a narrative, and I think it's honestly kind of something we make up. I don't think necessarily I'm playing any different than what I'm normally playing it's just every once in a while a ball will bounce this way or something will happen this way and we'll get a pressure on this look when we had somebody open, I had to throw it away and I wanted to hold onto it a little bit longer and the guy was open and next thing you know, statline looks different. We're talking about something completely different..."
Playing good and playing bad is a narrative? It's something we make up? How can that be true?
This is one of those strange cases where the messenger actually makes the message make more sense. Because we've seen Nix play "good" and "bad" football in the span of 60 minutes many times over the last three years. That's how the Broncos have the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025.
Take what happened in Week 3, for example. The Broncos were hosting Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams on "Sunday Night Football" and had an embarrassing first half, going down 16-0. However, like we've seen Nix and the Broncos do so many times before, they bounced back in the second half and scored a whopping 30 points to register another come-from-behind victory. It was Denver's third comeback win of 14+ points over the last two seasons, the most in the NFL.
So, did Nix play "good" or "bad" football vs. the Rams? It was both! It's not necessarily one or the other.
What has to be said is that the Broncos need to find a way to be consistent, because they would be a legitimate contender if they could play 60 minutes the way they usually play the final 30. Denver has the pieces to make a postseason run once again. Remember, if Nix hadn't injured his ankle in the divisional round vs. Buffalo, the Broncos had a great chance to represent the AFC in Super Bowl LX.
Coach Payton has to find a way to get the most out of his offense, and he has a tough test ahead of him this week, as the Broncos welcome the Seattle Seahawks and their top-ranked defense to town on Thursday night.

And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? title: NFL Week 6 picks, odds: Panthers stun Eagles in Philly, Buccaneers pull off upset
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets.
Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition.
Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something.
Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate.
Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.
Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch.
Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5
This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog.
Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game.
Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3
You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket.
Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7
I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here.
Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5
I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. title: NFL coaching hot-seat rankings: Todd Bowles, Dan Quinn and Jim Harbaugh face mounting pressure
summary: Quinn is one of several coaches who are feeling the heat
full_text:
As firing season inches closer in the volatile NFL, we ranked 10 head coaches facing job security questions and warming seats after the first five weeks. Several coaches saw their seats heat up this week after numerous multiple examples of coaching malpractice.
It doesn't appear that Ryans' job status is in jeopardy yet. But for a team that entered the season with Super Bowl expectations, a 1-4 start is less than ideal.
Momentum appears to be on Houston's side, however. Minutes after the Texans got their first win of the season (a decisive, 26-3 win over the Titans ), Ryans confirmed that Houston had acquired former Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. , who enjoyed a successful partnership with CJ Stroud at Ohio State.
Ryans' team has a pivotal showdown this Sunday in Jacksonville against the Jaguars , who have a three-game lead over Houston in the AFC South standings.
If we only went off team performance, Glenn would definitely be on the hot seat. The Jets are just 5-17 since the start of the 2025 season, Glenn's first in the Big Apple. New York is coming off a 17-12 win over the Browns that snapped a three-game losing skid.
It appears that the Jets are content to give Glenn more time to turn things around. He's signed through the 2029 season, and, based on previous comments made by Woody Johnson, it seems that the Jets' owner wants to exude more patience this time around. A horrible season, however, might compel Johnson to make yet another coaching change.
Saleh doesn't sound like a coach who is worried about his job. When recently asked about making changes amid the Titans' 0-5 start, Saleh said that Tennessee is "in game five of year one."
Either Saleh knows something we don't, or he is underestimating the situation in Nashville. While little was expected of them this season, the Titans are failing to even reach that extremely low bar , especially on offense. Tennessee's defense (Saleh's side of the ball) is 10th in the NFL in points allowed, but its offense is last in the NFL in scoring and 31st in passing.
Saleh might survive the season, but he will likely need changes to his offensive coaching staff if things don't improve during the season's final 12 games.
Desperate times call for desperate measures. Immediately after last Thursday's embarrassing loss to the previously winless Buccaneers, Schottenheimer announced that changes were coming for the 2-3 Cowboys.
Among the changes were the hiring of Mike Pettine as senior defensive assistant and the move of defensive coordinator Christian Parker from the coach's booth to the sideline. Dallas' defense took matters into its own hands with a player-led meeting on Monday.
Schottenheimer and company enter a season-defining stretch of their schedule with consecutive prime-time road games against the Packers and Eagles. Rest assured that the outcomes of those games will shape Schottenheimer's job security.
After a 0-2 start, the Colts evened their record and had a chance to get to over .500 with a win this past Sunday in Pittsburgh. But instead of that happening, the Colts lost another winnable game, which has become a staple of Steichen's time in Indianapolis.
While they've had their moments (especially last year's 8-2 start), the Colts have yet to turn the corner under Steichen, whose record in Indianapolis is 27-29 and includes just one winning season and no playoff seasons. It's hard to imagine the Colts retaining him if this season mimics the previous three.
One of the biggest current enigmas in Indianapolis is the defense given Steichen's background as a defensive coordinator. While the Colts are fourth in the NFL in red zone efficiency, their defense is near the bottom in most other league categories.
Moore's seat warmed up considerably after Saints owner Gayle Benson publicly expressed her disappointment with the team's 1-4 start.
"I will not make excuses and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard," Benson said . "I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team. Everyone on this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct mistakes that are costing us the games."
The Saints were considered a dark horse candidate to win the NFC South after Moore's team won four consecutive games late in the 2025 season. New Orleans played well during the season's first three weeks, but they were completely outplayed by the visiting Falcons in Week 4. This past Sunday, the Saints' offense gained just 142 yards and committed three turnovers during a 23-13 loss to the Vikings .
Mounting injuries undoubtedly contributed to the Saints' recent plight. Benson, however, is hellbent on seeing results, not excuses.
"Words will not restore our fans' confidence," she said . "Our performance must do that."
While it pales in comparison to what happened in Washington, Philadelphia's late-game gaffe against the Jaguars in London was brutal, nonetheless. Instead of booting the ball into the end zone with eight seconds left, Sirianni elected to kick it in play, which resulted in a 53-yard return that set up Jacksonville's game-winning field goal as time expired.
As all good leaders do, Sirianni took responsibility for the loss. But that hasn't spared him criticism from Philadelphia fans who were already on his case before Sunday's debacle.
It's not hyperbole to say that the Eagles -- now 2-3 -- are entering the most important stretch of the season. They'll host the Panthers on Sunday, then play three straight games against divisional foes before their Week 10 bye. All but one of those games will be at home.
Los Angeles hired Harbaugh to help Justin Herbert get to the next level. Instead, the Chargers have had two seasons without a playoff win and are 0-5.
Herbert shoulders a lot of the blame for the Chargers' current plight. Some of that criticism is warranted, but there's plenty of blame to go around. Herbert has had shaky pass protection, and his receiving corps is underwhelming. He also isn't meshing with Mike McDaniel.
For those who think that Harbaugh's previous success might buy him more time, Chargers owner Dean Spanos infamously fired Marty Schottenheimer after a 14-2 season.
Quinn's first season in Washington was magic, but the more the Commanders lose, the more distant that season feels.
If Quinn wasn't on the hot seat prior to Sunday, he is now following Washington's overtime disaster that prevented the Commanders from getting their second win of the season. Washington is now 6-15-1 under Quinn since the start of the 2025 season.
Instead of winning that game and evening their record at 2-2, the Commanders are now 1-3-1 with an upcoming road game against the 5-0 49ers . Barring an upset, Washington will go into its Week 7 bye at 1-4-1.
Bowels and his team showed serious resolve last Thursday night in Dallas while getting their first win of the season. The Buccaneers received big performances from undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving , who ran for a career-high 165 yards. The Buccaneers' defense also came up with a game-clinching stand.
The Buccaneers host a Steelers team on Sunday that is 0-2 on the road and is playing without three of its receivers, including Michael Pittman . It's a winnable game that the Buccaneers need to win if they want to turn their season around.

title: Prisco's Week 6 NFL picks: Seahawks over Broncos on Thursday night, Buccaneers upset Steelers

full_text:
After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2.
The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week.
Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row?
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game.
Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17
The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one.
Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20
The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it.
Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21
There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball.
Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13
The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game.
The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight.
Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13
The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one.
Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16
The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense.
Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20
Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it.
Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21
The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day.
Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20
The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye.
Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21
The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills.
Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21
The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout.
Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27
This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate.
Pick: 49ers 30, Commanders 21
