title: Is it time to cut ties with Cardinals DC Nick Rallis?
summary: The Detroit Lions blasted the Arizona Cardinals this past weekend, 45-21. Any time the opposition posts up close to 50 points on your club, it is a huge issue. Except for the 26-14 victory over the hapless Los Angeles Chargers on opening weekend, the Cardinals’ defense has surrendered 31, 36, 36, and now 45 points. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - DECEMBER 21: Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis of the Arizona Cardinals looks on prior to a game against the Atlanta Falcons at State Farm Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions blasted the Arizona Cardinals this past weekend, 45-21. Any time the opposition posts up close to 50 points on your club, it is a huge issue. Except for the 26-14 victory over the hapless Los Angeles Chargers on opening weekend, the Cardinals’ defense has surrendered 31, 36, 36, and now 45 points. RELATED: SHOULD THE CARDINALS TRADE JOSH SWEAT? Maybe it’s just time to let DC Nick Rallis go. The Cardinals have allowed a league-high 162 points in just five games. Every American Football team at every level wants to average scoring 32.4 points a game. That is a dream situation. For Arizona, that dream is currently a nightmare. Our offense will be fine under Lafleur. Our defense needs a new DC! — {•¥•} (@___1_618___) September 28, 2026 The Cardinals’ 1-4-0 record is indicative of their inability to keep opposing offenses out of the end zone. Against the pass, Arizona’s defense has allowed the most passing touchdowns (14), tied for third with the fewest interceptions (3), ranked #32 in passing yards gained per attempt (9.1), second-worst defensive ranking (117.2), has allowed the third-greatest first-down conversion ratio (41.7%), given up the fourth most plays of 20+ yards (18), given up the fourth most plays of 40+ yards (3), and is ranked #14 in the most sacks (11). Versus the run, the Cardinals are ranked #9 in total rushing yards (633), #9 in rushing attempts (144), tied for #4 in most rushing touchdowns allowed (6), tied for #10 in most yards per carry average (4.4), and allowed the tenth most first downs via the run (35). According to FOX Sports , Arizona’s defense is ranked #26 overall. That is broken down into a #25 ranking for the passing defense and a #23 ranking for the run defense. What are the issues? Against the Lions, the Cardinals’ defense forced three straight three-and-outs to begin the game. Then, it was a jailbreak, with Detroit scoring six touchdowns and a field goal. They scored 24 points in the second quarter and 14 in Quarter 3. Huge passing gains were rampant. And the pass rush? Should we say the lack of a pass rush? Only DT Roy Lopez was putting some pressure into Detroit’s backfield and had a good game against the run. In the postgame press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur didn’t act disappointed or sad; instead, he was pissed. Regarding the defensive effort, he stated: “Obviously, not good enough. I know we’re better than that, but that doesn’t mean s*** right now.” Before being hired as the head coach of the Cardinals, LaFleur and Rallis had no connection with past employment. While LaFleur has been situated along the West Coast, Rallis was mainly with the Philadelphia Eagles, coaching with former Arizona head coach Jonathan Gannon. LaFleur simply kept him as his DC. But last year, the Cardinals defense wasn’t spectacular either. They finished the year ranked #26 overall, allowing an average of 363.4 yards a game. Both the run defense and pass coverage were in the bottom third in the league. When Gannon hired Rallis, he was considered one of the brighter minds in the game with plenty of youth behind him. In 2025, The Athletic featured him in its “NFL 50 under 40” list of ascending coaches and front office personnel. Right now, Arizona’s defense under Rallis is struggling to play at a level that gives the team a chance to win. What do four consecutive losses giving up 30+ points tell any Cardinals fan? No matter what this offense accomplishes, it is erased by the defense not being able to close out games late. And this is not simply a one-off. Last year, the Cardinals had a late lead and lost in seven contests. Remember when the offense was down 14 points to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 only to come back and tie the game? Seattle got the ball back with just 28 ticks on the clock, then went bip-bip-bip before kicking the winning field goal. All the defense had to do was contain, then take the game into overtime. Look at this year’s Seahawks game. Everyone in the league knows what to expect from Seattle WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He is a weapon, yet did Rallis give Smith-Njigba double coverage and force their offense to throw to other pass catchers? Hell no. What occurred instead was that the talented receiver had 155 yards and scored three touchdowns. He became the runner-up for “NFC Offensive Player of the Week.” Against the Lions, where was the run defense? RB Jahmyr Gibbs ran willy-nilly on his way to 151 yards on just 25 carries with two touchdowns, then rarely got any coverage from a linebacker when he went out for a short pass. He had five receptions for 56 yards. The Cardinals’ continued defensive struggles don’t seem to have an end game. Each week, it is going to be more of the same. Maybe a change at the top needs to be made and is in the franchise’s best interest to move on from Rallis. Most NFL coaches and GMs will not reveal anything pertinent to almost every situation. In the presser, LaFleur was asked if any coaching changes are on the horizon after getting blasted for 45 points. The question specifically was, “Do you need to make any changes to the defense coaching?” LaFleur’s response: “There’s a lot to fix right now, and I respect the question. I understand that, and I get it comes with the territory right now. My focus is on me fixing everything. None of it’s good enough. And again, anytime there’s a blowout like this, it starts with coaching. It’s not the players. It starts with us.” Like always, just Hollywood talk without anything that has legs. And no head coach is going to come right out and say that one of his coaches is probably going to kick rocks. There is respect in this league, and it is a rarity to throw others under the bus. Plus, it is a decision that needs to be thought out first and discussed within the organization and not be decided on the spur of the moment at the podium after a bad loss. And LaFleur is a guy who is going to point the finger at himself all day long. During last week’s press conference, Rallis was asked about the weekly 30+ points per game. He said: “Yeah, that sucks. Just focus on the process.” Come again? That’s it? No resolutions to the issue? Now, we get that the offense has its own set of problems and such; the defense is on the field more than ideal. Players get winded, especially in the final quarter. But Rallis didn’t offer any solutions whatsoever. And it isn’t going to get any easier. A glance at the schedule reveals upcoming games against the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Broncos, Dallas Cowboys, Seahawks, Rams, and then the Kansas City Chiefs. Raise your hand if you believe things will be different against these offenses. The Arizona Cardinals are sticking with defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, despite allowing 30 points in four straight games. Here's why. https://t.co/Ss8Xxwu9C8 — azcentral (@azcentral) October 13, 2026 In LaFleur’s first stint as an NFL head coach, he surrounded himself with veteran coaches on both sides of the ball. Rallis was already in Arizona, and it was an easy fix. But there is very little pass rush; the defensive backfield suffers from having to cover guys for way too long, minimal coverage from the linebackers on tight ends and running backs flaring out of the backfield, and the run defense is allowing 126.6 yards per game. Last season, they gave up 28.7 points on average per game, which ranked #29 in the league. DT Walter Nolen was brought in to solve the run defense and has been hurt repeatedly. Even though he is healthy this year, he has been a non-factor. DE Josh Sweat was the big splash signing and netted 12.0 sacks last year, yet is the invisible man with the pass rush this season. DE Darius Robinson is taking up space and getting a paycheck, and LB…

title: Week 5 3 up and 3 down: The Falcons lost as a team
summary: The Atlanta Falcons blew it in primetime. It’s easy to handpick one or two plays, but this loss was a team effort. That said, there are still performances worth highlighting. Here’s the Week 5, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Sydney Brown Brown has been one of Cunningham’s best additions. In Jeff Ulbrich’s scheme, […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons flips while hurdling Jaylinn Hawkins #21 of the Baltimore Ravens in the third quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons blew it in primetime. It’s easy to handpick one or two plays, but this loss was a team effort. That said, there are still performances worth highlighting. Here’s the Week 5, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Sydney Brown Brown has been one of Cunningham’s best additions . In Jeff Ulbrich’s scheme, the hybrid safety does it all, playing in the box like a LB and as third safety/big nickel in other packages. He has a nose for the football and has been one of the secondary’s more reliable tacklers. Brown has far exceeded expectations and is more than an upside special teams addition; he’s a critical piece of Ulbrich’s defense. The team should prioritize extending him if he keeps playing well. Sydney Brown is a spark plug pic.twitter.com/9jIfyPBwii — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 Jessie Bates III Bates delivered a vintage performance after a lackluster start to the season. He scored his first defensive touchdown of the season and had his best day in coverage. Bates kept the lid on the back end of the field, and while the Falcons couldn’t hold on to the lead, his play wasn’t the reason why. It’s good to see Bates hitting his stride because the secondary continues to take on injuries, and they have a Ben Johnson offense on deck. Drake London London is still Penix’s go-to target, and it’s easy to see why. When third down reared its ugly head, London routinely moved the chains. London was targeted six times on third down and hauled in five passes, moving the chains on each completion. We’d all like to see Penix spread the ball a bit more, but it’s nice to know he has a legitimate security blanket for the game’s toughest moments. Thanks to the Falcons play-action offense, London is finding himself in more space than ever , but he’s still getting the job done when he doesn’t have that space. Every Drake London 3rd down target from Week 5 pic.twitter.com/dgAC9LN37g — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 3 down Divine Deablo When asked about the Ravens putting up 208 yards on the ground, Deablo said, “Put it on me.” While no one player is entirely to blame, Deablo is right that he deserves a fair share of it. He turned in a rough performance. Deablo has been out of his gap too often and has struggled to diagnose plays at the speed we became accustomed to in 2025. The hamstring injury is definitely holding him back, but the linebacker often seems to be in his own head and tries to make a play instead of just doing his job. He has regressed this season, but he’s not far off from getting back on track if he can clean up these mental mistakes. Jake Matthews Father Time comes for us all. Yes, the dropped touchdown was bad, but bigger issues need addressing. Matthews looks like a sled on most of his reps, getting blown off the snap with ease in both the passing and running game. He was dealing with an injury all week, but this performance isn’t a one-off. It feels like he’s hanging on by a thread, and it’s always hard to watch a team legend not perform up to their standard, but most people can see now that upgrading the tackle position will need to be a priority this offseason. Rough outing for Matthews and the OL pic.twitter.com/jAAAOLMkVE — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 Coaching This was the staff’s first disappointing game of the season. Why call a passing play for Jake Matthews when he’s been dealing with a groin injury all week? How do you see Zachariah Branch turn a short pass into a big 1st down conversion and never go back to that well? On the other side of the ball, Jeff Ulbrich flip-flopped between soft zone and ineffective blitzes to protect the lead. We can give him grace, knowing he was dealing with an injury to CJ Henderson, but the calls still weren’t good enough. The Ravens made better adjustments at halftime, and the Falcons staff had little to no answers. A loss like this feels all too familiar for Falcons fans. Frustration is high, and the team is below .500, but they’re still 2-1 under Penix and should remain competitive game to game. Being competitive is only a moral victory, but the season is far from over.
author: Tre'Shon Diaz

title: Michael Penix rib injury update: Falcons QB should be ‘good to play’ vs. Bears
summary: If you’re like me, you watched the end of Ravens-Falcons on Sunday night with an overwhelming sense of dread. The moment Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. pulled that towel over his head on the sideline as the Ravens rolled in overtime, I knew the game was over. And I was very worried about Penix’s availability […]
full_text: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you’re like me, you watched the end of Ravens-Falcons on Sunday night with an overwhelming sense of dread. The moment Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. pulled that towel over his head on the sideline as the Ravens rolled in overtime, I knew the game was over. And I was very worried about Penix’s availability in the short term. Thankfully, Penix was able to practice fully on Wednesday. After practice, he noted that he made all of his throws on Wednesday. “They get better every day. I felt good today at practice,” Penix said. “… I just gotta stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I’m doing all the right things.” Penix would not elaborate on the nature of the injury (he was asked if it’s a bruised rib, and he said he didn’t want to get too specific). But he did tell us the MRI was positive. Thankfully, before I got a chance to, Marc Raimondi from ESPN clarified with Penix that the MRI was not positive for any type of injury, but the results of the MRI were positive for Penix’s chances to start agains the Bears on Sunday. “Positive means I’m good to play,” said Penix. Even though Penix felt good in practice, it wasn’t perfect. “It’s not always comfortable, but I made every throw today,” he said. During the limited portion of practice we are permitted to watch, Penix was definitely moving around well today. There wasn’t any noticeable hesitation or gingerness in his rib area as he worked through drills. One little bit of luck for Atlanta is the absence of Montez Sweat this week due to his suspension for violating the league’s PED policy . But Penix, while acknowledging the mark Sweat can leave on games, said that the rest of the defensive front in Chicago is also tough. “I feel like he is an impact player, so he makes impacts on games, but the next-man-up mentality in the league — I feel like the guys that’s right behind are almost as good. They’re very close. So it’s hard for us to try to say that that’s going to change much because of him being out.” We’ll see what the official injury report says about Penix when it’s released Wednesday, and we’ll continue to monitor his status through the week and heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bears.

With Penix Jr. exiting the game with a rib injury—which doesn’t appear to be serious—Atlanta’s ability to compete in Week 6 and beyond becomes murkier. While the Falcons were in excellent position to win the game in regulation on Sunday Night Football, this team’s old habits of blowing late leads reared their ugly head once more. That makes projecting Atlanta all the more difficult heading into this week’s matchup with the red-hot Chicago Bears offense. FanDuel currently has the Falcons as 2.5-point home underdogs to the Bears , with an over/under set at 50.5. This is clearly expected to be an offensive showcase, but questions about the starting quarterbacks for both teams linger. That’s casting a bit of a shadow over this matchup, as the Bears are coming off their worst performance of the season against a Packers team that the Falcons absolutely embarrassed just a few weeks prior. If Williams returns, I’d expect the line to shift heavily towards Chicago before kickoff. If Penix Jr. returns, I’d think the same for Atlanta. If both are slated to play, things may largely stay the same—just with the over/under increasing several points. We’ll hope for positive health updates for the Falcons this week as we await the status of multiple players who left Sunday night’s game, including multiple cornerbacks. title: Ravens release WR Chris Moore with rookie Ja’Kobi Lane nearing return
summary: Update, October 14: Moore has indeed re-signed to the Ravens’ practice squad, according to the NFL’s daily personnel notice. He will likely remain the team’s next receiver up in case of another injury this season until and unless the coaching staff is comfortable with putting fourth-round rookie Elijah Sarratt on the field. The Baltimore Ravens […]
full_text: Football - NFL - Baltimore Ravens v Dallas Cowboys - Estadio Maracana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - September 27, 2026 Baltimore Ravens' Chris Moore celebrates scoring their third touchdown REUTERS/Brian Snyder | REUTERS Update, October 14: Moore has indeed re-signed to the Ravens’ practice squad, according to the NFL’s daily personnel notice. He will likely remain the team’s next receiver up in case of another injury this season until and unless the coaching staff is comfortable with putting fourth-round rookie Elijah Sarratt on the field. The Baltimore Ravens released veteran wide receiver Chris Moore on Tuesday, per a team announcement , likely clearing a roster spot for the return of third-round rookie Ja’Kobi Lane from injured reserve. Lane fractured his wrist in Week 1 and underwent surgery shortly after. He is eligible to return to practice on Wednesday. Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that the 6-foot-4 wideout has “done a really good job” staying physically ready to play during his time on the sidelines. “I think he is in a really good place from a conditioning standpoint, from what he has been able to do with the training room and the rehab standpoint,” Minter added. Moore, originally a Ravens fourth-round pick in 2017, returned to Baltimore in July and made a push for the 53-man roster. He was unlikely to dislodge second-year receiver/returner LaJohntay Wester, who would have been exposed to waivers if cut. As a vested veteran, he was not subject to waivers and immediately re-signed to the practice squad. He appeared in four of the Ravens’ first five games and played 97 snaps on offense, primarily as a blocker. He did make a few plays through the air, including a 53-yard catch in Week 1 and a four-yard touchdown in Week 3. The Ravens also released wide receiver Xavier Guillory from their practice squad on Tuesday, clearing a spot for Moore to re-sign on Wednesday. He still has two game day elevations remaining. Baltimore’s receiving corps has been just fine without Lane. Zay Flowers has been the most efficient pass-catcher in the NFL, Rashod Bateman has 233 yards in the last four games, and Devontez Walker is still making an impact play on nearly every catch. However, Lane’s size could be valuable amid the current issues in the Ravens’ tight end room. Durham Smythe is out for the season with a torn Achilles, and Matt Hibner suffered a hand injury in Atlanta, though he returned to the game. Mark Andrews has been struggling with drops and is not the athletic downfield threat he once was. With Smythe sidelined, Andrews is the Ravens’ best blocking tight end. He may need to take on more inline duties with Lane getting looks as a big slot who can find space in the middle of the field. His size could also help with Baltimore’s goal-to-go woes. The former USC standout was the Ravens’ most exciting rookie in training camp with highlight-reel catches almost every day. The team’s two draft picks before him, Vega Ioane and Zion Young, have impressed in the trenches thus far, and a strong comeback from Lane would cement 2026 as one of Eric DeCosta’s best draft classes.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens vs Falcons: the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: In a thrilling overtime win, the Baltimore Ravens managed to top the Atlanta Falcons despite missing Lamar Jackson. The 30-23 win moved the Ravens to 4-1 in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. It was mostly good on Sunday night, with two glaring issues: The Good Backup quarterback situation: Fans were caught […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Devontez Walker #81 of the Baltimore Ravens catches a touchdown against Mike Ford Jr. #28 of the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a thrilling overtime win, the Baltimore Ravens managed to top the Atlanta Falcons despite missing Lamar Jackson. The 30-23 win moved the Ravens to 4-1 in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. It was mostly good on Sunday night, with two glaring issues: The Good Backup quarterback situation: Fans were caught up in the Joe Fagnano hype during the preseason, but in Atlanta, Tyler Huntley reminded the NFL world why he is Lamar Jackson’s backup. He wasn’t perfect and waited to fully turn it on until the end of the game, but Huntley simply knows how to win as a spot starter. He’s now 3-0 in his starts dating back to last season. When the Ravens needed a quick drive and couldn’t lean on the run, Huntley drove the Ravens 71 yards in under two minutes to tie the game. When they needed to kill clock, he confidently commanded the offense down the field. The dude is simply a gamer who does what is needed to win. The WR trio: Zay Flowers with eight catches and 53 yards. Rashod Bateman with five catches and 62 yards. Tez Walker with the back shoulder fade ball touchdown catch. The Ravens needed offensive skill players to step up with Lamar Jackson out and the wide receivers did just that. This passing game officially runs through them, and now they’re finally getting Ja’Kobi Lane in the mix, too. Run defense: Michael Penix came into Sunday’s game hot, but the entire football world that the Ravens would have to find a way to stop (or at least slow) the even-hotter Bijan Robinson to beat the Falcons. Robinson is the best running back in the NFL this season and a monster primetime performer. He had games of 194 and 145 yards coming into this one since Penix’s return. And instead of allowing him to tote the rock all night, gashing them for first down after first down, and draining the clock, the Ravens held him to 86 yards. They allowed rushes of 20 and 38 yards and otherwise kept a lid on his carries. Baltimore also contained Robinson in the red zone and didn’t allow him to score. The coaching staff: This was a big moment for this new young staff. No Lamar Jackson, no Trey Hendrickson, a reshuffled offensive line, on the road, in primetime, against a red-hot team. All of those questinos, and the coaching staff answered. Jesse Minter and Anthony’s Weaver’s defense kept this game in striking distance all night, only allowing one defensive touchdown and containing Robinson. Declan Doyle dialed up plays and kept the game simple for Huntley. This staff made a plan that gave this team a chance to win. The Bad Third-and-long defense: The most concerning negative out of this game was the third-down defense. It continues to be a problem. The Ravens allowed multiple third-and-10s, a third-and-11, and a third-and-15 to be converted. The plan was clearly to force Penix to beat them after shutting down Robinson in the run game, and Penix did, multiple times, often to Drake London, the Falcons’ No. 1 receiver. Coverage on the back end still seems to be struggling if the rush doesn’t get home on third down. Jesse Minter took the blame on himself, saying his play calling left them in bad spots. Either way, it’s an issue that has to get fixed, and I believe it will. Trey Hendrickson returning to the lineup will help out a ton. It’s also something that will simply get better with time as Minter and the defense get more comfortable in their identity. As the comparison that everyone wants to look to, Mike Macdonald’s defense in Seattle struggled their first season as Macdonald adjusted to being a headcoach and a play calling while installing his vision. Minter’s unit will adapt. The Ugly Mark Andrews: I have been an advocate for Mark Andrews’ play this season. Not to say that I agreed with the decision to re-sign him, but Mark Andrews is still very much capable of playing the tight end position. He is still a good blocker and capable of being a possession tight end, as we saw in the last couple of weeks. But what occurred on Sunday was atrocious and near malpractice. Mark Andrews directly influenced a 13-point swing in favor of Atlanta. First, a dropped touchdown that traded three instead of seven for the Ravens. Then a fumble that was recovered for a touchdown by Atlanta. Then a dropped two-point conversion in the third quarter. Andrews did manage to make some pivotal catches on the last drive in regulation that led to the tie and the overtime drive for the game-winner. But the Ravens could have won this in regulation if not for his mistakes. Still, Baltimore’s offense is stuck with Andrews after Durham Smythe’s injury. They simply don’t have a choice. He’s the most experienced tight end with only two rookies and Nick Vannett joining him on the active roster in an unfamiliar scheme. He needs to transition into being a possession tight end and stop trying to be the player he once was.
author: Zach Canter

However, only two injured Ravens missed today’s practice entirely: quarterback Lamar Jackson and tight end Matthew Hibner. 12 others were limited, including seven with new injuries presumably picked up during […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens listed a whopping 19 players on their first injury report of Week 6 ahead of next Sunday’s matchup with the Cleveland Browns. However, only two injured Ravens missed today’s practice entirely: quarterback Lamar Jackson and tight end Matthew Hibner. 12 others were limited, including seven with new injuries presumably picked up during Sunday night’s win over the Atlanta Falcons. The most positive news was the full participation of rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane in his first practice since fracturing his wrist in Week 1 and outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, who missed the last two games after undergoing surgery to repair a broken finger. Here is Baltimore’s full Wednesday injury report ( * denotes new injury) Full participation TE Mark Andrews (hand) S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) * OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist, designated to return from injured reserve ) Limited participation WR Rashod Bateman (shoulder) LB Teddye Buchanan (groin) * CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) G Emery Jones Jr. (knee) * C Cam Jurgens (concussion) RT Roger Rosengarten (knee) * LG John Simpson (groin) LB Trenton Simpson (hamstring) * LT Ronnie Stanley (non-injury related/rest, toe, ankle) TE Nick Vannett (knee) * G Andrew Vorhees (foot) DT Broderick Washington (ankle) * Did not participate DL Calais Campbell (non-injury related/rest) TE Matthew Hibner (hand) * QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) The Browns reported 17 injuries of their own to start Week 6. Their top non-participants on Wednesday were defensive tackles Maliek Collins, Mason Graham, and Mike Hall, right tackle Tytus Howard, running backs Qunshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane to return to practice
summary: Update, 2:11 p.m. ET: Lane is indeed practicing with the Ravens on Wednesday, per multiple reports. Also on the field are outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, who has missed the last two games after finger surgery, and newly-acquired center Cam Jurgens, who is still progressing through concussion protocol in a non-contact jersey. However, Lamar Jackson was […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MD - AUGUST 26: Ja'kobi Lane #6 of the Baltimore Ravens makes a catch during the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens joint practice at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on August 26, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update, 2:11 p.m. ET: Lane is indeed practicing with the Ravens on Wednesday, per multiple reports. Also on the field are outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, who has missed the last two games after finger surgery, and newly-acquired center Cam Jurgens, who is still progressing through concussion protocol in a non-contact jersey. However, Lamar Jackson was not out on the field during the media viewing period. Not practicing in open portion of practice: QB Lamar Jackson (ankle), WR Rashod Bateman, TE Matt Hibner (hand) and DL Calais Campbell. Campbell has been getting Wednesday’s off. — Jeff Zrebiec (@jeffzrebiec) October 14, 2026 Ja’Kobi Lane’s Week 1 injury was by far the biggest disappointment coming out of the Baltimore Ravens’ season-opening win. The third-round pick had lit up the practice field throughout training camp and flashed in his limited preseason action, raising expectations for a rookie breakout in Declan Doyle’s new offense. But a fractured wrist that required surgery forced Lane onto injured reserve. His mandatory stay of four weeks has now elapsed, making him eligible to re-join his teammates at practice this week. He is expected to do so on Wednesday, per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo . This would be the first player the Ravens have designated to return from IR this year, so here is a quick reminder on the rules. Teams can activate up to eight players from IR during the regular season. Players can first be designated to return to practice, opening up a three-week window for them to participate with the team without counting against the 53-man roster. After that period elapses, those players must be activated or revert to season-ending IR. The latter should not be an issue for Lane, who was praised by head coach Jesse Minter on Monday for keeping up with his conditioning while sidelined . The Ravens released Chris Moore on Tuesday, seemingly opening up a spot for Lane. The 6-foot-5 rookie could even be activated directly off IR instead of ramping up in practice for a few weeks. Even amid Lane’s absence (and Zay Flower’s hamstring injury), Baltimore’s receiving corps has produced plenty over the last few weeks. Lane will only take the group’s ceiling even higher. He drew three targets on just 18 routes in his NFL debut and should play a major role in the red zone moving forward. His availability as a quarterback-friendly target could also be a boon for backup quarterback Tyler Huntley should he be tapped to start again in Week 6.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens Week 5 film study: Malaki Starks thrives in versatile role
summary: Baltimore’s comeback victory over the Atlanta Falcons featured plenty of heroics, but what made this performance different from previous weeks was the impact of several role players stepping up in critical moments. Malaki Starks delivered arguably his best performance of the season, Justice Hill reminded everyone why his versatility and pass protection make him such […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Trenton Simpson #32 and Malaki Starks #24 of the Baltimore Ravens tackle Brian Robinson Jr. #15 of the Atlanta Falcons in the third quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore’s comeback victory over the Atlanta Falcons featured plenty of heroics, but what made this performance different from previous weeks was the impact of several role players stepping up in critical moments. Malaki Starks delivered arguably his best performance of the season, Justice Hill reminded everyone why his versatility and pass protection make him such a valuable piece of the offense, and Nick Vannett stepped into a larger role following Durham Smythe’s injury, providing some much-needed stability as a run blocker. S Malaki Starks 62 snaps | 23 run defense | 38 coverage | 1 pass rush | 10 tackles | 3 TFLs | 1 pressure Starks entered Week 5 following an inconsistent start to the season, with some already questioning whether the former first-round selection would live up to expectations. Against Atlanta, Starks delivered arguably his best performance of the season, leading Baltimore with 10 tackles, including three tackles for loss and a pressure. One of the most interesting developments was how defensive coordinator Jesse Minter deployed him closer to the line of scrimmage. Starks operated from several different alignments, contributing as a run defender, underneath coverage player and occasional pressure threat. Ravens Safety Malaki Starks – 10 tackles, 3 TFL, 1 pressure. pic.twitter.com/o6wmSYJhkh — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 13, 2026 On one rep, Starks aligned near the far edge of the formation and worked down the line of scrimmage to bring down the ball carrier in the backfield. On another, he aligned outside the tight end and attacked into the backfield, forcing Michael Penix Jr. into an early throw. His tackling ability was also on display throughout the afternoon. After missing an opportunity on Atlanta’s opening possession, Starks settled in and showed excellent closing speed and technique in the open field. On one rep, he made an impressive tackle against Bijan Robinson, while on another he ran the alley and closed downhill to secure another stop. His ability to diagnose plays and attack his landmarks with confidence was particularly encouraging. Baltimore’s secondary has struggled with consistency through the early portion of the season, and Starks developing into a dependable presence would go a long way toward improving the unit. His versatility allows Minter to utilize him in several different roles without sacrificing personnel flexibility, particularly near the line of scrimmage. If Starks continues playing with the decisiveness and physicality he displayed against Atlanta, he has an opportunity to become a significant contributor to Baltimore’s defensive improvement as the season progresses. RB Justice Hill 35 snaps | 24 receiving | 5 pass blocking | 4 rushing | 73 yards | 2 catches | 5 rec. yards Hill made his impact felt in multiple phases of Baltimore’s victory over Atlanta, reminding everyone why the coaching staff continues to trust him in passing situations over Derrick Henry. Hill’s value extends well beyond his ability as a runner, and his performance in pass protection was particularly impressive. On one rep, Hill aligned as a wing attached to the offensive line and delivered a violent chip against an Atlanta edge defender, knocking him to the ground before releasing into his route. Later in the game, he executed another effective chip from a similar alignment. When working from the backfield, Hill consistently showed good timing and physicality, absorbing contact and redirecting pass rushers to provide additional support for his offensive linemen. Ravens RB Justice Hill 4 carries for 73 yards Pass pro isn’t passive. pic.twitter.com/yRiHrCXl6x — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 13, 2026 As a runner, Hill provided Baltimore’s longest rushing play of the afternoon. On that rep, he aligned as a fullback in the backfield and settled into a three-point stance, creating an interesting wrinkle for Atlanta’s defense. Hill exploded through the interior for a massive gain before eventually being brought down. He finished with 73 rushing yards on just four carries, adding two receptions for five yards. His ability to contribute as a runner, receiver and blocker gives offensive coordinator Declan Doyle flexibility in how he deploys Baltimore’s personnel. Hill’s reliability in pass protection will become increasingly important as the season progresses, particularly against defenses that utilize more complex pressure packages. His ability to recognize blitzes, deliver effective chips and redirect rushers makes him an invaluable piece of Baltimore’s third-down offense. While his production as a runner was impressive, his contributions without the football were arguably just as important. TE Nick Vannett 19 snaps | 2 receiving | 17 run blocking | 81.3 run-blocking grade (team-high) With Durham Smythe suffering a season-ending Achilles injury the previous week, Baltimore needed someone to step into a significant blocking role at tight end. Vannett, who was promoted from the practice squad to the active 53-man roster, answered that call with an encouraging performance against Atlanta. His usage was relatively straightforward, with 17 of his 19 offensive snaps coming as a run blocker. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle clearly intended to utilize Vannett as an additional blocker in Baltimore’s rushing attack, and he executed his assignments effectively. Ravens Tight End Nick Vannett Signed to the 53 man roster last week. Did a very nice job climbing to level 2 and sealing off running lanes. pic.twitter.com/xlZPtTDR4Y — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 14, 2026 On multiple reps, Vannett worked in combination with the neighboring offensive lineman before climbing to the second level of the defense, sealing off linebackers and creating rushing lanes for Derrick Henry. His functional play strength was particularly noticeable, consistently establishing leverage and using his hips to turn defenders away from the ball carrier. Rather than simply attempting to overpower defenders, Vannett showed a good understanding of blocking angles and positioning, working to place his body between the defender and the intended rushing lane. His ability to transition from combination blocks to second-level assignments was another encouraging aspect of his performance. With Smythe unavailable for the remainder of the season, Baltimore will need dependable contributions from its remaining tight ends, particularly in heavier personnel packages. Vannett may not offer much as a receiving threat, but his ability to execute blocking assignments and provide a physical presence along the line of scrimmage gives the Ravens another useful piece in their offensive rotation. As the season moves toward December and January, his ability to help establish the rushing attack and create running lanes for Henry could become increasingly valuable. Snap counts and grades via Pro Football Focus.

title: AFC North Week 5 recap: Ravens on top after gutsy overtime win
summary: The Ravens took the lead in the AFC North with their win in Week 5, though all four teams in the divisionremain over .500 through five weeks. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) Baltimore gutted out a road win without Lamar Jackson, beating the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime. Tyler Huntley proved again why the Ravens have full […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 11: Baltimore quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) calls the play in the huddle during the NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons on October 11th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Ravens took the lead in the AFC North with their win in Week 5, though all four teams in the divisionremain over .500 through five weeks. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) Baltimore gutted out a road win without Lamar Jackson, beating the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime. Tyler Huntley proved again why the Ravens have full confidence in him at quarterback in place of Jackson with a strong performance against the Falcons. He finished 24 of 32 through the air with 201 yards and two touchdowns, along with a third score on a quarterback sneak in overtime. Derrick Henry was the other star of the show, rushing 24 times for 102 yards and scoring on an 18-yard screen pass. Baltimore’s offense ran for a total of 208 yards against the top-ranked run defense entering the week. Rashod Bateman led the receivers with 62 yards on five catches, while Devontez Walker scored a touchdown on the final game-tying drive of regulation. The Ravens defense struggled on third downs, but was otherwise solid against Atlanta’s high-powered offense. Mike Green, Tavius Robinson, and Trenton Simpson all had sacks on Michael Penix, while Malaki Starks led the team with 10 total tackles. Penix was injured on Robinson’s sack on the Falcons’ final drive of regulation, bringing Tua Tagovailoa onto the field. Tagovailoa then went on to throw a game-ending pick to Kyle Hamilton in overtime. Cleveland Browns (3-2) The Browns’ three-game win streak ended with a 17-12 loss to the New York Jets on the road. Deshaun Watson was under constant fire from the Jets, being sacked eight times and losing a fumble. He finished the day 15 of 33 passing for 155 yards and a touchdown. Isaiah Bond was the leading receiver with 74 yards on three catches, while rookie second-rounder Denzel Boston was the recipient of Watson’s lone touchdown to go with 43 yards on three receptions. Fellow rookie receiver KC Concepcion left the game with a concussion. Cleveland’s ground game continues to struggle as Quinshon Judkins finished with just 44 yards on 14 carries. Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain against New York, but is considered day-to-day. The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year had eight total tackles while forcing a fumble on a sack that was recovered by Adin Huntington. Huntington, Maliek Collins, and Sam Kamara combined for the other three sacks on Jets quarterback Geno Smith while Quincy Williams led the defense with 11 total tackles. Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) The Steelers rebounded in Week 5 with a 34-22 home win against the Indianapolis Colts. It was the Jaylen Warren show for Pittsburgh’s offense on Sunday. Warren accounted for 188 total yards, with 101 coming on the ground and 87 as a receiver. His two biggest plays of the day were both touchdowns, the first on an 80-yard catch-and-run and the second on a 50-yard rush. Pat Freiermuth had two touchdown catches to go with 44 yards on five receptions. Aaron Rodgers was on point in the passing game, completing 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns while only being sacked once. Rodgers lost another of his top receivers during the game, however, as Roman Wilson is expected to miss time with a finger injury. This comes just after wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury prior to Sunday’s game. Cameron Heyward had the only sack for the Steelers’ defense. Payton Wilson led the team with 10 total tackles. Pittsburgh’s defense consistently held the Colts’ offense to field goals, with 15 of their final 22 points coming from the leg of Spencer Shrader. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) The Bengals got back in the win column before their bye week with a 31-24 road win over the Miami Dolphins. Joe Burrow was on fire on Sunday, tossing four touchdowns while completing 23 of 32 pass attempts for 190 yards. Ja’Marr Chase had another highlight-reel touchdown catch while racking up 77 yards on six receptions. Tanner Hudson, Samaje Perine, and Mike Gesicki were the targets on Burrow’s other three touchdowns. Perine led the team in rushing with 68 yards on 14 carries, finishing with one more carry than Chase Brown, who rushed for 39 yards and coughed up a fumble. Cincinnati’s defense allowed 217 total rushing yards on the day. The unit faired better against the pass, as Jordan Battle snagged two interceptions off Malik Willis, who finished with just 137 yards through the air. The defense also sacked Willis three times, with Barrett Carter, Jonathan Allen, and Boye Mafe all getting home. Carter led the team with 11 total tackles.
author: Dustin Cox

title: Ravens news: Jesse Minter cracked the NFL’s new overtime rules
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover the praise for Jesse Minter’s overtime strategy on Sunday night against the Falcons, Tyler Loop flashing his range, and an update on just how good Zay Flowers is this year. Did the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover the praise for Jesse Minter’s overtime strategy on Sunday night against the Falcons, Tyler Loop flashing his range, and an update on just how good Zay Flowers is this year. Did the Ravens reinvent NFL overtime? When Kyle Hamilton won the overtime coin toss, most expected him to announce that the Ravens were kicking off. Conventional wisdom regarding the league’s new(ish) overtime rules dictated that teams wanted to possess the ball second so they had an information advantage. Depending on the results of the first drive, they would know exactly how many points they need to score to win or keep the game going. The Ravens had other plans. Head coach Jesse Minter – aided by game management coordinator Charlie Gelman and others on the staff – wanted to take advantage of a tired Falcons defense that just let Tyler Huntley drive down the field in less than two minutes. Atlanta’s vaunted run defense did not hold up against Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Huntley had (finally) settled into a rhythm through the air. Baltimore’s defense had also just injured Falcons quarterback Michael Penix on the final drive of regulation. He said after the game that he could have taken the field if Atlanta got the ball first. But Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle executed a masterful 14-play drive that took 7 minutes (and three seconds) off the clock. In that time, the adrenaline keeping Penix’s pain at bay subsided. He threw on the sidelines, but Tua Tagovailoa instead entered the game. Kyle Hamilton took care of things from there. Not every team is as capable of executing a clock-killing drive as one with Henry in the backfield. It would be interesting to see Lamar Jackson under center in these scenarios; it’s almost hard for him (and Zay Flowers) to not generate explosive plays. Other NFL teams will still try to copycat the Ravens’ success on Sunday night in future overtime games, which could also put the league in position for more ties. The Ravens hacked NFL overtime to beat the Falcons – James Dator (SB Nation) Using a heavy dose of Derrick Henry and short passing from Tyler Huntley, the Ravens executed a 14-play, 7:03-minute touchdown drive that both moved the ball all the way down the field for a touchdown, but critically forced the Falcons to use both of their timeouts, while leaving fewer than 3 minutes left on the clock. Henry ran the ball six times on the drive, the longest pass completion was for 10 yards. So much time was taken off the clock that when Baltimore was at 2nd and goal it was almost as if the Falcons had to the let them score , just to ensure they had a chance to possess the ball. Ben Gretch (Stealing Signals) What happened last night is the Falcons had to use both of their overtime timeouts on defense to preserve time. They got the ball back with just under three minutes, and only the 2-minute stoppage, and it forced them to be one-dimensional. On the broadcast, Collinsworth suggested kicking to force the Atlanta QB situation onto the field quicker. What Baltimore did attacked the Atlanta QB situation more; if Atlanta got ball first, they could’ve tried a run-based offense. They really couldn’t do that with 2:50 and no timeouts. Setting aside the specifics of Atlanta’s QB situation, EPA models look at next-drive success, because that’s crucial in football. What I’m suggesting is missed here is when a team executes like Baltimore did last night, the opponent’s drive success takes a substantial hit because of the clock constraint… …Anyway, Baltimore executed this brilliantly last night, and more teams should take note. Kicking off gives your opponent the ability to execute this. The Falcons didn’t necessarily run well last night, but they’ve been great on the ground in other recent games, and an alternate result last night where they had ball first could’ve been them executing a run-based offense that bled clock and put the Ravens in the situation they found themselves in, with not enough time to run a balanced offense and force to be one-dimensional and throw. Tyler Loop’s big leg is finally showing up NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games – Jamison Hensley (ESPN) Trend to watch: Ravens kicker Tyler Loop has become automatic from long range. He hit two field goals from 51 yards, improving to 5-of-5 from 50 yards or longer this season. This is a major change from last season, when Loop was 1-of-4 from 50 or longer as a rookie. Ravens news, notes and opinions: Reinforcements on the way, Year 2 growth and Tyler Loop’s range – Jeff Zrebiec (The Athletic) Long-distance Loop Tyler Loop made just one of four field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards last year. While Ravens coaches consistently touted his big leg, he faltered in his limited opportunities from distance. Through five games this year, he’s 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, and the Ravens don’t win the Cowboys or Falcons games without his ability to come through on long kicks. Zay Flowers’ numbers through six weeks are (still) ridiculous Zay Flowers Is Redefining What a No. 1 Wide Receiver Looks Like – Ryan Mink (BaltimoreRavens.com) There shouldn’t have been any questions about Flowers’ premier status after he finished seventh in the NFL in receiving yards last season. But the same tired “Is he a No. 1?” question arose when the Ravens gave Flowers a four-year, reportedly $140 million contract extension this offseason, ranking him fourth in average annual salary among wide receivers. Flowers has put the question to bed this season. By any metric, he’s been the most productive and unguardable wide receiver on a per-snap basis in the NFL. Flowers’ 405 receiving yards this season ranks eighth in the NFL, but he’s missed two games’ worth of snaps due to a hamstring injury. His quarterback, Lamar Jackson, has also now missed a game and a half. Per route run, Flowers leads the NFL with 4.5 yards. When Jackson has been under center, Flowers has averaged 9.1 yards per route run (and 5.3 yards per play).
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Bills Week 6 rooting interests: Who can help Buffalo climb the AFC?
summary: That was a better outcome than the week before. It wasn’t easy getting there, but the Buffalo Bills outlasted the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night to keep their hold on the top spot in the AFC East — something they were in danger of losing after the New England Patriots took down the Las […]
full_text: That was a better outcome than the week before. It wasn’t easy getting there, but the Buffalo Bills outlasted the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night to keep their hold on the top spot in the AFC East — something they were in danger of losing after the New England Patriots took down the Las Vegas Raiders the day before. Now it’s the Bills’ turn to face the Raiders on Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas. Despite the win, the Bills slipped to the AFC’s fourth seed. The Kansas City Chiefs hold the top spot thanks to a bye week and no chance to lose. Baltimore, Jacksonville, and Buffalo all sit at 4-1, but only the Bills have a division loss, putting them on the bottom rung of that ladder. Here’s a look at how the conference stands right now: Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) Baltimore Ravens (4-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) Buffalo Bills (4-1) New England Patriots (3-2) Denver Broncos (3-2) Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) Cleveland Browns (3-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) New York Jets (2-3) Indianapolis Colts (2-3) Houston Texans (1-4) Miami Dolphins (0-5) Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) Tennessee Titans (0-5) So, we know we’re rooting for Buffalo, but there are plenty of other games around the league — most of them before the Bills kick off. Let’s take a look at this week’s rooting interests and see where we might be able to get a little help. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders Root: Bills It’s not like you needed to be told to root for here. The Bills need to keep winning, especially with New England refusing to go away. A win in Las Vegas would move Buffalo to 5-1 and keep them in control of the AFC East. And after watching what the Patriots did to the Raiders last week, there’s no reason Buffalo shouldn’t be able to take care of business. Go Bills! New York Jets at New England Patriots Root for: Jets Yes, we’re rooting for the Jets. New England is sitting just behind Buffalo in the division, and the Patriots have already benefited from the Bills’ loss to Baltimore. A Jets victory would give Buffalo some breathing room in the AFC East. We don’t have to like these New York imposters. We just need them to win one football game. Miami Dolphins — Bye The Dolphins are still looking for their first win, and they won’t be getting it this week. At 0-5, Miami isn’t exactly threatening Buffalo’s division lead, so we can enjoy a week without having to think much about them. _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Seattle Seahawks at Denver Broncos Root for: Seahawks Denver is another AFC team we’d rather see collecting losses than wins. Seattle is an NFC opponent, making this a fairly easy choice. A Broncos loss helps keep another potential playoff contender from gaining ground. Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars Root for: Texans Jacksonville is currently sitting above Buffalo in the conference standings, and that’s reason enough to want the Jaguars to lose. Houston is a division rival for the Jags, so a Texans victory would also tighten up the AFC South race. Plus, a second win for Houston will bolster the Bills strength of victory score. Baltimore Ravens at Cleveland Browns Root for: Browns Baltimore is currently sitting ahead of Buffalo in the AFC standings, so we need the Ravens to start collecting some extra losses. A Cleveland win would knock Baltimore down to 4-2 and give the Bills a chance to move ahead of them in the conference standings. And since it’s a division game, there’s always the possibility of an upset. Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Root for: Titans Indianapolis is the bigger concern in the AFC playoff picture, so we’ll take a Tennessee victory here. The Titans haven’t given us much reason to expect one, but that doesn’t mean we can’t ask. Every loss for a potential AFC wild-card competitor is useful. And, don’t forget, it would be helpful if the bottom feeder AFC teams were slightly better than the bottom feeder NFC teams when draft time rolls around next Spring. Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Root for: Buccaneers Another easy AFC-versus-NFC decision. Pittsburgh is coming off a win over Indianapolis, and we’d prefer the Steelers not start building momentum of their own. Tampa Bay can help by sending them home with another loss. Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs Root for: Chargers Kansas City got to sit at home last week and watch everyone else play football. Now it’s time for the Chiefs to put that undefeated record on the line. The Chargers are also an AFC playoff contender, but Kansas City currently holds the conference’s top seed. We’re going to need someone to knock the Chiefs off that perch, and a division rival seems like a good place to start. Plus, I’m done rooting for KC – I hope I don’t have to again this season. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons Root for: Bears Buffalo hosts Chicago in December, so we’d like the Bears to start putting some more wins on their record before they make that trip. Chicago winning helps the Bills’ strength of schedule, and if Buffalo beats the Bears later this season, those victories will count toward strength of victory, too. The Bears are coming off a rough loss to Green Bay, so let’s hope they can bounce back against Atlanta. Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Root for: Rams Buffalo just picked up a win over the Rams on Monday night. Now we’d like Los Angeles to start winning again, because every Rams victory makes Buffalo’s win look a little better in the strength-of-victory calculation. We wanted the Rams to lose last week. This week, we’re happy to cheer them on. Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers Root for: Packers Green Bay is another team Buffalo has on the schedule, with the Bills headed to Lambeau Field in December. That means we’d like the Packers to keep winning between now and then. A Green Bay victory helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule, and if the Bills can beat the Packers later this season, all those wins become part of Buffalo’s strength-of-victory calculation. So, as much as it might pain some of us, we’re pulling for the Packers on Sunday night. Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers Root for: Commanders San Francisco is still undefeated, so we’re going to pull for Washington to change that. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, so there isn’t much at stake for the Bills in this one. But there’s no reason to help another conference’s top team stay perfect. Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Root for: Panthers Philadelphia has already lost to Jacksonville, and we’d be perfectly happy to see the Eagles take another loss. Carolina winning also keeps an NFC contender from getting too comfortable. But, there’s really no reason to get too worked up over this game. New Orleans Saints at New York Giants Root for: Saints This one isn’t going to move the AFC standings, and there’s no major reason for Buffalo fans to get worked up about the outcome. We’ll take New Orleans simply because we are tired of the Giants trying to claim they are New Yorkers. Plus, you know, history. But, in all honesty, this is one of those games where we can live with either result. _____________________________________________________________________________ Teams on Bye: Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings _____________________________________________________________________________ The Bills took care of their business Monday night, but the win didn’t move them up the AFC standings. In fact, they dropped a spot. That’s what happens when the teams around you keep winning, too. This week gives Buffalo a few opportunities to get some help. Baltimore and Jacksonville both have division games, Kansas City has to face the Chargers, and New England gets another chance to put pressure on the AFC East race. There are plenty…
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Bills injury report: Spencer Brown, Joshua Palmer limited Wednesday
summary: The Buffalo Bills held a walkthrough practice Wednesday in Southern California where the team is staying as they prepare for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. With a Monday night game that ran late and well into overtime, head coach Joe Brady opted for the extra day of rest.   That means the latest […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Spencer Brown #79 of the Buffalo Bills walks off the field after an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills held a walkthrough practice Wednesday in Southern California where the team is staying as they prepare for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. With a Monday night game that ran late and well into overtime, head coach Joe Brady opted for the extra day of rest. That means the latest injury report is a guess – an educated one, but a guess just the same. It also means that any of the injuries, and be prepared – there are a lot of them, came from either the game or are carried over from last week. No new injuries from practice is the silver lining here. Wednesday injury report pic.twitter.com/ti0dJw5ZIy — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 14, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Bills players not practicing: WR DJ Moore DT Ed Oliver This hasn’t changed. It’s still DJ Moore and Ed Oliver. Good news is that Spencer Brown’s name isn’t in this category. Bills players with limited practice: RT Spencer Brown CB Dee Alford DT T.J. Sanders RB Ty Johnson WR Joshua Palmer This is where we find Brown, who left Monday’s game with a back injury (likely spasms). The fact that they feel he could have practiced some is a good sign, but we really won’t know until the Bills hold a full practice tomorrow. Dee Alford is continuing to try get back into the game after missing part of Week 4 and all of Week 5 games with an ankle injury. While he’s listed as limited, it’s likely he’s trending toward playing. The Bills cut cornerback Anthony Kendall (and then signed him to the practice squad) this week after having signed him to the active roster to fill in for Alford this week. T.J. Sanders now has a shoulder injury and Ty Johnson is dealing with a hamstring issue. It’s also a good sign to see that Joshua Palmer would have been limited today after what seemed to be a practice injury last week sidelining him Monday. Bills players with full practice: S C.J. Gardner-Johnson OLB TJ Parker CB Christian Benford ILB Terrel Bernard OLB Bradley Chubb WR Keon Coleman DL Landon Jackson OG Ar’maj Reed-Adams The only new names here are C.J. Gardner Johnson and TJ Parker. Gardner-Johnson has both ankle and knee injuries, but after a mid-game scare the fact that he’s listed as a full participant is a good sign. No longer on the Injury List: LB Joe Andreessen RB Ray Davis S Damar Hamlin LB Dorian Williams It’s worth noting that there are several players from last week’s injury reports who no longer need extra attention from the Bills’ training staff. Those include Joe Andreessen and Ray Davis as well as Damar Hamlin and Dorian Williams. _____________________________________________________________________________ Again, Wednesday was a walk through, so the real test will comes Thursday when the pads go on and we get to see how these injuries hold up under more stress.

title: Buffalo Bills HC Joe Brady endorses current play of team’s starting LBs
summary: Fielding questions from the media inside the Bren Events Center on the campus at University of California, Irvine, Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady embraced taking advantage of opportunities. The center for this was of course the team’s decision to stay on the West Coast between Weeks 5 and 6, leveraging added time to prepare […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Terrel Bernard #8 and Dorian Williams #42 of the Buffalo Bills prepare to play the Detroit Lions at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fielding questions from the media inside the Bren Events Center on the campus at University of California, Irvine, Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady embraced taking advantage of opportunities. The center for this was of course the team’s decision to stay on the West Coast between Weeks 5 and 6, leveraging added time to prepare for their next game against the Las Vegas Raiders in Nevada. Yet one question lobbed about linebacker Shaq Thompson, who re-joined the team via the practice squad several week ago, revealed that Brady wasn’t willing to embrace the idea of any immediate opportunity at SAM or MIKE linebacker. When asked if there had been “any consideration to maybe getting him out there and seeing what it looks like,” Brady stoically said: “No. I mean right now (smirking) I think you’re not as [much of] a fan of the way our linebackers are playing, based off some of the questions. But no, I have no issues with the way our linebackers are playing right now. You know, Shaq, Shaq has — he knows he was brought here as, obviously from a leadership component and, you know, if an opportunity came up, and, you know, it’s a long season that having a guy like himself with his background and his history to be able to come in and play, and play meaningful football… and, you know, that’s why he’s here.” At its surface, that seems to settle any debate about how, when, or where Brady, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, and inside linebackers coach John Egorugwu plans to utilize Thompson this season. However, Brady elaborated on why the Bills have yet to turn to Thompson on games days. “Look, I like where the linebackers are at right now. They’re continuing to get better. I’d love for, you know, (rookie linebacker) Kaleb (Elarms-Orr) to play a little more than you know, he played the other day. And that’s not an indictment on Dorian (Williams) or TB (Terrel Bernard). That’s just being able to get these guys fresh, you know, throughout games and when the game’s on the line. So, no, I love having Shaq here. There’s a reason Shaq’s here, but I like how — where our linebackers are at right now.” Plenty of outsiders have asked for the team to begin a meaningful youth movement on defense, which includes linebacker. That includes giving Williams a true featured opportunity, and perhaps throwing Elarms-Orr to fight off the bulls as a rookie. It also means allowing Bernard to adapt to a new system — the same as his position mates. In listening to Brady, it sounds like a youth movement is in order on the field, and that means embracing any hiccups or struggles that may prove marginally detrimental. In Thompson, it’s clear Brady brought him back for the leadership component. It’s just that, for now at least, Thompson will have to continue doing so from the sidelines and in practice.

title: Are the 4-1 Buffalo Bills headed in the right direction after Week 5 win?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills stole a soul-crushing win from the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, reminding anyone still tuned in well past midnight on the East […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - October 12: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) is chased by Los Angeles Rams linebacker Nate Landman (53) during overtime of an NFL football game at Sofi Stadium on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026 in Inglewood, CA. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills stole a soul-crushing win from the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, reminding anyone still tuned in well past midnight on the East Coast that with quarterback Josh Allen, anything is possible. There were several heroes for Buffalo to embrace following the thrilling Monday Night Football win, from Allen, to outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, and a special teams unit highlighted by kicker Tyler Bass and his game-winning 48-yard field goal. Depending on your stance, you might even put running back James Cook III among the game’s heroes. Might… and why? It’s true that his fumbles have taken on a featured role in 2026, but it’s also worth wondering how many games they win this season with him on the sideline. That’s true of Week 4’s game. At 4-1, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East with a tenuous half-game lead over the 3-2 New England Patriots. Their only loss was to those Patriots, and it’s a situation where Buffalo must play their best football to maintain that lead throughout the season. Apart from Rousseau, the defense is a work in progress at best — while at times appearing to be a complete mess in trying to hold off opposing offenses. Buffalo currently ranks 30th in total defense, and 28th in points per game. The Bills also currently hold a turnover differential of -4, are they’re among the top-10 most penalized teams ( hat tip Trey Wingo ). There is a lot to work on, which you’ll hear ad nauseam from head coach Joe Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. That, of course, must happen while managing injuries, which right now has Buffalo evaluating right tackle Spencer Brown, who couldn’t finish in LA thanks to a back injury.
