title: NFL analyst claims Joe Burrow is ‘the best quarterback in football’
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have entered their 2026 bye week with a 3-2 record after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins this past weekend. The Bengals are in a better spot so far through 5 weeks than in the past few years, and that should excite Cincinnati fans. Another piece fans may not realize is […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have entered their 2026 bye week with a 3-2 record after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins this past weekend. The Bengals are in a better spot so far through 5 weeks than in the past few years, and that should excite Cincinnati fans. Another piece fans may not realize is that Joe Burrow is playing the best football of his career in the early part of a season. Burrow had some frustrating turnovers against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars, but outside of those, he has played at an elite level. One football analyst turned on the 2026 Burrow tape and believes without a doubt that he is the best quarterback in football right now. Mark Schlereth of the OG Football Podcast shared his thoughts on Burrow and stated: “I can see why they never run it.” "He's Brady-esque" Mark just was on the call for the Bengals vs Dolphins in Hard Rock and what he saw out of Joe Burrow made him rethink how he would evaluate this offense 😳 pic.twitter.com/501rNvmG1k — The OG Football Show (@OGFootballShow) October 12, 2026 “He is in a complete cylinder. He is so ‘Brady-esque’ in that he is the best scrambler in football that never leaves the pocket… If he sees a profit, he takes it instantly… It is incredible to watch; he is just the best quarterback in football without question,” Schlereth said. Burrow is the most accurate quarterback in the NFL and can dice up any defense across the league when healthy. The Bengals QB currently has 1,361 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and 3 interceptions through the first 5 games. Cincinnati will have their hands full out of the bye, visiting their AFC North rival in Baltimore, and Burrow will need to be at his best to leave with a win.
author: Patrick Carey

title: Bengals News: Is it Jack Endries time?
summary: With Tanner Hudson headed to IR and done for the season with a torn pec suffered in the Cincinnati Bengals’ win over the Dolphins, the offense is down one reliable tight end who has proven to be a trusted safety valve for Joe Burrow. While there’s no shortage of mouths to feed on the Bengals’ […]
full_text: With Tanner Hudson headed to IR and done for the season with a torn pec suffered in the Cincinnati Bengals’ win over the Dolphins, the offense is down one reliable tight end who has proven to be a trusted safety valve for Joe Burrow. While there’s no shortage of mouths to feed on the Bengals’ offense, they are down one tight end, and they just happen to have a tight end from this year’s draft on the roster. Former Texas tight end Jack Endries fell to the Bengals in the seventh round of this Spring’s draft and made the 53-man roster. He hasn’t taken any offensive snaps so far this season, only making a handful of appearances on special teams, but he caught six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown throughout the preseason. With Erick All not quite clicking, Endries has a real chance to shine now that Hudson is done for the year . Here’s what else is going on: Bengals RT Amarius Mims calls out major names after his unique problem pops up yet again in win over Dolphins “It’s crazy because that was the second I pair busted open, but that was my first time wearing the shoe,” Mims told WLWT’s Jaron May after the game. “Like I just got these in literally before we left for Miami, before we got on the plane, and I wore them. I looked down, man. My shoes are talking, man. My big toe. I see my big toe. I said, ‘Oh God, man, it’s not good.’ The Bengals fed the hot hand out of the backfield on Sunday in Miami, opting to give Samaje Perine 14 carries to Chase Brown’s 13. It’s close to being even, but Brown came into the season with a lock on RB1, and seemed to be the guy through the first couple games. Possibly not so much now, though, as Bengals’ offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher sees the situation as more fluid as they begin to run out of shotgun more, which suits Perine. Why the Bengals’ run game – and RB carry distribution – could be changing “I wouldn’t want to tackle (Perine),” Karras said. “When we get into our gun 11 (personnel) runs, Chase and Samaje both bring unique stuff where Chase can find a hole and hit it at 20 miles per hour. Samaje, even if you don’t get to the linebacker, he is running through it and going to take him 2, 3 yards to tackle him.” It wasn’t too terribly long ago when Jake Browning kept the Bengals’ playoff hopes alive while Burrow rehabbed from injury. Now Joe Flacco is the backup quarterback and Browning has a new home in Los Angeles. Browning has signed with the Chargers , who’ve started the 2026 season with an 0-5 record. title: Week 6 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland sees first fade in weeks after loss
summary: It is Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of a tough loss in the rain against the Jets. It’s one of those games that I can forgive them for because of the elements, but also, they were oh-so-close to being 4-1, which would’ve been incredible. Now, at […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns leads the offensive huddle during the third quarter of the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of a tough loss in the rain against the Jets. It’s one of those games that I can forgive them for because of the elements, but also, they were oh-so-close to being 4-1, which would’ve been incredible. Now, at 3-2, some of the national media has given them a cooler for their late-game mistakes, while still keeping them on the level of respectability. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.6 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 19.7 . Ranking-wise, that is still third in the division. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 19 (down 3 spots) They came back to reality some in the loss to the Jets. But at 3-2, they have to be thrilled with their start. ESPN – No. 23 (down 4 spots) Biggest issue on defense: Run defense The Browns’ defense rebounded after giving up 34 points to the Jaguars in Week 1, but the inability to stop the run has been a consistent theme this season. Cleveland is giving up 4.5 yards per attempt, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL. And its success rate on opponent rushes (52.8%) is the second-worst mark in the league. Tackling has been an issue; opponents are averaging 2.53 yards after contact per rush, which ranks 30th. NFL.com – No. 21 (down 4 spots) Cleveland’s method of leaning on defense and hoping the offense finds a fourth-quarter rhythm nearly worked out in the Browns’ favor, but a miserable sequence that included a regrettable-at-best approach while nursing a late lead, a botched snap on a punt and a disastrous final possession proved they can’t keep getting by with late-game heroics. They also still cannot run the ball, which won’t help matters in the future, no matter how effective rookie receiver Denzel Boston is in the second half. Sporting News – No. 20 (down 3 spots) The Browns came crashing down to earth around Deshaun Watson as he was denied a fourth consecutive fourth-quarter game-winning drive. Being pounded on the ground by the Jets was odd, too. Watson is on pace for 65 sacks after being dropped by the Jets eight times. That would be the most for him in his career, surpassing his second NFL season with the Texans, when he was sacked a league-high 62 times. Yahoo Sports – No. 22 (down 2 spots) The Browns were close to a much better day. Receiver Isaiah Bond was pressed into action after KC Concepcion’s concussion and he had a big drop in a big moments and once ran out of bounds when it seemed he could have pushed upfield for more yardage. One drop came in the end zone and another was on a second-and-19 that could have given the Browns a first down just ahead of the two-minute warning. Those plays were huge in a five-point loss. Still, the Browns failed to top 200 yards against a Jets defense that had just given up 492 yards to a Tyson Bagent-led Bears offense. Cleveland’s 3-1 start came with some close wins and the Browns were due some regression. Week 6’s game against the Ravens, who may be without Lamar Jackson, will be telling. Bleacher Report – No. 17 (down 5 spots) The Cleveland Browns are who we thought they were a few weeks ago. To their credit, they briefly held the lead in the fourth quarter Sunday. The defense is keeping the team in games week after week, but the offense remains a major weakness. Facing a Jets defense that the Chicago Bears dominated a week ago, the Browns did next to nothing. Bad weather or not, Cleveland managed just 198 yards of offense. There were no running lanes. Deshaun Watson was dropped a whopping eight times. After three straight wins, the Browns delivered an ugly, mistake-filled performance. Next week’s AFC North matchup against the Baltimore Ravens may not be a must-win, but Cleveland needs a strong response to bolster its credibility as a contender in 2026. USA Today – No. 16 (down 4 spots) Rookie WR Denzel Boston is leading the league with 20.6 yards per reception out of the gate − his three TD catches averaging 43.3 yards in length. full_text: (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns head into a big-time AFC North matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6, with injury concerns aplenty , including WR KC Concepcion . After what many fans believe was a dirty hit from S Minkah Fitzpatrick , Concepcion missed most of Week 5’s game. The Ravens have also been dealing with injury issues, including starting QB Lamar Jackson . Both teams have a number of other injury issues, as the first practices of the week get started, with the host Cleveland squad a betting underdog in Week 6 . That is especially true when you are talking about a famous player like Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders. Sanders […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 24/7 nature of sports media coverage almost never misses anything anymore. Things that used to happen behind closed doors quickly become out in the open, little things become big things, and interest almost never wanes. That is especially true when you are talking about a famous player like Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders . Sanders has only played one snap for the 3-2 Browns this season, after losing the starting quarterback competition to Deshaun Watson . The young QB was reportedly “chasing” in the competition the whole time. Trade speculation around Sanders is nothing new. A little over a week ago, ESPN added Sanders’ name to a list of young quarterbacks that could change hands, only to see Mary Kay Cabot throw fire on that possibility. On Wednesday, the trade rumor mill fired up once again after Sanders decided to hire an agent, instead of representing himself. How did hiring an agent connect the dots to a trade? Marvin Harrison Jr. : not saying he will be traded… but Marvin Harrison Jr. was also agent-less, until recently when he hired an agent to help facilitate a trade https://t.co/YKtjsUz13R — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 14, 2026 Is it possible that Sanders expects to be traded and hired an agent? That Sanders wants to be traded, so he hired an agent? That the Browns informed him he might be traded, so he wanted representation? Yes to all of those: Shedeur is in year 2 of a 4 year deal. He’s stuck behind Watson. He didn’t hire an agent when he *needed* one during the draft process. But now he hires one 5 games into his second season, with 12 games + 2 years left on his rookie deal? Use your brains. An agent seeks options. https://t.co/zrBLfOC7xM — Charles Robinson (@CharlesRobinson) October 14, 2026 Both @egoldie80 and @HammerNation19 think that something is up with the Browns and Shedeur Sanders and the news of him hiring an agent. Is a trade on the way? pic.twitter.com/d6e0S3TBN0 — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) October 14, 2026 It is also at least equally plausible that Sanders just decided to hire an agent at this time and chose the same one as his buddy, WR/CB Travis Hunter . For now, it is all speculation, but like when Cleveland adjusted DE Myles Garrett’s contract months before his trade, decisions like this could mean a lot… or nothing at all. title: Can the Browns’ offensive line be fixed? Does it need fixing?
summary: The Cleveland Browns lost to an inferior opponent this past weekend, when mistakes and a huge number of sacks gave the New York Jets a 17-12 victory. This was one team that all Cleveland fans had stuck a “W” on the schedule. The loss put the Browns at 3-2-0 instead of 4-1-0 and a lead […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns lost to an inferior opponent this past weekend, when mistakes and a huge number of sacks gave the New York Jets a 17-12 victory . This was one team that all Cleveland fans had stuck a “W” on the schedule. The loss put the Browns at 3-2-0 instead of 4-1-0 and a lead in the division. The Jets had eight sacks. It was a jailbreak on almost every passing down. RELATED: PLENTY OF BLAME WHEN THE OFFENSE STRUGGLES Is Cleveland’s offensive line that bad? What happened, and what is the fix? And not during the offseason, but now. Is this an offensive line issue, or is Browns QB Deshaun Watson to blame, or does it fall on the scheme, system of Todd Monken? Cleveland currently starts two rookies along their offensive line: LT Spencer Fano and RG Austin Barber. Barber has been inserted for the injured Tevon Jenkins, who remains out with a back issue. Maybe the inclusion of undeveloped players in the lineup can be the source of the blame for the poor play. Eight sacks. Obviously, something isn’t gelling. The Jets have had a formidable defense for years, with their problems usually on the offensive side of the ball. And they showed that on Sunday. It seemed like every time Watson dropped back to pass, there was a green jersey or two wrecking the pocket. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF) , the Browns offensive line as a whole is ranked #28. Ouch. But hold the phone. By PFF’s data, five of those sacks were credited to the offensive line. Sack #1 let's go rook 👏 #CLEvsNYJ on CBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/IxeJ0TlaaV — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 11, 2026 Fano is credited with a sack in the first quarter from LB David Bailey when Watson dropped the snap and the pocket went haywire. Sack #2 On a first down at New York’s 42-yard line with 12:57 left in the second quarter, Watson was back in shotgun, took the snap, and was almost instantly leveled by former Browns draft pick DE Jowon Briggs. What happened was that right off the snap, center Jenkins squared up but did not have a defender to block. At the same time, Barber took on Briggs while MLB Demario Davis came in without any blocker until he met RB Quinshon Judkins. Judkins’ block of Davis slammed the Jets defender into Barber, who then lost control of Briggs, and Briggs was now free and able to bear hug Watson for the sack. Sack #3 first career sack for Jarvis Brownlee Jr. 💪 📺: CBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/v1mdZ75lek — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 11, 2026 The third was also in Quarter 2 with 7:05 before the half. Bailey lined up at left end. Off the snap with Watson in shotgun, NB Brownlee blitzed, and Howard blocked down to take him. Meanwhile, Bailey was completely unblocked and had a free lane that Watson could do nothing about. Sack #4 here for the flamethrower nickname pic.twitter.com/0MZKqcDHKA — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 13, 2026 With 13:01 left in the game, Cleveland had a third-and-30 at their own 35-yard line. Bailey came off the snap like a bullet; the new RT, Dawand Jones, could not extend that long paw far enough, and Bailey was all over Watson quickly. Sack #5 Then, with 2:41 remaining, the Jets rushed six; Jones could not contain Bailey, who had the first shot, and then Watson went down; he had four New York defenders on top of him. Officially, it was Jackson credited with the sack. One sack was on the tight end. Early in the fourth quarter, facing a first-and-15 at the midfield stripe, the Jets were up 10-6. Brownlee came off the left side and met TE Harold Fannin. As Brownlee took an inside move, Fannin threw a shoulder at him and then had a straight shot at Watson. The QB tried to throw the ball in the direction of Boston, but the officials had ruled him down. On this play, the offensive line had provided a beautiful pocket. The other two sacks were on Watson. As the second quarter was winding down, Watson took the ball in shotgun, and the pocket stood up as the Jets only rushed four, then brought a fifth on a delay. Sanders stayed in to block and took out LB Jamien Sherwood. Watson had a window, but held it. He pumped, then brought it in. Meanwhile, Barber has lost control of his man, the blitzing safety Dane Belton. As Watson tried to go to his left and leave the pocket, Belton had a clean shot and decked the quarterback. Take the third-and-five play in the first quarter with the Browns on New York’s seven-yard line. Right off the snap, the Jets rushed six. Rocket Sanders was positioned in the backfield and remained in to block. Fano did not strike his defensive end, Darrell Jackson, but instead jumped outside to take on blitzing LB Will McDonald. Sanders would block Jackson. Johnson and Jenkins took on their defenders as usual. But on the rightside, the defensive end crashed down towards the middle, which left blitzing nickelback Jarvis Brownlee with a straight shot to Watson. Watson had to get rid of the ball quickly and threw it too high for WR Denzel Boston. Now, how should this formation be changed? The most obvious is to stick a blocking tight end alongside Howard, hit Brownlee as he approached, and then go out for his route. Boston had a small opening, but he would have been open if Watson had time to get off a good pass instead of forcing the throw. ( Editor’s Note: Does the Cleveland roster have a blocking tight end?) The end result was a field goal instead of six points. On the game’s final play, the pocket was there with enough time to survey the field. Bailey eventually got loose from Jones and then chased Watson. Now, if everyone was covered, then they were covered. Watson tried to scramble and look downfield since it was a fourth-and-11 play and there wasn’t a chance that Watson could run for that distance. Bailey caught up with him and the game was essentially over. Offensive line help Barber is really struggling. On several plays, he is just being pushed out of the way by much stronger men. On the sack with 2:41 left in the game, it was Bailey who made Watson step up, but Jackson completely pushed Barber out of harm’s way as he then smashed into the Browns signalcaller. His pass-blocking grade is pretty good at 64.0. Fano is playing very well. His pass-blocking grade is an impressive 77.2 so far. He has allowed just nine pressures in five games and has had one penalty accepted. He is ranked #14 out of 72 qualified offensive tackles. C Elgton Jenkins is the ace of this group and has been exceptional this year, especially with pass protection. His overall PFF grade is 62.6, but his pass-blocking ability has garnered him an 82.4 grade. That is #1 among 33 centers graded this year. Johnson also has a good pass protection grade of 76.6, but his run blocking needs work, plus he collects laundry, as he has four accepted penalties. But he has allowed zero sacks so far. At right tackle, Tytus Howard suffered a knee injury in the first quarter against New York and tried to return. His overall PFF grade is 50.3, but his pass-blocking skills are decent at 64.8. In his place, Jones was beaten badly and often by the Jets. If his man, Bailey, was getting to Watson, his actions were making Watson adjust his pocket presence or simply forcing him to leave the pocket entirely. The bad offensive line play against the Jets was a fair assessment. Here are a few facts that affected the outcome of the game: Total dropbacks under pressure: 18 Total sacks allowed: 8 Watson pressures allowed: 5 Offensive line pressures allowed: 8 RB/TE pressures allowed: 5 The eight pressures the offensive line allowed equate to 44.4%, which was the second-lowest rate in the league over the weekend. Another body in-line What would help the offensive line is to have a tight end or two who can actually block. ( Editor’s Note : Maybe don’t make the first editor’s note before reading the whole article, yet here we are with editor’s note #2) Blake Whiteheart looks to be involved in the blocking game, but he does not remain engaged and often loses his defender. title: Browns Week 6: Scouting the Baltimore Ravens with a new coach, lots of changes
summary: As the Browns look to rebound after a difficult loss at the hands of the New York Jets, the team will prepare for another divisional clash as the Baltimore Ravens come to Cleveland. Like the Browns, the Ravens also underwent a coaching change this past offseason. It’s the first meeting between the two teams, with […]
full_text: As the Browns look to rebound after a difficult loss at the hands of the New York Jets , the team will prepare for another divisional clash as the Baltimore Ravens come to Cleveland . Like the Browns, the Ravens also underwent a coaching change this past offseason. It’s the first meeting between the two teams, with the winner having sole possession of 1st place in the AFC North . New Year, New Harbaugh disciple It’s well documented that the Baltimore Ravens originally wanted current Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald as their head coach. Macdonald left the Ravens to be the Seahawks’ new head coach, and if he stayed he would’ve been next in line after John Harbaugh. It didn’t happen, but the Ravens decided to settle for Jesse Minter. Minter, who was on the Michigan Wolverines football staff with current Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, was the defensive coordinator for the Chargers last season. Minter going from the Chargers to the Ravens felt predictable, but it’s clear why Baltimore coveted him. Minter has put together an impressive staff, with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle evolving into a future head coaching candidate with how Baltimore’s offense has looked this season. Ravens offense could be better than last season’s One of the biggest improvements for the Ravens from last season is their offense. Current Browns head coach Todd Monken was able to improve the Ravens’ offense during his tenure, but this year’s looks more potent. Doyle, who was previously with the Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, deserves credit. Having an MVP-level quarterback in Lamar Jackson helps. The tandem of Jackson and running back Derrick Henry is one of the best QB/RB tandems in the league. This is an offense that can generate explosive plays early and often. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is starting to emerge, and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner is becoming a reliable target in the passing game. Despite an offensive line that’s unsettled in the interior, this is still one of the top offenses in the league. Baltimore is better than last year, dangerous down the stretch The only loss the Ravens had this year was to the New Orleans Saints, a game that Baltimore gave away. Outside of that, this team is better than last year’s team. The defense has some concerns but it’s still a unit that is talented. It seems as if Minter has tapped something into this team that Harbaugh couldn’t do the last two years. In close matchups in previous years, the Ravens would find ways to lose those games, but with wins over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil and recently with an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons (minus Lamar Jackson), this team seems to have gotten over their close-game woes. Baltimore is expected to get healthy, and if they do, this team will be primed for a deep playoff run in a wide-open AFC. What are your thoughts on the Ravens heading into Week 6 versus the Browns? title: Browns AFC North chances after Week 5 loss
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ loss to the New York Jets snapped their three-game winning streak and dropped their record to 3-2. It was definitely a setback in a part of the schedule that should have featured a very winnable game. One loss this early in the season doesn’t eliminate the team’s hopes of making a push […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ loss to the New York Jets snapped their three-game winning streak and dropped their record to 3-2. It was definitely a setback in a part of the schedule that should have featured a very winnable game. One loss this early in the season doesn’t eliminate the team’s hopes of making a push for the playoffs , but it is certainly a setback. The Baltimore Ravens now hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North at 4-1 and are favored on the road over the Browns in Week 6 , while the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, and Browns are all tied at 3-2. The division looks to be competitive this season, and any mistake or misstep could be the difference between winning the division and falling short. Cleveland takes on the Ravens in Week 6, so the game could shake up the current standings. FanDuel has the orange and brown among the lowest odds to make the playoffs in the AFC , despite their winning record, not exactly a glowing statement about expectations for Week 6 and beyond. The Browns will need to execute on offense to avoid putting their defense in a tough position against Baltimore’s talented offense. If Cleveland can get back on track in this game, they will still be considered a contender in the division. Let me know what you think in the comments – Does this loss affect the Browns’ ability to contend in the AFC North?

title: Cowboys news: Dallas could be squandering the best years of Dak Prescott
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have had some good fortune with Dak Prescott as their quarterback, but it hasn’t been nearly enough during the best seasons of his career. Joey Porter Jr. dove into why he didn’t play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and how much he could play versus the Green Bay Packers. Team owner Jerry […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have had some good fortune with Dak Prescott as their quarterback, but it hasn’t been nearly enough during the best seasons of his career. Joey Porter Jr. dove into why he didn’t play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and how much he could play versus the Green Bay Packers. Team owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer seem to have different ideas about where Christian Parker will call plays from now on, and the Cowboys also released some midweek injury updates. Are the Cowboys wasting prime years of Dak Prescott’s career? – Jon Machota, The Athletic The Cowboys have made five playoff appearances with Dak Prescott as their quarterback. Their lack of building consistently good rosters have resulted in a lack of postseason success. During Prescott’s first nine NFL seasons, the Cowboys were 76-46 when he started. Average that out over a 17-game season and that’s between 10 and 11 wins every year. It’s a record that basically means a playoff berth any time the franchise quarterback plays a full season. Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer since the start of last season, the Cowboys have had the 33-year-old Prescott for every start. They are 9-12-1. Certainly not good enough to even make the playoffs. Joey Porter Jr. explains sudden illness, hints at plan for him vs. Packers – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Joey Porter Jr. was abruptly sent home before th Cowboys played the Buccaneers last week. He speaks on what happened and what the outlook is for him in regards to playing time against the Packers. “I really just couldn’t hold anything down,” he told DallasCowboys.com on Wednesday, after returning to practice. “You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn’t hold in deep down. “So that’s when they made the call to send me home.” It certainly wasn’t for lack of effort that Porter missed the game. He took a nap to try and feel better after reporting to the team earlier in the day that he felt a little off, apparently then missing the team bus to the stadium and catching a rideshare to try and suit up. Cowboys haven’t used their best weapons consistently in 2026. That needs to change soon – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Dallas averages a lot of points per possession on offense. However, their struggles on defense have limited their ability to score even more. “You never want the defense on the field a lot,” Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark said. “Our job is to get off the field.” Therein lies the root of the Cowboys’ lack of offensive possessions. The Cowboys have been victimized often by long drives. The New York Giants set the tone for the season — and that game, notably — when they allowed a 10-play touchdown drive on their opening possession . That tone was echoed even louder when the Buccaneers, with an undrafted rookie quarterback, went on a 15-play scoring drive in last Thursday’s win over the Cowboys. That drive lasted 10 minutes and 58 seconds. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Brian Schottenheimer directly contradicts Jerry Jones on Dallas Cowboys’ plan with Christian Parker – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Jerry Jones said that defensive coordinator Christian Parker would call plays from the booth earlier this week. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer sung a different tune on Wednesday. Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones broke news earlier this week when he casually said defensive coordinator Christian Parker would move from the sidelines to the coaching booth moving forward. After mentioning it as an off-the-cuff comment, Jones was asked to confirm if he was saying Parker was moving to the booth. Jones said yes. Well, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is now publicly contradicting Jones. “None of those decisions have been finalized,” Schottenheimer told reporters on Wednesday. Cowboys injuries: DeMarvion Overshown, Cobie Durant DNP – LP Cruz, Blogging The Boys Dallas released injury updates on several players as they prepare for the Packers. Cowboys CeeDee Lamb (quadriceps) and Tyler Guyton (back) were full participants on Wednesday. DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) has been out since being injured in the season opener and did not practice. Cobie Durant (hamstring) was listed as a DNP, and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) was limited. Drew Shelton, Ameer Speed and Von Miller (rest) did not particpate.

title: Cowboys run game won last time at Lambeau, now is time to find it again
summary: After three games in 12 days, a pair of brutal losses and a gut-it-out win at the Houston Texans, the next Dallas Cowboys game on Sunday comes after a ten day rest. Unfortunately, even this break hasn’t felt long enough to forget about the most recent game from last Thursday night. Al Michaels called the […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images After three games in 12 days, a pair of brutal losses and a gut-it-out win at the Houston Texans, the next Dallas Cowboys game on Sunday comes after a ten day rest. Unfortunately, even this break hasn’t felt long enough to forget about the most recent game from last Thursday night. Al Michaels called the Cowboys home game against the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers a “can’t lose” game instead of a “must win”. Well, the Cowboys did lose in lackluster fashion, and now are approaching that “must win” territory so much earlier than we ever could have imagined for this 2026 season. The next opportunity to win comes back in primetime, at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers. The Cowboys only managed to throw a clunky tie in the record books between these historic franchises last season, but prior to that had lost 10 of the last 11 (including playoffs) to the Packers. That win did come on the road for Dallas though, all the way back in Dak Prescott’s rookie season of 2016. The Cowboys won their fifth straight game out of eleven in week six in Green Bay, 30-16. They would finish with 13 wins, still the high water mark of Prescott’s career, but go one and done in the playoffs in a rematch against the Packers at home in the Divisional round. That playoff loss to the Packers set the Cowboys back to where they were out of the playoffs the following season. The Cowboys also lost to the Packers in the 2023 Wild Card round, have yet to make the playoffs since, and will see their chances of doing so for a third season in a row plummet if they can’t get their first win against the Packers in a decade this Sunday night. Probably the most surprising thing happening to the 2026 Cowboys right now is the way going from Matt Eberflus to Christian Parker as defensive coordinator has not improved even the fundamentals of defense this team is playing through five games. The bar is incredibly low for Parker’s defense to have a better outing against the Packers compared to last year’s Eberflus experience, with the 40 points allowed through overtime being the second most surrendered that season (44 twice, to the Broncos and Lions, being the most). The Packers scored on every one of their second half and overtime possessions in last year’s primetime meeting. The Cowboys started the game offensively with three straight punts as well, and even though they turned a 13-0 deficit into a 16-13 halftime lead, managing only a field goal sealed their fate in overtime. Jordan Love’s last-second throw to the end zone for a chance at the win was knocked away by Jack Sanborn. The one second remaining after this defensive stand allowed the Packers to kick the tying 34-yard field goal as the overtime clock expired. Third down differential was a major problem for the Cowboys in this tie, going 4-11 on offense and allowing the Packers to convert 10-14. Last week, the Packers managed to beat the Bears 31-7 despite going 4-12 on third down, forcing the Bears in 14 attempts with the same four conversions. The Cowboys were 4-10 against the Buccaneers while surrendering 7-13 to an undrafted rookie quarterback. Carson Wentz and Michael Penix Jr. are the two quarterbacks to beat the Packers so far this year, while Matt LaFleur’s team’s wins have come against a Tyson Bagent led Bears team, Jalon Daniels in his first start for the Bucs, and the Geno Smith Jets. It stands to reason that Prescott will be the best quarterback the Jonathan Gannon coordinated Packers defense has faced this season. It also stands to reason that Cowboys fans are flat-out tired of trying to talk themselves into Prescott alone being enough to will this team to victory, certainly not with how many things are going wrong on both defense and special teams at the moment. The remedy for all of this could lie in the finer details of how Penix and the Falcons got a surprise Thursday night win at Lambeau, as well as the Vikings with Wentz at home in the season opener. Starting with the only team to win on the road at the Packers so far this year, the Falcons outrushed the Packers 242-17. They had 15 of their 25 total first downs come on the ground. Atlanta averaged 5.9 yards a rush, while the Packers only ran the ball nine times for 1.9 yards on average. Bijan Robinson went for 194 yards and scored twice while Brian Robinson also added a touchdown. The Vikings also leaned on a pair of running backs to control the game against the Packers, Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. Mason led the way with 59 yards on 15 carries and a score, while Jones had 40 yards on 12 carries also with a touchdown. Both teams averaged 3.1 yards a carry, but the Vikings outrushed the Packers 107-66 and went 4-4 in the red zone while holding the Packers to 1-4. The Packers got forced into another unfavorable run/pass split, having Love drop back 42 times compared to 21 runs. To tie this all back to where we started, that 2016 win for the Cowboys at the Packers, the run game had a strong influence as well. Rookie Ezekiel Elliott had a new career high in this game with 157 yards on 28 totes. Prescott was comfortable the entire game as a result, throwing for a gaudy 9.1 yards per attempt, racking up 247 yards, and three touchdowns. Dallas jumped ahead 20-6 and put Green Bay passer Aaron Rodgers in position to throw 42 times compared to 24 rushing attempts, the majority of which went to Eddie Lacy. Among the things that feel the absolute most fixable coming off the Buccaneers loss for the Cowboys, not running the ball enough has to top the list. The Cowboys came out and welcomed Tyler Smith back to the lineup at left guard by leaning on the run all the way for an opening drive Javonte Williams touchdown, but went away from this approach after the very first sign of the Bucs being able to control the ball themselves. To make matters worse, the Cowboys didn’t get the short passing game going as a response either until it was too late. The offense will need both to beat the Packers, and if nothing else cool down the hot seat underneath Brian Schottenheimer right now. The Jason Garrett comparisons for Schotty have not come favorably here in the early going of 2026, but right now things feel so desperate that getting the Garrett-esque team that won at Lambeau in 2016 would be a major win for Schotty’s team in ‘26. The Packers passing offense is going to like their matchup against the Cowboys secondary if they can build momentum and get on the field in as many neutral situations as possible. The Cowboys simply cannot forget about the run game this week, and doing so could let enough other things fall into place to bring hope back to this season at 3-3. The Dallas Cowboys are currently in the middle of a 3-game streak of primetime games. Last week was TNF, this week is SNF, next week is MNF. Last time the Cowboys had at least a 3-game streak of primetime games without a bye involved was in December of 2016. A decade ago. — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) October 14, 2026 To do so, the Cowboys are looking to hand the Packers their earliest second home loss since 2022. Their only losing season under LaFleur, Green Bay lost back to back games to the New York franchises in weeks five and six at home, the last loss coming on October 16th – two days before the Cowboys and Packers are set to battle for the 41st-ever time this weekend. Dallas is also looking to avoid back-to-back primetime losses for the first time since 2020, to the Arizona Cardinals and Philadelphia Eagles.

title: Improving this one area on offense could help a lot of Cowboys’ problems
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are a mess right now. Defensively they are just as bad as last year, if not worse, and offensively they currently aren’t playing up to their talent level. The good news is we’re only five games in the season was time to turn things around, but whether they’re capable of doing so […]
full_text: Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are a mess right now. Defensively they are just as bad as last year, if not worse, and offensively they currently aren’t playing up to their talent level. The good news is we’re only five games in the season was time to turn things around, but whether they’re capable of doing so remains to be seen. Surprisingly enough, the Cowboys most pressing issues can be helped by doing one simple thing better from here on out, running the ball. An improved rushing attack would have a positive ripple effect throughout the team, both offensively and defensively. And, there’s no reason to believe this isn’t easily accomplishable. As things stand right now, the Cowboys are only averaging 81.6 rushing yards per game, ranking a measly 30 th in the league. This is completely unacceptable considering Javonte Williams was one of the best running backs in the league last year, rushing for over 1,200+ yards and scoring double-digit touchdowns on the ground. Sadly, he’s only managed to rush for a total of 276 yards in the ground this year, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry. He has proven to have a nose for the end zone once again scoring six touchdowns in just five games so far this season, but is still unfortunately having difficulty finding consistency in the running game. It’s true some of his lack of production can be tied to game situations this season, however, that doesn’t change the fact this is an area that can be better by leaps and bounds. That’s especially true considering the offensive line is at their best as run blockers. Starting this week against the Green Bay Packers, establishing the running game early on should prove beneficial to the team as a whole. The Packers are currently allowing 127.6 rushing yards per game, ranking 24 th in the league. By rushing the ball more effectively the Cowboys not only can control the time position, but also keep their struggling defense off the field. This is a win-win for everyone. Brian Schottenheimer has been questionable as a play-caller all season, but an improved run game opens up the entire offense. Play-action suddenly becomes more effective as does opening up their lethal aerial attack. Defenses have to defend the entire field instead of pinning their ears back to rush the passer. Christian Parker’s defense also benefits by not having to be on the field so often. By playing less and staying fresher, they should hopefully be able to execute better. At the very least, the less they are on the field the less they can mess up. By controlling the game clock with a strong rushing attack, it kind of kills two birds with one stone. There’s still a lot of things the Cowboys need to clean up, but improving their rushing attack should be at the top of the list. It’s the easiest issue to fix right now that could have the biggest impact throughout the team. Hopefully it starts Sunday in the Week 6 matchup with Packers and continues throughout the rest of the season. It could be a true difference maker.

This came just a day after Brian Schottenheimer announced that Mike Pettine was joining the Cowboys’ defensive staff amid, um, some challenges that the team is facing. Coupling these two things (Pettine and the literal Parker move) together made it seem like the Cowboys were really focused on making some adjustments. Hold the phone, though. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer took to the podium himself on Wednesday and said that nothing has been decided. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer when asked about DC Christian Parker moving to the coaching booth during games, which Jerry Jones said yesterday would be happening: “None of those decisions have been finalized.” “There’s a good chance Christian is on the field.” “Christian… pic.twitter.com/VwSxPJaCTu — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) October 14, 2026 It is sort of rare to see anyone affiliated with the Cowboys, even the head coach, declare that something Jerry Jones said may have been wrong. Ultimatley, when Jerry Jones speaks it is usually pretty set in stone given who he is relative to the team. Schottenheimer publicly challenging that (so to speak) is rather bold. As things relate to Christian Parker though, obviously there is a lot of discussion surrounding him given the poor performance from the Cowboys as of late. Whether he is on the sideline or in the booth… the on-field product has to change.

title: The Cowboys have a horrible streak going right now
summary: It has been a long time since the Dallas Cowboys recorded an interception on defense. It may feel like the Cowboys are allergic to interceptions in a way never seen before, more on that in a moment, but they have had five-game streaks (what they have going at the moment) without interceptions before. Thanks to […]
full_text: Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images It has been a long time since the Dallas Cowboys recorded an interception on defense. It may feel like the Cowboys are allergic to interceptions in a way never seen before, more on that in a moment, but they have had five-game streaks (what they have going at the moment) without interceptions before. Thanks to resources like Stathead and Pro Football Reference we can measure this against all of franchise history, and I am sad to report that the findings are not great. This season is only five games long so the 2026 Cowboys have yet to celebrate catching a pass from an opposing quarterback. Did you know that this is the longest interception-less to start any Cowboys season ever? Before last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2026 Cowboys were merely tied with the 2008 and 2018 versions of the team that only went four games without a pick to start their seasons. Each of them broke through in game number five, though. Not this team. Odds would suggest that the Cowboys won’t get an interception in their next game based on all of this. Sunday night in a contest against Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers offers the next opportunity. Say the Cowboys fail to pick him off, though. If that is the case they will tie the longest single-season streak ever (so at any point, not just to start a season) without an interception. They have gotten to six on two occasions before, both in fairly recent memory. Honestly the most amazing takeaway from this particular group is that the 2016 Cowboys went undefeated in their six-game streak without any interceptions. That was a simpler time. Getting away from hypotheticals though, I saved the most sobering note for last. Again, sorry. While the Cowboys have a five-game streak going without any interceptions this season , they also ended last season on a three-game one. This means that overall they are currently riding an eight-game streak (again, dating back to last season) without recording one. That truly is unfathomable. This is the longest streak of such kind (combining seasons if necessary) in franchise history. This “title” was actually won after the Cowboys failed to pick off C.J. Stroud, apologies on the tardiness, but it really is insane to think that it has been so long since the defense got their hands on a pass adn caught it. Wouldn’t it be the greatest thing if the Cowboys got an interception on Sunday night and we could put all this to bed?

full_text: Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s time to play the blame game. The Dallas Cowboys 2026 season has not gotten off to the start fans wanted. At 2-3, the season isn’t over, but it certainly is headed in the wrong direction. There was plenty of optimism heading into the season. Jerry Jones had largely stayed out of the limelight and was willing to make deals. Brian Schottenheimer was being praised for his offensive performance in 2025 and his way of dealing with being the Cowboys head coach. Everyone was hyped about the acquisition of Christian Parker at defensive coordinator. And it was thought that the roster had gone through a definite upgrade. Now we look at those things and other thoughts come to mind. Did Jerry Jones just settle for Schottenheimer as head coach, so if you blame Schotty, you could blaming Jerry. He is also the general manager, so he’s responsible for the makeup of the roster. Or is Schottenheimer the one to blame, he is the head coach and all phases of the team are having their issues right now. Or was Christian Parker overvalued, to the point that they are bringing in outside help mid-season. His defense has cost the Cowboys games. Maybe in the end you blame the players. After all, they are the ones missing tackles, falling down in coverage, making dumb penalties and just failing to execute. Finally, there is the injury, schedule, miscellaneous category. title: Cowboys at Packers: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 6
summary: Just five weeks into the 2026 regular season, the Dallas Cowboys are at a crossroads. With a 2-3 record and matchups on the road against the Green Bay Packers and Philadelphia Eagles coming in the next two weeks, we are about to learn a lot about what this Cowboys team ultimately will be over the […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just five weeks into the 2026 regular season, the Dallas Cowboys are at a crossroads. With a 2-3 record and matchups on the road against the Green Bay Packers and Philadelphia Eagles coming in the next two weeks, we are about to learn a lot about what this Cowboys team ultimately will be over the next 12 days. After an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Thursday, Dallas certainly will need to shake some things up if they want to walk out of Lambeau with a win on Sunday night. With that thought in mind, here are two players the Cowboys should use more in Week 6. 1) CB Ameer Speed Of all the problem areas on the abysmal Cowboys’ defense, you could make a solid argument that Dallas’ secondary is the biggest cause for concern. Five games into the regular season, Dallas’ defense has the worst defense Dropback EPA (0.382) in the league while allowing the second-most NY/A (7.8). As a whole, the Cowboys’ cornerbacks have been extremely disappointing. Daron Bland has been borderline unplayable, while two guys who Dallas was betting to play a significant role, Cobie Durant and Shavon Revel Jr., have battled injuries and inconsistent play. Of all the corners on Dallas’ roster not named Joey Porter Jr., the guy who has arguably played the best is 27-year-old Ameer Speed. Speed signed with the Cowboys this past summer after playing with the Houston Gamblers in the UFL. The former sixth-round pick showed enough in training camp to make the 53-man roster and, to this point, has been extremely productive in limited opportunities. In 34 coverage snaps, Speed has allowed just two catches for a total of 28 yards. In the Cowboys’ last two matchups against the Houston Texans and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Speed has allowed just one reception for eight yards, to go with a 65 coverage grade, the best of any cornerback on Dallas’ roster over that two-game span. Another pack of Ameer Speed clips. Week 5 vs the Bucs. I said he was real good last week, but honestly I think he was even better this week. Bland getting a single snap over this guy is malpractice pic.twitter.com/whtIIaDoOY — Rob (DakshotSZN) (@GalacticRebirth) October 10, 2026 The Cowboys may have found an unsung hero at CB in someone NOBODY saw coming: Ameer Speed. Over the last 3 weeks, he’s played 34 coverage snaps and been targeted just twice, allowing 1 catch for 8 yards. The numbers are impressive, but the film is even better. Speed looks… pic.twitter.com/pRJ3ezIFcm — Bumi (@Bumi_mind) October 10, 2026 With how well Speed has been performing and their overall struggles at the position, the Cowboys absolutely must give him more opportunities against the Packers this week. Green Bay will test Dallas’ secondary and has two receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, who are consistent big-play threats. Dallas cannot afford to have any coverage busts this week and needs their stickiest corners on the field to attempt to slow down Green Bay’s passing attack. He may have been in the UFL less than a year ago, but Speed is without a doubt one of the Cowboys’ best cornerbacks at this point in time. They need to realize that and get him on the field often in Green Bay on Sunday. 2) OT Broderick Jones After bringing in former first-round pick Broderick Jones right before the start of the regular season, it seemed like the Cowboys were giving themselves some insurance in case starting right tackle Terence Steele got off to a bad start. Five games into the season, that very scenario has played out, and it’s time for Dallas to pull the trigger and make the switch. Steele has been bad in all facets this year. His pass-blocking (54.4) and run-blocking (51.8) grades are both below 55, and he has allowed seven pressures and five hurries in five games. Steele’s lack of success in run blocking has led to Dallas virtually being unable to run the ball to the right side. Starting running back Javonte Williams is averaging just 2.58 Y/A when running to the right side, as opposed to 5.32 Y/A when running to the left side. Steele has been the main reason for their lack of success running to the right, and his drop-off in run blocking, something he did fairly well each of the past two seasons, is a major cause for concern. Broderick Jones has not shown much throughout the course of his brief NFL career, but Steele has played so poorly that Dallas has no choice but to make the change. It’s clear Steele is the weak link on the Cowboys’ offensive line, and replacing him with Jones is at least a chance to improve their overall strength on the right side.

title: Cowboys Week 6 opponent: A look at the 2026 Green Bay Packers
summary: Green Bay enters Week 6 at 3-2 after dismantling the Chicago Bears 31-7, while Dallas sits at 2-3 following its debilitating 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. The Packers are coming off a performance in which Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns, Christian Watson delivered a pair of scoring receptions, and the defense […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images Green Bay enters Week 6 at 3-2 after dismantling the Chicago Bears 31-7, while Dallas sits at 2-3 following its debilitating 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. The Packers are coming off a performance in which Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns, Christian Watson delivered a pair of scoring receptions, and the defense forced five turnovers. The Cowboys have plenty of their own offensive firepower, but this matchup could come down to whether they can slow down Love and a Green Bay passing attack that looked particularly dangerous against Chicago. Here’s what Cowboys fans need to know about Green Bay heading into Week 6. Jordan Love is coming off his best game of the season Everything is coming up Jordan Love today ‼️ @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yzQQJ2IQ98 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Love has been productive throughout the first five weeks, but his performance against Chicago was a reminder of how dangerous he can be when the Packers’ passing game is clicking. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns, finishing with a 137.5 passer rating. He repeatedly attacked downfield, found receivers in space and took advantage of a Chicago defense that struggled to contain the Packers’ explosive plays. Through five games, Love has thrown for 1,408 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. His completion rate sits at 60.5%, and his 95.5 passer rating reflects a quarterback who has generally protected the football while producing big plays. Love’s deep-ball ability is especially concerning. Against Chicago, he completed six of eight passes thrown at least 20 yards downfield for 258 yards. When given time to throw, he has the arm strength and accuracy to turn a relatively ordinary drive into a scoring opportunity in a matter of seconds. Christian Watson could be a nightmare matchup If there is one Green Bay receiver Cowboys fans should be watching closely, it is Christian Watson. Watson is coming off a six-catch, 143-yard, two-touchdown performance against Chicago, including a 53-yard touchdown reception that helped put the game away. His first touchdown came on a 42-yard connection with Love, illustrating how quickly the Packers can produce explosive plays when their quarterback and receivers find their rhythm. JORDAN LOVE JUST THREW ONE OF THE MOST RIDICULOUS LASERS YOU WILL EVER SEE 60 YARDS IN THE AIR: CHRISTIAN WATSON AND MOSSED A CHICAGO DEFENDER FOR A RIDICULOUS TOUCHDOWN. HOLY FUCK… pic.twitter.com/pClF9N4uZY — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 11, 2026 Through five games, Watson has 26 receptions for 474 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 18.2 yards per catch. That average illustrates the problem he presents for opposing defenses: Watson can turn a routine completion into a major gain, and he has the speed to stretch the field vertically. Watson is not Green Bay’s only option, either. Matthew Golden had six catches for 123 yards against Chicago, while tight end Tucker Kraft remains another important target for Love. The Packers demonstrated that they can spread the ball around and punish a defense that commits too much attention to one receiver. Green Bay’s defense is creating turnovers The Packers’ defensive performance against Chicago showed why this matchup is about more than Love and Watson. Green Bay intercepted Chicago quarterbacks three times, including two interceptions by safety Xavier McKinney, and recovered two fumbles. The Packers finished with five takeaways and converted those turnovers into 15 points while keeping their own side of the ledger clean. Xavier McKinney intercepts it for the second time! @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/64InTW9DdB — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 That performance pushed Green Bay’s season total to seven interceptions through five games, alongside 14 sacks. McKinney is an important part of this Green Bay defense. His two interceptions against Chicago highlighted his ability to capitalize when opposing quarterbacks make mistakes, and the Packers have several other defenders capable of disrupting the passing game. Micah Parsons’ potential return against Dallas has been one of the more intriguing storylines surrounding this matchup before the season. Parsons tore his ACL in December 2025 and has been working through a lengthy rehabilitation. While initially having hope he could return against his own team, Parsons is not ready to begin practice this week, meaning he’ll miss the game. Green Bay has already demonstrated that it can generate sacks and turnovers without Parsons in the lineup. The irony is difficult to ignore. Dallas traded Parsons to Green Bay in 2025 and later acquired Rashan Gary from the Packers as part of its effort to rebuild its own pass rush. Five games into the season, Green Bay has been considerably more productive at creating negative plays. The Packers’ defense has shown that it can disrupt an opponent’s rhythm and turn mistakes into points. Dallas cannot afford to be careless with the football, particularly against a secondary that has made takeaways a central part of its early-season success. A trip to Lambeau brings plenty of Cowboys history The Cowboys and Packers have one of the NFL’s most recognizable rivalries, shaped by decades of memorable regular-season games and postseason meetings. The overall series has been competitive, but recent trips to Lambeau Field have generally been difficult for Dallas. The Cowboys’ last regular-season win at Lambeau came in October 2016, when rookie Dak Prescott and Dallas defeated Green Bay 30-16. More recently, the Packers have repeatedly been the team to deliver the most painful blows in this rivalry. Green Bay defeated Dallas 48-32 in the 2023 season’s wild-card beatdown. The Cowboys’ most recent regular-season meeting with Green Bay was a 40-40 tie in September 2025, in Arlington. Overall the Packers lead the all-time series against the Cowboys 22-17-1, and Dallas is 2-10 all-time at Lambeau. The historical context doesn’t decide Sunday’s game, but it does add another layer to a matchup in which Dallas needs to prove it can compete against one of the NFC’s more dangerous teams in a difficult road environment. The Packers are not invulnerable. Their offense had been inconsistent before the Chicago game, and they, like the Cowboys could still be looking for answers.

title: Broncos aim to topple defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks on Thursday Night Football
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos have a big test tonight when they battle the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. It’ll take a complete effort in all three phases to find a way to topple the defending Super Bowl champions. With a 3-2 record, the Broncos have fared decently through five games. They’ve […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Courtland Sutton #14 and Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrate a receiving touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos have a big test tonight when they battle the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . It’ll take a complete effort in all three phases to find a way to topple the defending Super Bowl champions. With a 3-2 record, the Broncos have fared decently through five games. They’ve played a lot of great opponents, and the Seahawks will be no exception. They’re a well-coached team, have a powerhouse defense, one of the NFL’s best wide receivers, and are performing well on special teams. One big question that looms large is this: Can Denver’s offense find a way to be consistent against a top-tier defense? The Seahawks are off to a great start defensively. They are the best in the NFL at creating turnovers with eleven thus far. Very few quarterbacks have success against them through the air—surrendering just 150 passing yards per game. Additionally, they’re a Top 3 unit on third downs and are allowing less than 30-percent of plays to be converted for a first down. This is an extremely tough matchup for the Broncos to get things right on offense. Head Coach Sean Payton recently spoke about what makes Seattle’s defense hard to prepare for and play against at a high level. “They’re complete in all three areas. In every statistical mark you look at, they have a real good front. They’re fantastic in their coverage fits. They defend the run well when they’re in their seven-and-a-half man fronts very well. You don’t see plays get on top of them. They have a real good pressure package. Mike Macdonald has done a real good job in, really, a short period of time, putting together a super-talented defense,” stated Payton. The margins for error are razor thin in every game. However, with a defense as formidable as the Seahawks, they are even slimmer. The Broncos can’t afford to put themselves in bad situations this evening. In many ways, Denver has been their own worst enemy to start their 2026 gridiron campaign. They’ve had a penchant for penalties and miscues which have derailed a lot of drives. And even though the defense has done a great job forcing turnovers, the Broncos are just +1 in turnover differential. They’ve thrown three interceptions and lost three fumbles on the season. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton knows that protecting the ball will be huge in order to find a way to grind out their fourth victory of the season. The longtime veteran noted it has been an emphasis of theirs during preparation on a short week. “They are a well-coached team. You can tell that they are very confident in their scheme. You can look on film, the teams that do a really good job of attacking the ball. Watching these guys, the way that they take the ball away, sitting in the zone, watching the quarterback, being able to break on the ball,” stated Sutton. “When you have those zone teams protecting the ball underneath, they want you to throw the ball underneath so they can have a chance to ride to the ball and punch the ball out. For us it’s ball security, even though it’s a short week, we preach and work to maintain really good ball security when we’re carrying it.” It won’t be easy, but it’s time for Denver’s offense to rise to the occasion. It would be nice see them put together a complete game on that side of the ball and be a primary reason why the team wins. Doing so against an elite Seahawks defense will be a monumental challenge. Can they rise to the occasion in front of a sellout crowd under the bright lights? We’re fixing to find out. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

Denver’s secondary will be out a few players which makes me wonder if they can limit Smith-Njigba’s impact. With Denver’s offense struggling, I don’t have much faith that Nix and the passing attack will turn things around against a Seahawks defense that is surrendering 150 yards per game through the air. – Chris Hart Seahawks 31, Broncos 17 We all see the issues with the Broncos. We know that the struggle is real for the offense. Now, the defending champs are coming to Denver and it could get ugly. With key pieces missing on defense, and Bo Nix looking like he has lost confidence, don’t expect much Thursday night. – Adam Malnati Broncos 24, Seahawks 23 This is one of those games where Nix and Denver find a way. And wearing g the throwback uniforms will give the Broncos a little extra magic on Thursday. The defense does just enough, and the offense does its thing late for the big Thursday night win. – Ian St. Clair What is your score prediction for the Broncos-Seahawks game? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: Broncos vs Seahawks preview: Denver looks for TNF win
summary: If not for an unfortunate injury, this likely would have been the Super Bowl matchup last February. Alas, it’s what we have for Thursday Night Football to start Week 6. For Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos (3-2), they’re coming off a win over the Los Angeles Chargers. For Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on during the second quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images If not for an unfortunate injury, this likely would have been the Super Bowl matchup last February. Alas, it’s what we have for Thursday Night Football to start Week 6. For Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos (3-2), they’re coming off a win over the Los Angeles Chargers. For Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks (3-2), they’re coming off a tough home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. It’s a clash of old AFC West divisional rivals who will also be rocking their throwbacks. For what it’s worth, the Broncos are unbeaten in their snot rocket-fueled sky blue and orange D beauties. Denver is a +2.5-point home underdog at FanDuel Sportsbook to the Seahawks. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Seattle : Seventeenth in total offense (328.0 yards per game), 17th in rushing offense (106.0 YPG), 16th in passing offense (222.0 YPG), eighth in scoring offense (26.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (269.0 yards per game), 25th in rushing offense (86.2 YPG), 25th in passing offense (182.8 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.4 points per game). Defensive Rankings Seattle : First in total defense (251.2 yards per game), 11 in rushing defense (100.4 YPG), first in passing defense (150.8 YPG), eighth in scoring defense (21.0 points per game). Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (347.4 yards per game), 29th in rushing defense (145.2 YPG), ninth in passing defense (202.2 YPG), 13th in scoring defense (22.2 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Thursday night’s game. Win the line of scrimmage on defense For a defense that is likely to be down the best cornerback in the NFL against arguably the best receiver in the NFL, the Broncos pass rush has to consistently harass, hit, and pressure Darnold. To be effective on Thursday night, the Broncos front is going to have to get home and do the job. If you want to take the big-play ability from Seattle, don’t give Darnold time and make him see ghosts. “Get home” also means Denver stopping the run. This is one helluva challenge for the Broncos, but winning the line of scrimmage on defense sets them up for victory. — Ian St. Clair Win the TOP battle The Broncos offense hasn’t done a great job controlling the clock. Against a team like Seattle, this will be a major key to the game. Keep the Seahawks defense on the field and limit the opportunities they will have on offense to generate a big play. — Tim Lynch Create turnovers For the Broncos to win this week, the defense will need to continue creating turnovers. The Seahawks, with JSN against a very banged-up secondary, are likely to generate a lot of offense. If the Broncos can take it away, they have a great shot at beating the champs. — Sadaraine Block For the love of all that is holy, be better on the offensive line. Watching the Chargers just get in the backfield for almost an entire game was really disheartening. The blame for all the offensive woes can be placed on Sean Payton, or Bo Nix, or a disappearing Courtland Sutton, or a juiceless J.K. Dobbins, but who is going to perform behind an o-line that has so much in common with a spaghetti strainer? It’s been bad. It could be disastrous against the defending Super Bowl champs. — Adam Malnati Score more points than Seattle Using deep analytics, I have come up with the foolproof way for the Broncos to improve to 4-2. They have a 3-0 record when outscoring their opponents and a 0-2 record when they do not. They are also undefeated when wearing their throwbacks. So, score more points than the Seahawks while wearing the throwbacks, and the Broncos will come away with the victory. — Scotty Payne Broncos have to be better on third down If teams can’t convert on third down, they usually lose the game. Last week was an exception for the Broncos, whose flurry of turnovers made up for their disastrous 1-of-12 performance on third down. The Seahawks boast the third-best defense in the NFL on third down, allowing just a 29-percent conversion rate on the season. Bo Nix and the entire offense must do significantly better in these situations to have a shot at winning in primetime. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Thursday night’s game?
