title: Scouting the Enemy: Seattle Seahawks
summary: The 2026 regular season rolls on for the Denver Broncos and so does their gauntlet schedule of opponents. On Thursday Night Football, the Broncos will host the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Here is a deeper look at their Week 6 opponent. 2025 Seattle Seahawks Season Review The Seattle Seahawks finished the 2025 regular […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Sam Darnold #14 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks look on against the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 regular season rolls on for the Denver Broncos and so does their gauntlet schedule of opponents. On Thursday Night Football, the Broncos will host the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Here is a deeper look at their Week 6 opponent. 2025 Seattle Seahawks Season Review The Seattle Seahawks finished the 2025 regular season as the NFC West champions with a 14-3 record. They had top 3 units on offense and defense and went on to defeat the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LX. 2026 Seattle Seahawks Offseason Additions and Departures When you win the Super Bowl, it’s hard to keep all your good players in the fold the following season. Seattle was no exception and lost a handful of quality contributors during the free agent period. Defensive backs Riq Woolen and Coby Bryant headed to the NFC in free agency earning big contracts, while edge rusher Boye Mafe signed with the Cincinnati Bengals. On offense, Kenneth Walker III, last year’s Super Bowl MVP, earned himself a huge payday from the Kansas City Chiefs and has revitalized their rushing attack. The Seahawks made some modest additions in free agency, but most of their remaining salary cap space was dedicated to extending defensive lineman Leonard Wililams, cornerback Devon Witherspoon, and edge rusher Derick Hall. The Seahawks had eight selections in the 2026 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, their top two picks are injured and most of their rookie class isn’t seeing any playing time. Rookie running back Jadarian Price suffered a chest injury in the third game of the year and is on injured reserve. Bud Clark, the tenacious TCU safety they selected in the second round, broke his ankle in the preseason versus the Tennessee Titans. Offensive X-Factor: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba In his fourth season with the Seahawks, wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has solidified himself as one of the best receivers in the National Football League. Heck, he might just be one of the best players in football. Smith-Njigba has posted back-to-back seasons of at least 100 catches. Last season, he won the Offensive Player of the Year honors after he reeled in 119 catches for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns. Five games into the season, and the former first-round pick is on pace to blow away those numbers. He already has 37 catches, 583 receiving yards, and 7 touchdowns. Of those 37 catches, 28 have resulted in a first down or a touchdown. Currently, he is averaging 117 yards per game receiving. Quite simply, Smith-Njigba has been dominant to start the season. He already has four games with at least 100 receiving yards. He is certainly the player the Broncos’ defense is going to have their hands full trying to limit the most—especially with multiple starters out in their secondary for the second straight week. Defensive X-Factor: Defensive lineman Byron Murphy The Seahawks boast one of the best defenses in the National Football League. They’re a top-flight unit against the pass, force a lot of turnovers, and limit big play ability when defending against the run. It’s hard to pinpoint a weak spot in their defensive lineup. Their defensive line is stout, they’re secondary is making a lot of plays, and their linebackers can cover a lot of ground. The Broncos haven’t performed that great in the trenches thus far. Thursday night’s primetime matchup will be another big test for them. One underrated player for Seattle is third year defensive lineman Byron Murphy . After a relatively quiet rookie season in 2024, the former Texas Longhorns standout started every game last season and put up 62 tackles, 7 tackles for loss, 7 sacks, and 13 quarterback hits. This year, Murphy is picking up where he left off. He already has 18 tackles, 5 tackles for loss, 5 quarterback hits, and 3 sacks. He is an ascending player and one of the best young interior defensive linemen in all of football. Denver’s interior offensive line is going to have their work cut out combating him and long-time veteran Leonard Williams. They are good against the run and the pass, so Denver’s guys up front better be prepared. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Seahawks I usually try to be optimistic about Denver’s chances most weeks. Alas, this gridiron matchup is one where I’m struggling to find ways for them to win. We all know the Broncos are struggling on offense. It would be a big leap of faith to believe they’ll get back on track against a defense that creates a lot of turnovers and limits big plays down the field. However, they may have a path if their defense can come up big like they did against the Los Angeles Chargers. Limiting Smith-Njigba will be their biggest test. Though quarterback Sam Darnold hasn’t played well since returning from injury and their run game is struggling. If the Broncos defense can force a few turnovers, that would give them a fighting chance. At the end of the day, I do expect the Seahawks to win. They’re just a tough draw at this juncture for the Broncos who can’t seem to figure out the right recipe for success offensively. Hart’s Prediction: Seahawks, 27, Broncos 17.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos vs. Seahawks: 3 Players to Watch in Week 6
summary: The stakes are high when the Denver Broncos host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. Finding a way to topple the defending Super Bowl champions is going to be extremely difficult. Here are three players that need to perform at a high level in order for Denver to earn their fourth victory of the […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The stakes are high when the Denver Broncos host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . Finding a way to topple the defending Super Bowl champions is going to be extremely difficult. Here are three players that need to perform at a high level in order for Denver to earn their fourth victory of the season. Riley Moss — Cornerback On a short week, it’s still uncertain if Riley Moss is going to play on Thursday Night Football . He has been limited in Denver’s practice sessions thus far. We will probably know much more sometime this afternoon in that respect. In the event he doesn’t, you can just throw in “Whoever is tasked with covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba” here instead. The Broncos have faced some really good offenses to start the season. In my mind, there is no doubt Smith-Njigba is the premier playmaker for the Seahawks on offense. He is the reigning Offensive Player of the Year. The star wide receiver already has four 100 receiving yard performances this season, seven touchdowns, and is on pace to shatter the career best numbers he put up last in 2025. Denver’s banged up secondary will be without Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga. That will make it even harder to limit Smith-Njigba’s impact. If Moss is a go, I expect most of that responsibility to be on his shoulders. The savvy wideout can beat you deep and he can create after the catch. He’s one of the most well-rounded receivers in the NFL. I’m very interested to see what kind of coverage plan Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph has in store to keep him from having a huge game. Jaylen Waddle — Wide Receiver The Broncos traded multiple premium picks to add Jaylen Waddle to their receiving corps. The hope was that the sixth-year wideout would be an impact player for the team and take their passing attack to new heights. Unfortunately, Waddle has been missing in action for most of the season. Outside of the Broncos’ Week 2 win versus the Jacksonville Jaguars where he had eight catches for 138 yards, the sixth-year wideout hasn’t made much of an impact. He has just 18 catches for 204 yards and 1 touchdown. Through five games, Waddle is sporting the worst catch percentage of his career at 58-percent. The Seahawks have been phenomenal shutting down opposing team’s passing attacks. Even so, this is a game where Waddle has to make an impact for the Broncos. They invested a lot of resources to acquire him, and the early returns aren’t too great. Can he rebound and be a difference maker in primetime? Denver will need that to happen to be victorious. Bo Nix — Quarterback It’s been a slow start to Bo Nix’s third season as the starting quarterback of the Broncos. I’m quite honestly surprised. I felt he was poised for a big jump in productivity and efficiency. Unfortunately, the results thus far aren’t great. In four of five games, Nix has thrown for less than 215 yards. Four of those contests have resulted in a completion percentage below at or below 60-percent. He has also had a turnover in four of five games. He has one of the worst EPA ranking for any quarterback in the NFL. The Seahawks sport a very good defense. They force turnovers, are fantastic on third down, and are allowing just 150 yards per game through the air. This will be a very tough game for Nix to get back on track. However, the Broncos desperately need a spark and much better play from their third-year signal caller. Can he hit some concepts over the middle of the field? Will he be able to find a few big plays down the field like he did often during the ’25 season? I have no idea if that transpires. If it does, I really like Denver’s chances of winning. Most importantly, I also think a good performance would give him a much-needed boost of confidence. I don’t expect an elite performance, but I want to see a good outing from Bo on Thursday Night Football .

title: Survey: Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact?
summary: Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and since the Lions are on a bye in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, we are shifting from our regular opponent-based question to a roster-focused […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) watches a drill after practice during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and since the Lions are on a bye in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, we are shifting from our regular opponent-based question to a roster-focused one. Here are our two questions for Lions fans this week: Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact? (weekly question) Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll) Our recurring “confidence the Lions are headed in the right direction” survey results hit an all-time low in the Dan Campbell era last week, plummeting to a meager 12%. However, after hanging 45 points on the Cardinals in Week 5 and the defense showing signs of improvement, it’ll be interesting to see if this survey rebounds this week. As for our new survey this week, the Lions are on the cusp of returning two key starters from injury in the next two weeks, as safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays have opened their 21-day evaluation windows and could return as soon as Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers, as Campbell noted last week: “They won’t have other teammates around, running plays and all that stuff, but they’re going to be here continuing to condition, get ready (during the bye week),” Campbell said on Friday. “As (much) football stuff as they can do without it being that with the training staff. Then let’s get them going Green Bay week. Let’s get them going, and then we’ll assess. Hopefully by midweek, we’ll have a pretty good idea (if they can return to play).” Note: Since we’re looking a bit ahead this week, the Lions Week 7 opening betting line against the Packers, set by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , is already at Lions -3.5 points and could shift if the Lions can return Branch and Mays. While each player’s return is still to be determined, our question this week hopes to uncover which Lions player returning from injury do fans think will have the most immediate impact? When Branch returns, he should jump directly into a starting role, creating a rippling effect on the Lions secondary. However, Achilles’ injuries are notoriously difficult to return to form from, and it could be a while before we see the Pro Bowl version of Branch that Lions fans have become accustomed to. Mays is also expected to step back into a starting role once he returns, but with Juice Scruggs playing well, might the Lions consider taking their time returning their prized free agent to play? We have also added an “other” option for fans this week, in case anyone believes another player expected to return from an injury list this year might be more impactful. The players eligible for this include safety Kerby Joseph, safety Thomas Harper, running back Isiah Pacheco, and offensive lineman Giovanni Manu, who was recently spotted at practice working with trainers. full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs into the end zone for a touchdown against Arizona Cardinals during the second half at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has been named the Week 5 NFC Offensive Player of the Week for the 2026 season. The honor comes after Gibbs rushed for 151 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for an additional 56 yards against the Arizona Cardinals. His output helped the Lions cruise to a 45-21 victory, leading Detroit to a 3-2 record into their bye week. This is the fourth time Gibbs has been named NFC Offensive Player of the Week. He had the honors twice last year and once in 2024. The only Lions running back to clear four Player of the Week honors is Barry Sanders (11 times). Beyond all the efficiency with the ball in his hands, Lions coach Dan Campbell praised Gibbs’ growth in pass protection this week. “I hit him up this morning. I said, ‘One of my favorite clips of everything you did’—he had a ton of eye-opening plays—’was his protection rep on the fourth-and-1, (Sam) LaPorta’s touchdown,’” Campbell said. “That was outstanding. And to me, that’s why he’s different. All this other stuff, of course he’s got that and it’s rare. It’s that. He’s unselfish and he’s tough and he’s willing to do anything for his teammates.” There goes Sam pic.twitter.com/jWOW1mJVFT — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 On Sunday, Gibbs also set an NFL record that he may put out of reach. Considering Gibbs won’t turn 25 until the end of the season, he is almost certainly going to create some distance by the end of the year.

title: Dan Miller reacts to outpouring of love from Detroit Lions fans
summary: On Sunday, Detroit Lions play-by-play announcer Dan Miller missed his first radio broadcast in 22 years following the death of his wife. Cynthia “Cindy” Miller passed away after a two-year battle with cancer. When the news dropped just before Detroit’s Week 5 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals, there was an outpouring of love from friends, […]
full_text: The WJR-AM broadcast team of Dan Miller (foreground), spotter Joe Abramson and Lomas Brown (background) on Sunday, September 20, 2020 call the action of the Detroit Lions game against the Green Bay Packers. The broadcast was done at Ford Field though the team was playing at Lambeau Field. Lions | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Sunday, Detroit Lions play-by-play announcer Dan Miller missed his first radio broadcast in 22 years following the death of his wife. Cynthia “Cindy” Miller passed away after a two-year battle with cancer. When the news dropped just before Detroit’s Week 5 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals, there was an outpouring of love from friends, family, the Lions organization, and fans who had connected with Dan through his passionate radio calls, thoughtful interviews with the team, and loving personality. Miller’s impact on the community was obvious after the game, too. Lions coach Dan Campbell and quarterback Jared Goff fought back tears to share just how much they were thinking of him and his family . And the Lions community raised more than $20,000 to support research for Leptomeningeal cancer, the one that took Cindy’s life way too soon. The Leptomeningeal Cancer Foundation received hundreds of donations of $45.21, matching the score of the Lions’ victory that day. Those donations will help the foundation create a virtual national tumor board, which will allow doctors and experts across the country to share cases, provide support, and educate both patients and clinicians. The hope is to make serious progress in treatment and finding cures. On Tuesday evening, Miller made his first public appearance since his wife’s death, calling in to FOX 2’s “The Sports Office” to show his gratitude for all the recent support and love. “I can’t express enough how much it has meant to me and my family, and how healing it has been to me and my family as we work our way through this,” Miller said. Miller talked about Cindy’s the two-year battle, and why support and research is so important for this rare condition. “It’s a terminal disease, it’s incurable, and you’re basically just trying to buy time,” Miller said. “We did buy some time. We were blessed to buy some time. But we knew we were going to lose her at some point, and we did. It’s a very rare form of cancer. It’s not one that a lot of people are familiar with, and it’s not one that a lot of people get. But it is one that we need to find some way to attack and find some better treatments for so that when people get it, they have a chance to extend life as long as possible.” Miller admitted he has wanted to craft some sort of expression of gratitude for the outpouring of love, but just couldn’t find the words. But, personally, I thought he said it beautifully on the show. “To see people respond like that has meant the world to us. And, honestly, not just the donations, but everybody that has reached out, everybody that has sent condolences, everybody that has sent—just saying they’re thinking about us, it means the world,” Miller said. “I’ve honestly tried to sit down and craft something on social media and I could never find the words. I could never find the appropriate tone. I could never find enough to cover my wife, our loss, her battle, the kindness of people, and just how it all meets at some point to the point where we’re at in our lives, and just how important they’ve been helping us get through these couple of days. “Look, I’m well acquainted with One Pride and Lions fans, and I’m well acquainted with sports fans in Detroit. But when you’re in the vortex of something that we’ve been in here, and you feel their kindness and it’s right there aimed at you and your family, words can’t express how much it means.” You can watch Miller’s entire segment on The Sports Office below: You can watch the full episode The Sports Office here, which features a segment with yours truly talking about Dan, our fundraising campaign, and some Lions football, as well. If you’d like to make a donation to the Leptomeningeal Cancer Foundation, you can do so here .

title: Lions mailbag: How much of a difference can Cade Mays, Brian Branch make?
summary: When the Detroit Lions return from the bye, they could have two very important pieces ready to make their 2026 debut. Center Cade Mays, the Lions’ prized offseason signing, appears close to returning from a fractured wrist suffered in training camp. Safety Brian Branch has been champing at the bit to get back on the […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 2: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch #32 enters the field prior to an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 2, 2025 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images When the Detroit Lions return from the bye, they could have two very important pieces ready to make their 2026 debut. Center Cade Mays, the Lions’ prized offseason signing, appears close to returning from a fractured wrist suffered in training camp. Safety Brian Branch has been champing at the bit to get back on the field after a torn Achilles ended his previous season in early December. The Lions could really use both players, but how will they use them, and how much of an impact can either make? That’s one of the main topics on this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast. But let’s get into it a little in this space. Starting with Mays, the Lions are faced with an interesting conundrum. Mays’ replacement, Juice Scruggs, has been playing at a pretty high level in his absence. PFF actually has him as the highest-graded center in football, although that doesn’t quite pass the eye test. Still, even coach Dan Campbell has praised Scruggs’ growth at the position over the past month. “I feel like Juice has gotten better playing center, just getting more comfortable, particularly on the road, silent count, making the IDs, all that,” Campbell said. So what do they do with Scruggs? Where does Mays provide an upgrade? Will the Lions have to worry about chemistry restarting with Mays in the lineup? Plus, there was one interesting thing that Campbell said about returning Mays to the lineup that may question the timing of his activation. “We’ve got to see exactly where he’s at. We’ve got basically two days of half practices with him and so let’s see what it looks like next week,” Campbell said. “He’s going to continue to train here and then we got to make a decision on how do we work this. That’s what’s a little unique, he plays center. It’s not like you’re rotating a guard. So how do we handle this? What’s the best way? Can he go 70 reps? So, there’s a lot of factors that go into it right now.” Does that mean we get one more week of Scruggs? Could the Lions hold off Mays’ return longer than expected? We discuss it all on this week’s pod. As for Branch, I don’t think there’s much question that Detroit wants him out there ASAP to help a struggling and beat-up safety room. Detroit hasn’t had much answers on the back end. Things got so dire that Detroit played fifth-round cornerback Keith Abney at safety last week—and it seemed to actually settle things down a bit. So what will that room like upon Branch’s return? Will Branch go back to his nickle/safety hybrid role, or do the Lions need so much help at the deep, single-high spot that they put Branch there? And who will be playing aside him? And how much of a difference can he truly make? We tackle those topics, plus: Are the Lions in a better spot at cornerback now? Why are the Lions still bad at third-down offense? Should the Lions be playing more young players on defense? (e.g. Derrick Moore) What’s with the slow starts on offense? What’s the diference between a good kick and punt returner? Who could win those jobs after Tom Kennedy’s injury? Catch this week’s episode on your favorite podcast platform by searching “Pride of Detroit” or just using the embedded Spotify player below. If you want even more Lions mailbag content, be sure to watch this week’s episode on our YouTube channel and/or Twitch page . There we have a bunch more between-segments content.

title: Checking in on former Detroit Lions players lost this offseason
summary: This offseason, the Detroit Lions made an unusual number of changes to their roster. With a tightening salary cap and a need to get younger, the Lions said goodbye to several players who had long been part of the organization. With the Lions on their bye week, we thought this would be a good chance […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 08: Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts following an interception during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 08, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images This offseason, the Detroit Lions made an unusual number of changes to their roster. With a tightening salary cap and a need to get younger, the Lions said goodbye to several players who had long been part of the organization. With the Lions on their bye week, we thought this would be a good chance to check in on those departed players and see how they’re doing with their new teams. RB David Montgomery New team: Texans Stats: 52 carries, 138 yards (2.7 YPC), 2 TDs; 7 catches, 67 yards, 1 TD PFF grade: 68.1 (20th out of 53) Montgomery is getting a bigger share of carries than he would’ve in Detroit (Woody Marks has 11 more carries than Montgomery at 149), but the efficiency numbers have fallen off a cliff. Montgomery’s 2.7 yards per carry is the lowest of his career by a full yard, and his 40.4% rushing success rate is also a career-low. Unfortunately, Montgomery suffered a groin injury last week and is considered week-to-week. WR Kalif Raymond New team: Bears Stats: 24 catches, 226 yards, 1 TD; 9 punt returns, 93 yards (10.3 avg.) PFF grade: 73.0 (34th out of 97) Raymond is already close to surpassing his yardage total from last year with the Lions (289) and is on pace for a career year. He has played in 62.4% of the Bears’ offensive snaps, which is his highest percentage since his first year in Detroit (71.4%). But his production has slowed down, catching five passes for 12 total yards in the last two games combined—albeit with a pair of backup quarterbacks. WR Greg Dortch New team: Bills Stats: 0 catches; 9 punt returns, 84 yards (9.3 avg.); 16 kick returns, 421 yards (26.3 avg.) PFF grade: 72.1 return grade (12th out of 70th) Dortch has only played in 11 snaps on offense, but he’s been a solid returner for the Bills—something the Lions could certainly use after the injury to Tom Kennedy. Dortch’s punt return average is below league average, but his kick return average is just above it. G Kayode Awosika New team: Chargers Stats: 2 starts PFF grade: 59.2 (44th out of 81) Awosika won the starting left guard job for the Chargers out of training camp, but has missed the last three games with a fibula injury. For what it’s worth, he’s currently graded higher than Lions’ reserve guard Ben Bartch (48.0). DT Roy Lopez New team: Cardinals Stats: 5 starts — 20 tackles, 1.0 sacks, 3 TFLs PFF grade: 71.3 (21st out of 140) As Lions fans saw a taste of on Sunday, Lopez continues to play strong football on the interior. He’s been a big reason why the Cardinals have a strong run defense, and he flashed some of his pass-rushing chops with his first sack of the season opposite Juice Scruggs. DT DJ Reader New team: Giants Stats: 5 starts—13 tackles PFF grade: 85.8 (2nd out of 140) Reader apparently still has it at age 32. He’s not only continued to be a strong run defender (77.4, fourth), but PFF is giving him an outstanding pass-rushing grade at 78.5 (eighth) despite producing only five pressures this year. Also interesting, despite having Reader playing at his best, the Giants run defense is giving up the second-highest yards per carry average (5.2) in the NFL. EDGE Al-Quadin Muhammad New team: Buccaneers Stats: 5 games, 2 starts — 4 tackles, 2 QB hits, 0.0 sacks PFF grade: 77.1 (24th out of 123) Muhammad’s standard stat sheet is quite bare, as he continues to look for his first sack of the season and only has four pressures through five games. However, PFF credits him with above-average scores in every phase of the game. EDGE Marcus Davenport New team: Bears (now retired) Stats: 1 game — 1 tackle PFF grade: 70.8 I felt compelled to add Davenport to this list, given he was considered a starter in Detroit. He made the Bears’ practice squad, got an elevation for a game, and announced his retirement from football last week. EDGE Tyrus Wheat New team: Cowboys Stats: 4 games — 3 tackles (14 defensive snaps, 67 special teams snaps) PFF grade: 61.9 PFF special teams grade After logging 215 special teams snaps for the Lions last year, Wheat remains a staple on the third phase of the game in Dallas. LB Alex Anzalone New team: Buccaneers Stats: 5 starts — 27 tackles, 1.0 sacks, 1 INT PFF grade: 41.1 (75 out of 76) Anzalone’s start to his Tampa career was a complete disaster, with fans calling for his benching after just two games. He’s since settled in a bit, and he helped the Bucs get their first win of the season on Thursday with a game-clinching interception. What has been particularly concerning about his play is missed tackles. He had four in the first two games of the season after tallying just eight all of last year. LB Grant Stuard New team: Rams Stats: 5 games — 2 tackles (0 defensive snaps, 99 special teams snaps) PFF grade: 66.9 special teams grade Stuard remains a four-core special teamer with the Rams, but has yet to find the field on defense. CB Amik Robertson New team: Commanders Stats: 5 starts — 33 tackles, 8 passes defended, 1 forced fumble PFF grade: 74.9 (13th out of 111) If there’s one player the Lions may regret letting go, it’s Robertson—who signed a lucrative two-year, $15 million contract with Washington this offseason. Robertson has been excellent, leading the league with eight passes defended. He’s allowed a passer rating of just 79.8 when targeted (17 catches on 31 targets for 158 yards and 1 TD). However, he does have five penalties on the season—second-most among all cornerbacks. He remains an elite run defender, producing an 87.3 grade in that phase —fifth-best among all cornerbacks. S Daniel Thomas New team: Browns Stats: 3 games (0 starts) — 4 tackles (0 defensive snaps, 64 special teams snaps) PFF grade: 69.8 special teams grade The Lions didn’t have room for Thomas after overhauling the safety room, but he’s been an effective special teamer in Cleveland Notable former Lions with no playing time QB Kyle Allen (Bills) TE Shane Zylstra (unsigned) OT Taylor Decker (unsigned) C Graham Glasgow (unsigned) EDGE Josh Paschal (unsigned) LB Zach Cunningham (unsigned)

title: Packers’ special teams show improvement under Cam Achord
summary: The Packers added two new coordinators this offseason, bringing on Jonathan Gannon as defensive coordinator to replace Jeff Hafley and hiring Cam Achord as special teams coordinator to fill Rich Bisaccia’s spot.  Gannon’s unit has largely been solid (though against a slate of subpar quarterbacks), but how have things been on special teams? It’s complicated. […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: wide receiver Skyy Moore #23 of the Green Bay Packers reacts to a successful challenge of a touchdown call against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers added two new coordinators this offseason, bringing on Jonathan Gannon as defensive coordinator to replace Jeff Hafley and hiring Cam Achord as special teams coordinator to fill Rich Bisaccia’s spot. Gannon’s unit has largely been solid (though against a slate of subpar quarterbacks), but how have things been on special teams? It’s complicated. At least, it’s complicated if you’re looking for a true one-to-one comparison with Rich Bisaccia. Our fearless leader Justis Mosqueda did a deep dive on Rich Bisaccia earlier this year and came away with a few broad conclusions. First, the Packers put themselves behind the eight ball when it comes to special teams, generally speaking, because of their “draft and develop” philosophy. They tend to draft players a couple of years ahead of when they’ll need them, stashing them as developmental prospects on the roster in the meantime. That leaves special teams units to be filled out by draft picks waiting their turn. Additionally, his study showed the Packers have historically only really cared about punt and kick coverage. They’re not worried about the return game, because to excel in the return game they’d have to sign a dedicated returner, which would snipe a roster spot that could otherwise be used on a draft pick waiting for a higher profile gig to open up. But this offseason, the Packers broke with their established mentality a bit. They signed Skyy Moore with the intention that he’d handle their punt and kick return duties, making it clear fairly early in training camp they anticipated he’d make the 53 man roster, which he did. And that has thrown the Packers’ numbers on special teams for a bit of a loop. For starters, the Packers currently rank second in the NFL in average punt return (15.5 yards per return) and are tied for eighth in average kickoff return (27.2 yards per return). The Packers’ punt return number is boosted by a 63-yard punt return by Moore in Week 2 against the New York Jets; Moore also had a 43-yard kickoff return in the same game. The Packers never ranked that high in punt returns under Bisaccia, and only beat that kick return ranking in 2022 and 2023, when Keisean Nixon was handling the job full-time. But it’s hard to bestow too much credit for that change on Achord, when we see the difference a quality return man can make. Invest in a good returner and you get good returns, it seems. As far as coverage goes, the Packers are handling things well on punts and not so well on kickoffs. They rank fifth in average punt return yards allowed (7.4), but 31st in average kickoff return yards allowed (30.1). Their kickoff ranking plummeted after they allowed a 61-yard return by the Bears on Sunday, and it’s worth noting that the Bears entered the game as one of the worst kick return teams in the league. Under Bisaccia, the Packers never ranked higher than 18th in punt coverage and never worse than 21st in kickoff coverage. By way of comparison, Bisaccia’s units were never as good as Achord’s in punt coverage and never worse than Achord’s in kickoff coverage. But to return to the original point about personnel, we have to factor that into Achord’s special teams rankings, too. Surely the Packers’ punt coverage is boosted by the fact that Daniel Whelan is, to put it mildly, kicking the crap out of the ball right now, not to mention the fact that certified special teams demon Nick Niemann has already racked up five tackles in the kicking game. Players matter! And it’s hard to say the Packers haven’t invested more in their players under Achord than they did under Bisaccia. The Packers have also been a bit less tolerant of special teams miscues this year than in the past, though admittedly we don’t have many firm examples. But after Jonathan Ford bore much of the blame for a blocked field goal in Week 3, he disappeared from the Packers’ field goal and PAT units, and has yet to play there again. So yes, in some ways, the Packers’ special teams have improved under Cam Achord, but it’s hard to tease out the difference that we can attribute to a new coordinator and what seems to be the result of a slightly altered roster approach. It’s a situation worth monitoring as the season wears on, though, and hopefully Skyy Moore returns from his tweaked ankle to continue to bolster the return units.

title: Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are eating up a ton of targets
summary: Through five games, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have been the engines of the Packers’ passing attack. Together, they’ve caught 50 passes for 871 yards and eight touchdowns, averaging 17.42 yards per catch as a duo. They’re truly a dynamic duo, and they’re producing in a way we haven’t seen in more than a decade. […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Christian Watson #9 of the Green Bay Packers catches a pass to score a touchdown during the first quarter of the NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through five games, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have been the engines of the Packers’ passing attack. Together, they’ve caught 50 passes for 871 yards and eight touchdowns, averaging 17.42 yards per catch as a duo. They’re truly a dynamic duo, and they’re producing in a way we haven’t seen in more than a decade. Watson and Golden are putting up such big numbers in the passing game because they’re getting the lion’s share of the targets. Golden leads the Packers with 44 targets so far this season, while Watson isn’t far behind with 40. Tucker Kraft, incidentally, is third with 29. Golden and Watson have accounted for 24.3% and 22.1% of the Packers’ targets, respectively, so far, the first time since 2014 that two Packers players have received more than 20% of the team’s targeted throws in a given season. That year, Jordy Nelson and Randall Cobb hauled in 28.4% and 23.9% of the Packers’ targeted passes en route to dual 1000-yard seasons. But that’s the last time it happened, and a pair of Packers’ receivers has only come close one other time. You’d probably guess that Davante Adams regularly received over 20% of the Packers’ receiving targets, and you’d be right. During the “all Davante, all the time” period of the Packers’ passing offense, Adams surpassed the 20% threshold in five consecutive seasons (2017-21), but only once did he have a comparably productive running mate. In 2016, fresh off a torn ACL, Jordy Nelson posted a 19.7% target share, falling short of 20% by literally two targets. It does paint the Packers’ passing attack as a bit top heavy, but what else would you do? Watson and Golden are almost literally always open. You might as well keep putting it up there for them. One may fade as Tucker Kraft continues to get his feet under him post-ACL, but until then, Golden and Watson will continue to get targets at a rate that we haven’t seen in quite some time.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Defense is doing the job so far
summary: Two things are simultaneously true about the Packers’ defense: they really haven’t played a decent quarterback yet this year, and they’re doing about as well as could be expected, given the circumstances. It’s absolutely true the Packers haven’t played any significant quarterbacks this year. They’ve faced backups in three of their five games so far, […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates after a play during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two things are simultaneously true about the Packers’ defense: they really haven’t played a decent quarterback yet this year, and they’re doing about as well as could be expected, given the circumstances. It’s absolutely true the Packers haven’t played any significant quarterbacks this year. They’ve faced backups in three of their five games so far, and the two starters they played were Geno Smith (not playing his best ball) and Michael Penix Jr. (in his first game back from a torn ACL). In a quarterback driven league, the Packers haven’t faced any opponents with anyone interesting in the opposing driver’s seat. But it’s also true the Packers have largely taken care of business against those backups. The scoreboard hasn’t always reflected it, but that’s mostly been for circumstances out of their control. The Packers’ offense handed the defense consecutive short fields against the Vikings (while the officials handed the Vikings an entire drive). And against the Falcons, the offense hardly saw fit to stay on the field at all, leaving the defense to absorb body blow after body blow from the all-Robinson Falcons backfield. Outside of that, though, they’ve shut down the Jets, Buccaneers, and Bears. Again, you have the backup quarterback caveat, but what are they supposed to do? I doubt Jonathan Gannon was sitting at home on Sunday night saying “Gosh, I wish the Bears had been able to play their preferred quarterback.” You can only play who you play, and the Packers have put together some good performances on defense against those opponents. This week we’ll start to find out what parts of their defense are for real. And given who the Cowboys are rolling out at wide receiver, we’d better hope part of the real stuff is in the secondary. title: Packers Film Room: Attacking after an interception
summary: If you watch football for any amount of time, you have no doubt heard the same talking points repeated hundreds of times. Thousands of times. An ocean of times, spreading out over the vast and speckled horizon. Some of those things are good, some of them are bad, and some simply roll off your back […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden (0) catches a pass against Chicago Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson (1) during their football game at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you watch football for any amount of time, you have no doubt heard the same talking points repeated hundreds of times. Thousands of times. An ocean of times, spreading out over the vast and speckled horizon. Some of those things are good, some of them are bad, and some simply roll off your back and find a nice home somewhere outside of your mind. One of those things is this: “after forcing a turnover, the offense should take a deep shot.” While it’s not something you can do every time, it is something that you can have success with, and it’s something you’ll see coaches looking to do. Whether it’s a straight deep shot or a trick play, you’re trying to catch the defense on the first play of the series when they’re not expecting to be out there. Maybe they were in the middle of sitting down with a coach to look at the last possession. Maybe they were in the middle of drinking a Gatorade and are now cursing their QB for making their rest so short. The thinking is that maybe you can catch a defense that is not quite as focused as they could be. It’s something the Packers took to heart in their Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears and had some nice success with. While the Packers had 5 turnovers on the day, I’m only going to look at the plays following the 3 interceptions, as the score was 31-7 midway through the 4th quarter when the first of two fumbles occurred. Play 1: 1st & 10, 5:32 remaining in the 1st quarter The Packers are up 7-0 when Tyson Bagent throws a pass to Luther Burden that is tipped up by Javon Bullard and intercepted by Xavier McKinney: That sets the Packers up at the Bears 45 yard line. This is the least aggressive of the calls, but they’re still looking to push it with the primary concept. The Packers are in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR). They shift to a balanced formation (an in-line TE to each side, a WR split wide to each side, the RB aligned directly behind the QB). They’re running deep curls off play action against a two-high look. It’s a good call against that defense, but the Bears linebackers are dropping back deep, taking those away. With the linebackers dropping that deep, Jordan Love [10] takes the checkdown to MarShawn Lloyd [32] under the linebackers. Not much, but 6 yards is 6 yards. Play 2: 1st & 10, 00:34 remaining in the 3rd quarter The Packers are up 23-7 when Tyson Bagent throws to Colston Loveland and is, once again, intercepted by Xavier McKinney. McKinney is initially dropping down to pick up the motion TE, but, when that man stays back to block, he drops back to the middle, reads Bagent’s eyes and jumps the throw. That sets the Packers up at their own 45 yard line. Once again, they come out in 12 personnel in a balanced formation, but this time they’re looking to drive the ball downfield. Love sees something pre-snap and he Cans the call to a variant of High Cross. It looks like Matthew Golden [0] and Christian Watson [9] are going to be running deep over routes, crossing each other in the middle of the field. Instead, they both reverse course and break back to their respective sidelines. Watson gets a little tied up in his route, but Golden does a nice job at creating separation off the line, keeping that separation down the field and breaking back outside over the defender. Golden really shows his speed here: he gives up quite a bit of ground to the inside on the release, but he’s able to burn up that distance throughout the route and create late separation as he breaks back outside. With the single high safety breaking to the middle of the field, Golden has a lot of room to work back outside to. Love lays it up to the outside. Instead of tracking the ball to his outside shoulder (and potentially giving the safety a chance to knock it free), Golden jumps up and twists back to high-point the ball. 36 yard gain. Play 3: 1st & 10, 12:49 remaining in the 4th quarter The Packers are up 31-7 when Case Keenum throws to Rome Odunze in the red zone and is intercepted by Ty’Ron Hopper. Hopper returns it 19 yards, setting the Packers up on their own 19. Once again, the Packers are looking to push it. They trot out Yankee, a two-man concept that has a receiver from one side (Watson) running a deep over route and the receiver from the other side of the formation (Golden) running a deep post route. The Packers are in 12 personnel and shift to a balanced formation. The Bears are in a single-high look and Love is reading the single-high safety. That safety drops down to pick up Watson on the crosser, giving Golden inside leverage on his man. So Love chucks deep to Golden. The defender from the other side is looking to fall under this route as soon as Watson is passed off to the safety in the middle (good communication there), but the throw is far and Golden is fast. Once again, Golden goes up for the ball and comes down with a 50 yard catch (in front of a tumbling ref). Here’s what Jordan Love did on the play immediately following an interception by the defense: 3/3 for 92 yards (30.7 YPA). Not too shabby. title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 6
summary: Finally, with great mercy and grace, the Houston Texans shook off the burden of a rough start and began their ascent back to an even record with a convincing, 26-3 victory over the hapless Tennessee Titans. The hot hand of QB CJ Stroud delivered the Texans from their worst start since 2005,  targeting six different […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 11: Woody Marks #4 of the Houston Texans rushes for yards during the first quarter of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Finally, with great mercy and grace, the Houston Texans shook off the burden of a rough start and began their ascent back to an even record with a convincing, 26-3 victory over the hapless Tennessee Titans. The hot hand of QB CJ Stroud delivered the Texans from their worst start since 2005, targeting six different receivers four or more times and accounting for 261 passing yards and two touchdowns. Likewise, the DE combination of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter was on fire most of the day, showcasing Houston’s first extended stretch of complementary football in 2026. Anderson and Hunter combined for four sacks, five QB hits, four TFLs, seven combined tackles, and one tipped pass that resulted in the first interception of Texans LB Jake Hansen’s career! Cam Ward intercepted by Jake Hansen ‼️ @HOUvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z4wwcwNZEt — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 It took a full month of regular season action, but the Texans have finally gotten back on track, and did so against the same division-rival that christened their 12-2 run last year! Now, the Texans still have a long way to go before anything like that happens this year, but following this big win, head coach DeMeco Ryans made an announcement making it clear the team was all-in on a comeback in 2026: the Texans were trading for Arizona Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr.: #Texans HC Demeco Ryans walked off at his presser: “You guys want to know, huh?” Yes, we traded for Marvin Harrison.” See ya! EPIC. https://t.co/D60u1qNgdD pic.twitter.com/p16VkjvA9P — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 11, 2026 🚨 🚨 🚨 The Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr to the Texans in a blockbuster, per me and Adam Schefter.It’s Harrison and a 7th rounder to Houston for a 2nd rounder this year and a 6th rounder. — Ian Rapoport (@rapsheet.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T20:33:53.223Z This is huge news for a team that entered 2026 with Super Bowl aspirations and isn’t ready to bail on them quite yet. A former fourth-overall pick out of Ohio State in 2024, Harrison arrives in Houston looking to rekindle the connection he and CJ Stroud shared in college together. He and Stroud dominated college football in 2022, and if a reunion can get Harrison Jr. back to his rookie form, the Texans could be in store for their best offense of the Stroud/Ryans era! Finally, there’s some good news surrounding the Houston Texans. This victory and the Harrison Jr. trade – even if you’re disappointed with the move – give us something to look forward to in Houston’s upcoming game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. It’s like a ray of sunshine after a full month of dreary, messy…poorly blocked weather. What will all of this mean for their position on the power rankings, though? Will this positive momentum send the Texans bouncing up the rankings, or will the pundits remain bearish on a 1-4 franchise? Well, let’s find out! Here’s where the Houston Texans are ranked following their 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans: NFL.COM : 25. Houston Texans (1-4) (Last Week: 23) Houston did what everyone expected it to do: take care of business against the worst team in the NFL. C.J. Stroud added another fruitful week to what is quickly becoming a very strong rebound season, the Texans finally got a little bit more out of their ground game (despite losing David Montgomery to injury), and the superior AFC South team walked away with an easy win . It’s a start, and we’ll see what becomes of the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade , but it’s going to be a long climb out of 0-4. – Nick Shook ESPN: 21. Houston Texans (1-4) Week 5 result: Beat the Titans 26-3 Week 5 ranking: 24 Biggest issue on defense: Health at all three levels The Texans have dealt with injuries to key players. Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair sat out time because of a groin injury. Nickelback Jalen Pitre just sustained a shoulder injury against the Titans, defensive tackle Kayden McDonald was on IR because of a quad injury to start the season, and linebacker Henry To’oTo’o landed on IR after Week 1 because of a shoulder injury . That has factored into their defense giving up 234 passing yards per game (23rd). Overall, Houston is tied for 15th in scoring defense (22.4 per game) after ranking second last season (17.4). – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 14. Houston Texans (1–4) Last week’s ranking: No. 20 Last week’s result: beat Titans, 26–3 This week: vs. Jaguars (London) My column on the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade . Something tells me this is going to be a fleecing for the Texans. But either way, there will be one clear winner. – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 26. Houston Texans Last Week: 28 Week 5 Result: Won at Tennessee 26-3 Don’t write off the Houston Texans yet. Yes, they should’ve beaten the winless Tennessee Titans, and no, Marvin Harrison Jr. isn’t the savior who’ll turn the offense into a juggernaut. However, if the Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London this week, they’ll be 2-4, like last season before winning 10 of 11 games. It’s a tough feat, but Houston did it with mostly the same players from the previous campaign. It’s not time to jump back on the Texans bandwagon, but a win over the division-leading Jaguars could spark a season turnaround. – Maurice Moton CBS SPORTS: 23. Texans (1-4) (Last Week: 26) The offense with C.J. Stroud has been playing good football. The change to DeMeco Ryans calling plays seemed to work as they ready to play a big game this week with Jacksonville. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 26. Houston Texans (27): Just noting DE Will Anderson Jr. is on pace for 25½ sacks, which would break Garrett’s nine-month-old record. Of course, Anderson couldn’t have expected his Texans to be as bad as Garrett’s Browns were. – Nate Davis YAHOO! SPORTS: 24. Houston Texans (1-4, LW: 26) Beating the Titans this season doesn’t mean a whole lot. But at least the Texans looked good doing it. Their defense gave up a 58-yard drive and a field goal on Tennessee’s first possession of the game. The rest of the day, the Texans allowed no points, 129 yards and no drive longer than 27 yards. C.J. Stroud played well, and while the running game still lagged at 2.9 yards per carry, it was good enough on offense. The next question is whether Marvin Harrison Jr. can help the offense. The Texans must think so considering they sent a second- and seventh-round pick to Arizona for Harrison and a sixth-round pick. They need some punch in the offense. It’s questionable if Harrison can come in and be an impact player in the middle of the season after having just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown for Arizona in 2026. It’s tough for any receiver to learn an offense and establish chemistry with a quarterback during a season. However, if it works it could transform Houston’s offense. That’s the Texans’ gamble. – Frank Schwab THE ATHLETIC: 21. Houston Texans (1-4) Last week: 24 Sunday: Beat Titans 26-3 Who have you beaten? Titans Finally, some positive vibes in Houston! title: Not just Big Q: Colts have another standout offensive guard playing some elite ball
summary: We’re always searching for silver linings as the Indianapolis Colts sit at 2-3, but look closer to approaching a full blown rebuild than realistically contending for a Super Bowl title anytime soon. One of them is regarding the standout play so far of starting offensive lineman Matt Goncalves, the 3rd-year pro who just began his […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - JANUARY 04: Matt Goncalves #71 of the Indianapolis Colts steps up to block during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re always searching for silver linings as the Indianapolis Colts sit at 2-3, but look closer to approaching a full blown rebuild than realistically contending for a Super Bowl title anytime soon. One of them is regarding the standout play so far of starting offensive lineman Matt Goncalves, the 3rd-year pro who just began his second season as a full-time starter at right guard due to positional necessity. The former 2024 Colts’ 3rd round pick out of Pitt is blossoming into one of the better young starting offensive guards in all of football right before our very own eyes this 2026 season. While there was consensus concern among Colts fans that allowing breakout starting right guard Will Fries, who Indianapolis will face in two weeks, to leave in free agency to the Minnesota Vikings in the 2025 offseason, would prove to be a critical mistake in hindsight, Goncalves appears to have sufficiently filled those rather large shoes. Per PFF, Goncalves is their 12th best graded offensive guard with a +75.9 overall grade through 5 starts in the 2026 campaign. Specifically, he’s allowed just a sack and 3 total QB pressures so far in 195 total pass blocking snaps. His allowed pass pressure rate (5.7%) is among the best at his starting right guard position. If this keeps up, the big man, approaching 320 pounds, can chug as many footballs as he wants in celebration!

title: Jaguars Reacts Survey: Do you trust Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. The Jacksonville Jaguars were among the NFL’s least-injured teams through the first month of the 2026 season. Unfortunately, they were finally dealt a poor hand in […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Cole Van Lanen and Walker Little of the Jacksonville Jaguars come out of the tunnel before the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. The Jacksonville Jaguars were among the NFL’s least-injured teams through the first month of the 2026 season. Unfortunately, they were finally dealt a poor hand in Week 5. Long snapper Ross Matiscik and left tackle Anton Harrison each exited Jacksonville’s game against Philadelphia. Matiscik (shoulder) seems to have avoided injured reserve, and until he returns, the Jaguars will find a short-term replacement to relieve nose tackle DaVon Hamilton of his emergency duties. But Harrison (knee) sustained a non-contact injury that has already landed him on the IR list. We won’t know the extent of his absence until after he undergoes arthroscopic surgery . Hopefully, Harrison will return in time for the playoffs, but that’s no guarantee. Either way, losing a starting lineman is never ideal. The Jaguars will promote Walker Little to left tackle, where he’s played in 31 of his 39 career starts. Cole Van Lanen will continue to start at right tackle, though he’s been pretty shaky coming off his December 2025 knee surgery. “I have a lot of confidence in Walker and Cole to go in there,” head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday. “These guys have played [the Houston Texans] so many times and have had success against them and know what they’re in for in terms of the battle and next man up mentality.” “Anytime you’re playing good rushers, you got to have a plan. It takes all 11. It’s not just those tackles. It’s having a plan in the chip game. It’s having decision, timing, accuracy getting the ball out, having a plan. It takes a village. It’s not just really about one guy. That’s kind of on all of us.” It will certainly take a village to contain DPOY frontrunner Will Anderson Jr. and the rest of Houston’s pass rush in Week 6. As much as the Jaguars need good performances from Little and Van Lanen, it’s almost as important that they just stay healthy… because another loss to the OT room could truly be devastating. How confident are you that Little and Van Lanen can hold up over the next few months in Harrison’s absence? Are you confident in Little and Van Lanen? Are you confident in the Jaguars? title: 5 Questions with Battle Red Blog: Making Sense of the Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
summary: As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Houston Texans in Week 6, we exchanged questions with Scott Barzilla of Battle Red Blog to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Texans spent a second-round pick to reunite Marvin Harrison Jr. with his college quarterback. Does Houston’s current record (1-4) or Harrison’s past […]
full_text: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 19: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 and C.J. Stroud #7 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrate a victory against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium on November 19, 2022 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Houston Texans in Week 6, we exchanged questions with Scott Barzilla of Battle Red Blog to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Texans spent a second-round pick to reunite Marvin Harrison Jr. with his college quarterback. Does Houston’s current record (1-4) or Harrison’s past inefficiencies (53.5% career catch rate) make you question the move? Or do you appreciate the urgency from GM Nick Caserio to compete for Super Bowls right now? No, I definitely question the move on multiple fronts. Even if we assume Harrison is the Harrison from OSU, then we’d have to question whether you are a WR away. I’d argue that running back, offensive line, and linebacker are more pressing needs right now. I suppose the biggest hope is that Harrison was bad because Arizona was a horrible situation and not because he’s not as good as what was advertised. I appreciate the urgency but I wish it had been applied at another position. Question 2: What is your biggest gripe with Houston’s coaches at the moment? Is it playcalling? The overall schematic system? Questionable in-game decisions? Where do they have to improve for Houston’s record to improve? On the offensive side of the ball, it is scheme and playcalling. Juice Scruggs was all but cut because he wasn’t going to make the team. He is now the No. 1 graded center in football in Detroit. Clearly it’s not a talent problem. It’s a scheme and playcalling problem. On defense, I think it’s more a player issue. There have been key moments in games where players made plays that just haven’t been made. Kamari Lassiter is the biggest culprit there, dropping an easy INT in Week 1 that would have sealed the game. You change two or three plays and this is a 3-2 football team right now. Question 3: Do you have more confidence in the defense being an elite unit, or the offense being a “good enough” unit? I think the offense on paper is already good enough. They’ve scored 25 or more points in three of the five games. They just haven’t been able to match a good offensive week with a good defensive week until Week 5. I think the defense will continue to be good but they’ve been bitten by the injury bug on their linebacking core and that hurts them in the middle of their defense. They will usually be good but might not ever get back to great. Question 4: Who are some under-the-radar players that Jaguars fans should know of before Sunday’s kickoff? title: Patrick Mahomes sees how the Chiefs’ offense can take it to the next level
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs enter Week 6 undefeated, with one of the NFL’s top offenses. The Chiefs rank fifth in points per game (29.5) and second in total yards (412), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes seems to have found his groove. He has thrown nine touchdowns and thrown just two interceptions in four games, averaging 8.1 […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs enter Week 6 undefeated, with one of the NFL’s top offenses. The Chiefs rank fifth in points per game (29.5) and second in total yards (412), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes seems to have found his groove. He has thrown nine touchdowns and thrown just two interceptions in four games, averaging 8.1 yards per pass attempt. Kansas City always self-evaluates over the bye, and no player is likely to do it more than Mahomes. The self-critical MVP sees where he and the offense can improve over the remaining 13 regular-season games. He spoke to local media Wednesday before practice, pointing to himself first as the area that can improve starting in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting the ball out faster “Continue to hit the deep shots when they’re there, but then when it’s not there, maybe get the ball out of my hand a little bit quicker,” Mahomes said. “Get it to guys where I’m not taking some of those hits.” In the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , the Chiefs surrendered two sacks and eight quarterback hits. The team was dealing with a significant change on the offensive line—veteran backup Mike Caliendo filling in at left guard next to undrafted rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson—but Mahomes understood what he could have done to reduce the hits he took. “In the Raiders game, I feel like there were times I was holding onto the ball a little longer than I had in the previous games,” Mahomes reflected. ”So being better at that: just keep getting it out of my hand like I was in the earlier games in the season and not getting into some old, bad habits.” Patrick Mahomes says he didn’t go a week without getting tackled. Says his son Bronze is really into tackling right now. #chiefskingdom pic.twitter.com/WjCBEYSRej — McKenzie Nelson (@McKenzieMNelson) October 14, 2026 So far this season, Mahomes has the sixth-fastest time to throw (2.7) among qualified NFL quarterbacks according to NFL Next Gen Stats . In Las Vegas, the quarterback’s average time to throw was a season-high 3.04 seconds. Finding more consistency It will be a challenge for the Chiefs’ offense to “continue to hit deep shots” without its No. 1 big-play receiver: Tyquan Thornton. He suffered a serious ankle injury that is expected to sideline him for the season. Still, the top factor in Mahomes’ mind will be finding a rhythm and staying in it for all four quarters. “The biggest thing is about being more consistent throughout the game,” Mahomes said. “There have been spells in each game where we necessarily haven’t played our best football. Having those explosive plays helps out a ton, so we have to continue that and then be more consistent throughout the entire game. That will kind of take us to the next level.” To avoid droughts and three-and-outs, Mahomes understands the team needs to keep leaning on running back Kenneth Walker, who still has the second-most rushing yards (537) in the NFL after the bye week. He has understood that since before Chiefs Kingdom saw how special Walker could be. “It was easy once I saw Kenneth running the football,” Mahomes reflected about the offseason. “I was like, ‘We have to make sure we give him the best chances to succeed.’” “Obviously, he has run the ball terrific under center, and the offensive line has taken it upon themselves to fire off the ball and get that stuff down,” Mahomes continued. “I knew if we were able to do that, the play action game would open up even more. Then it’s about me just being the best quarterback for this team. It’s always going to be different, and this team was about being under center, getting him going and then play action off of it. I’m sure the defenses will adjust, and we’ll adjust off of that as well.” Mahomes says this year’s Chiefs are “about being under center,” and that theme has been successful. No team averaged more yards per play than Kansas City (7.3) does on under-center plays this season. Still, Mahomes leaves plenty of room for self-improvement, and he believes there’s another level of effectiveness Kansas City’s offense can reach as he and the unit move forward. “I have to be more consistent getting the ball out of my hand,” Mahomes said. “I have to be more consistent going through my reads and getting to the right progressions, but guys are getting open. I think that’s the most important thing, and as I get more and more comfortable getting back at it, I can start getting through those progressions and hitting those guys. If we can take that consistency to another level, I think the offense will even take another step.”

title: Chiefs’ Josh Simmons to practice for the first time this season
summary: During his Wednesday press conference ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 6 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, head coach Andy Reid shared a major injury update: left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) will return to the practice field for the first time since training camp. Reid shared that wide receiver Rashee Rice (Hamstring) would be the […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images During his Wednesday press conference ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 6 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers , head coach Andy Reid shared a major injury update: left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) will return to the practice field for the first time since training camp. Reid shared that wide receiver Rashee Rice (Hamstring) would be the only one sidelined for the first practice of this week. “Rashee will be the only one who doesn’t go today,” Reid said during his opening statement. “Everybody else is scheduled to do something.” On Simmons, Reid made it clear this will be the start of working him back in. “Just going to ease him back in,” Reid said. “Ease him into practice, so he’s going to practice, but it will be on a limited basis.” Andy Reid says Josh Simmons will practice today and they’ll ease him back in. Rashee Rice will not practice today. pic.twitter.com/JgztoiHyKw — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) October 14, 2026 Simmons started missing practice during the final week of training camp in August and hasn’t been on the practice fields at One Arrowhead Drive since. His back flared up in the preseason, and Reid told local media that he was dealing with bulging discs a few weeks ago. Rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson has filled in admirably, but Simmons’ upside as a former first-round pick could elevate the offense further once he presumably returns to the starting lineup. Now, it’s about waiting to see when that will be, and how the rest of the lineup adjusts to Simmons’ return. “I haven’t even gone there,” Reid said about what a starting lineup with Simmons would look like. “I’m just glad he’s having the chance to come back, for sure. “When you start dealing with backs, you have to ease back in — if you can get back in at all — and see how he does,” Reid emphasized. “I know he’s wanting to get back out there and this is the first step of that.” Arrowhead Pride will share the official injury report from Wednesday’s practice this afternoon.
