title: Chiefs Rookie Report: Grading Peter Woods through four games
summary: Last week, the Kansas City Chiefs enjoyed the bye week with a perfect 4-0 record and the top position in the AFC. The first quarter of the Chiefs season went better than many anticipated, and the team has seen a slew of new faces making contributions early on. One of the new faces to see […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, the Kansas City Chiefs enjoyed the bye week with a perfect 4-0 record and the top position in the AFC. The first quarter of the Chiefs season went better than many anticipated, and the team has seen a slew of new faces making contributions early on. One of the new faces to see the field early has been rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods. The 30th-overall selection in this spring’s NFL Draft, Woods has been one of the Chiefs rookies playing extensive snaps early in the season. He hasn’t been overly productive through his first four career games, but flashes on film suggest a player the Chiefs should keep betting on as the season progresses. Let’s look at his four-game grades and film. Grades When evaluating Woods, I broke his grades into run-game wins and losses, one-on-one pass-rush wins and losses, and neutral pass-rush snaps, and tallied impact plays as well as pressures. I gave Woods a 71% grade for run defense this season, and this is where he has shone the brightest early on in his career. As for one-on-one pass-rush win rate, this is an area where he has struggled. In 17 true one-on-one pass-rush snaps, Woods has won only 5, around a 29% win rate, and I recorded only three pressures for Woods all season, with zero quarterback hits and zero sacks. He has been on the field for 48 of the plays I graded as “Neutral,” where the slide protection went his way or the play was a play-action or RPO look that took the defense out of the equation. I do have Woods recorded for five impact plays , not including pressures, that range from impressive plays in the run game to batted passes and high-level effort plays. Run defense Woods is far from a traditional defensive tackle run stuffer, and early in his career, he has used his athleticism to make plays in the run game. A strong point-of-attack player with good leverage, moving Woods off a spot can be hard for any player, including Las Vegas Raiders Pro Bowl Center Tyler Linderbaum. On the snap, Woods collides with Linderbaum in the backside A-gap on the Raiders’ trap run. As they meet, Woods stands his ground and tosses Linderbaum out of the picture, blowing up the play. Strength is one aspect of his game, and explosion is another. Lined up as the backside three technique against zone left, Woods explodes out of his stance and gives the right tackle no chance to block him. Woods makes the tackle for loss, showing how his quickness off the snap can make him “unblockable” against certain plays. Woods still has work to do on his technique, but defeating one-on-one run blocks has been where he’s been at his best this season. On the snap, he is late off the ball, but he has the lateral movement and strength to overcome the guard’s reach block and take away the lane the running back is looking for. One-on-one, Woods is a problem in the run game. He can still improve at holding double teams, but when it comes to penetrating quickly and beating reach blocks, he is hard to beat. One-on-one pass rush Woods’s most glaring issue so far has been his inability to create pass rush in one-on-one situations. He has shown glimpses but nothing consistent. Woods is at his best as a pass rusher when he has gap returns or uses his lateral mobility to quickly work through pass lanes before the offensive linemen can fully get a grip on him. On the snap, he quickly swats the left guard’s hands down, and without the running back delivering a chip block, he would have generated more pressure. Woods has been less effective when he has to engage and then work a move, but he has shown he can develop more pass-rush moves. Woods locks up with All-Pro Quenton Nelson, reading the run first. When the quarterback pulls the ball, Woods quickly uses a strong push-pull move to toss Nelson and apply pressure on the passer. The play action delayed Woods a bit, but the move was there. Given his lack of length, the push-pull is a good secondary move when quick wins don’t come with hand fighting or quick penetration. Woods still has room to grow as a rusher, but the tools are there. Motor Woods’ motor is undeniable, and it’s been on display multiple times throughout the first four games of the season. The quarterback fires a quick checkdown to the running back in the flat to avoid pressure from the opposite side of the field. On the snap, Woods is tasked with containing the quarterback, and that containment forces the quick pass. Woods has unique movement for a big man, and he doesn’t waste it. Hawking the back from behind, he makes the stop. With consistent effort like this, the next time Woods makes a play like this, it will likely be a fumble. The bottom line No young player is perfect, and Woods is no exception. While he lacks the elite length and size of other high-level defensive tackles, he has the mobility and strength few in the league possess. Seeing him excel in the run game during the early stages of his career is a great sign for Kansas City and gives him an area where he can provide value to the team while he continues to develop his pass rush arsenal. The rest of his season will be worth watching, and it will be interesting to see how the coaching staff uses him on pass-rush downs later this season.
author: Caleb James

title: Week 6 AP NFL Power Rankings: Patriots and Packers are on the rise
summary: Football is a beautiful, hilarious, and unpredictable game. The ball is oddly shaped, one of the worst teams can beat a good team any given day, and it’s ultimately the best drama we watch on television on a weekly basis. Week 5 had it all. It started with the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers upsetting the […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is a beautiful, hilarious, and unpredictable game. The ball is oddly shaped, one of the worst teams can beat a good team any given day, and it’s ultimately the best drama we watch on television on a weekly basis. Week 5 had it all. It started with the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers upsetting the Dallas Cowboys in Dallas. The drama continued Sunday morning, as the Philadelphia Eagles bumbled their lead with only eight seconds remaining after a special-teams gaffe against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Both “Sunday Night Football and “Monday Night Football” games went into overtime. All four NFC East teams played and finished the week 0-2-2. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo tried to win it for the Washington Commanders in overtime, but quarterback Jayden Daniels said, “No thanks.” We saw the first major trade before the deadline: the Arizona Cardinals shipped wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the one-win Houston Texans . Three teams remain undefeated, while an equal number remain winless. The season is just starting to heat up, and the Arrowhead Pride staff is back with updated power rankings. Biggest riser: Green Bay Packers +10 Biggest faller: Dallas Cowboys -7 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, Jared Sapp, and Matt Stagner . 1. San Francisco 49ers (1st) Kyle Shanahan has done an impressive job as head coach to start the season. What appears to be the cream of the NFL crop this season remains on top. 2. Kansas City Chiefs (2nd) I fully expect a classic Chiefs-Chargers thriller, in which we make the Chargers look 5-0 instead of 0-5, yet squeak out a win in spectacular fashion to preserve Andy Reid’s amazing post-bye-week record. 3. Baltimore Ravens (6th) We were subjected to the annual Snoop Huntley primetime game. And it did not disappoint. 4. Buffalo Bills (5th) Congratulations to Josh Allen on winning the first overtime game of his career. Running back James Cook tried to give the game away twice before it happened, however. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd) The London Jaguars won in incredible fashion on Sunday. 6. Minnesota Vikings (7th) Undoubtedly, Week 5 saw Kyler Murray’s best performance as a Viking. If he plays that well, this team could be a legitimate NFC contender. 7. Seattle Seahawks (4th) Sam Darnold hasn’t looked the same since his glute injury, and aside from JSN, this offense lacks the juice it once had. Chiefs fans owe the 12 a thank you. 8. Los Angeles Rams (8th) This season is on pace to age head coach Sean McVay a good 30 years. 9. Cincinnati Bengals (10th) The bye week could be coming at a great time for the Bengals to reset and get some dinged-up players healthy. They then face a favorable upcoming slate of opponents. Their next seven: Ravens, Titans, Falcons, Steelers, Commanders, Saints, and the Browns. 10. Chicago Bears (9th) Head coach Ben Johnson wanted blowouts. I’d say 31-7 suffices. 11. New England Patriots (16th) The Pats were a Bills’ blocked field goal away from being tied for first place in the AFC East. Who would have guessed that three weeks ago? 12. Denver Broncos (13th) I’m worried that despite the Broncos winning games, Bo Nix isn’t playing well enough to justify paying him 60 million per season. 13. Detroit Lions (15th) The Lions actually could have won this week without scoring over 30 points. 14. New York Giants (17th) Cam Skattebo owes Jayden Daniels a big thank you. 15. Philadelphia Eagles (11th) That had to be a long flight home. Horrible way to lose a football game. Three straight losses after a 2-0 start. 16. Green Bay Packers (26th) The Bears-Packers rivalry is one of the best in sports. I think that’s the only reason the Packers turned it around as they did on Sunday. 17. Carolina Panthers (20th) The Panthers remain in first place in the NFC South without having played a game. 18. Las Vegas Raiders (12th) The combined record of teams the Raiders beat: 1-14 The combined record of teams the Raiders lost to: 7-2 19. Pittsburgh Steelers (22nd) Jaylen Warren is small but mighty. 20. Atlanta Falcons (23rd) Apparently this team can only function if Michael Penix is under center. And unfortunately for the Falcons, his biggest problem is availability. 21. Dallas Cowboys (14th) You’ve reached an all-time low when the hot dog guy in the concourse is trash-talking on your quarterback. 22. Cleveland Browns (18th) Should have seen this one coming. They may have won three in a row, but I’m sorry. You just can’t be taken seriously from week to week, losing to the Jets. 23. Indianapolis Colts (19th) The very definition of “mid.” 24. Houston Texans (25th) I’m not sure the trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. solves any of this team’s issues. 25. New Orleans Saints (21st) The Saints’ offense has plummeted back down to earth. Facing the Vikings’ defense certainly doesn’t help matters. 26. Arizona Cardinals (24th) That Week 1 upset over the Chargers looks increasingly less impressive the further it gets in the rearview mirror. And it’s never a good sign to trade away a top-5 draft pick three years later. 27. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (30th) You could see Todd Bowles breathe a heavy sigh of relief on the sideline, as he likely saved his job with the upset win over the Cowboys. Also, give it up for KU alum Jalon Daniels. 28. New York Jets (28th) It’s almost Halloween, and the Jets aren’t completely irrelevant. 29. Washington Commanders (27th) I never saw the label “game manager” as a negative trait for a quarterback. And this game is a perfect example as to why. Your franchise quarterback simply cannot make that mistake at the end of the football game. But man, was it entertaining. 30. Miami Dolphins (31st) It’s now week 6. The Dolphins still haven’t held a lead this season. 31. Los Angeles Chargers (29th) “I’m not sure what the message is,” Jim Harbaugh said after the Chargers’ latest loss which dropped them to 0-5. Yeah, this team’s season is toast. 32. Tennessee Titans (32nd) One of my good buddies is a Titans fan. He told me this team may legitimately be one of the worst teams in NFL history.
author: Dakota Watson

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Jury returns mixed verdict in Tyreek Hill civil battery case, awards $500,000 to ex-wife | Pro Football Talk The civil lawsuit brought by Tyreek Hill’s ex-wife alleging multiple counts of battery and related legal claims has resulted in a verdict. Via Diana Moskovitz of Defector Media , the jury found Hill responsible for two counts of battery. He was found not responsible on the remaining counts. The jury awarded Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury did not enter an award of punitive damages. The jury’s decision not to award punitive damages is curious. Battery is an intentional tort. In Florida, however, the law requires “clear and convincing evidence” of intentional misconduct. It’s possible, in theory, that the jury found evidence of battery under the lower “preponderance of the evidence” standard but not “clear and convincing” proof, which is a higher bar. State shares boundaries for Kansas City Chiefs STAR Bonds District | KSHB 41 The district stretches across Wyandotte County and Johnson County, including KCK, Bonner Springs, Edwardsville, Shawnee, Lenexa and Olathe. The map excludes the University of Kansas Medical Center complex, a predominantly vacant portion of Shawnee and existing STAR bond districts. In a Kansas Department of Commerce press release, the state said the map was designed with “clear goals shared by the administration and the legislature.” Those goals include maximizing economic benefit and paying off bonds as quickly as possible. Long Time Ex-Chiefs’ 6-Year Veteran Re-Signs with Playoff Rivals 1 Day After Release | Heavy Sports “The Bills reversed the transaction they made to have CB Anthony Kendall on the 53-man roster for Monday’s game to help play slot CB in the absence of Dee Alford. Today they released Kendal & signed OLB Mike Danna back to the active roster.” Chris Brown, the team’s play-by-play radio broadcaster, posted on Tuesday. The day before, as Brown alluded to, the team made the opposite move and signed Kendall to the active roster and released Danna; a move that was designed to give the Bills more depth at nickel cornerback against the Rams on Monday night. The Jury Is Still Out on Chiefs’ Safety Room Following Bye Week | Sports Illustrated Starting with Gilman, the former Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens standout isn’t exactly lacking statistically compared to his last couple of seasons. Across Pro Football Reference , Pro Football Focus and NFL Pro ‘s data, his coverage data averages out to 10 targets and six completions, 8.3 yards per target and a 120.6 passer rating. He’s being tried more often down the field (13.9-yard average depth of target) and performing at his recent — albeit underwhelming — standard, but it’s the lack of ball production that’s really hurting. One of Gilman’s main draws is his ability to make splash plays, evidenced by his 28 career pass breakups, six fumble recoveries, five forced fumbles and five interceptions. Four games in, he’s been quiet, which is a concern. Chiefs star Travis Kelce now embraces a practice drill he once loathed | The Kansas City Star “Even after the whistle is blown and the play is so-called dead, defensive players are still running up to you trying to punch the ball out,” Kelce said of the training-camp drills. “And I don’t know why … it’s very annoying, especially when you’re in your third day of pads or sixth day of pads in seven days or whatever there was (at training camp), and you’re just getting … haymakered by linebackers and DBs down the field as you’re trying to, like, finish the play. So I was just being a (jerk) one day. I was like, I better see (teammates) throwing haymakers in the game, or I’m … pissed. Around the NFL 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw’s 1-game suspension upheld on appeal | The Athletic San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw’s one-game suspension has been upheld on appeal, the NFL announced Tuesday night. He will miss Monday night’s home game against the Washington Commanders and will be eligible to return Oct. 25 at the Atlanta Falcons. “Hearing officer James Thrash, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has upheld the one-game suspension of San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw,” Michael Signora, the NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, posted on social media. NFL suspends Rams’ Alaric Jackson for two games after punch | ESPN The NFL on Tuesday suspended Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games without pay after he punched Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s 37-34 overtime loss in Los Angeles. The league said Jackson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” “Have to make better decisions than that,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis after disastrous loss to Bills, sign Jets’ practice squad kicker | CBS Sports The Los Angeles Rams are making a special teams change on the heels of their 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. NFL Media reports the team is releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets’ practice squad. Mevis, affably known as “the Thiccer Kicker,” made all four of his extra-point attempts on Monday, but missed his two field-goal attempts. His first miss came from 50 yards in the first quarter, and his final miss came in overtime on a 48-yard game-winning attempt — a kick that was tipped by Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride How Chiefs’ receiver rotation could adjust without Tyquan Thornton Allen, on the other hand, could step into the big-play role that will be missing without Thornton. Last season at the University of Cincinnati, Allen caught 51 passes for 674 yards and an FBS-leading 13 touchdowns. Six of those scores came on throws of 20 or more yards downfield; 23% of Allen’s targets in 2025 were deep throws. During the preseason and training camp, Allen appeared to be developing chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on difficult throws, whether against tight coverage over the middle or on the sideline. Allen may not have Thornton’s linear speed, but his route running and ball skills could make up for it when the ball’s in the air. title: 2 kickers among potential trade targets for Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams cut kicker Harrison Mevis this week and immediately picked up Blake Grupe as a replacement, but that doesn’t mean that general manager Les Snead’s search is over. One — or even two — potential options could come on the trade market, specifically in the form of veterans on 0-5 teams who […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams cut kicker Harrison Mevis this week and immediately picked up Blake Grupe as a replacement , but that doesn’t mean that general manager Les Snead’s search is over. One — or even two — potential options could come on the trade market, specifically in the form of veterans on 0-5 teams who may be open to any type of deal that helps them in the future. Those kickers are Joey Slye of the Tennessee Titans and Riley Patterson of the Miami Dolphins, as noted by OvertheCap’s Nick Korte, they are cheap veterans on winless teams. Slye is due $1.16 million over the rest of the season, while Patterson is due $931,000. It’s cheap enough for L.A. to actually afford a trade . Whenever I start thinking about the trade deadline, my mind always drifts to vested veterans who are on the final season of their contracts. Here's the list of those players who are on the five 0-5 teams: pic.twitter.com/txAW6BxC80 — Nick Korte (@nickkorte) October 14, 2026 Slye is 5-of-6 on field goals this season and 5-of-5 on extra points. Playing on the Titans, Slye doesn’t get many chances to score. In his career, Slye has made 81.4% of his kicks, including 35-of-56 from 50+. Last season he went 28-of-35 with the Titans and 9-of-14 from 50+. It’s the type of leg that the Rams did not have with Mevis. Tennessee is Slye’s seventh team, however, indicating that he always loses the job eventually. Patterson is 7-of-9 with the Dolphins, and 5-of-6 on extra points. In six years, Patterson has struggled on long kicks, going just 7-of-14 from 50+. He’s been really accurate inside of 50, however. Miami is Patterson’s eighth team. The Rams are going with Grupe now. They might pivot to a kicker on a bad team in the future if Grupe doesn’t work out, which is totally within the real of possibilities.

title: The Rams should target Cedric Gray at the trade deadline
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams want to bolster their defense at the trade deadline, Tennessee Titans linebacker Cedric Gray should be near the top of their wish list. That’s a position of need for the Rams, while Gray himself has fallen out of favor with the Titans despite an especially productive 2025 campaign. Los Angeles […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams want to bolster their defense at the trade deadline, Tennessee Titans linebacker Cedric Gray should be near the top of their wish list. That’s a position of need for the Rams, while Gray himself has fallen out of favor with the Titans despite an especially productive 2025 campaign. Los Angeles isn’t necessarily the first destination you think of when it comes to taking a swing on a linebacker. Under coach Sean McVay, the Rams simply have not put much emphasis or capital into building their off-ball linebackers group . But in a year when you’ve already committed to going all-in for a Super Bowl title, there’s no better time than now to take a swing at an oft-neglected spot. Currently, Nate Landman is the Rams’ best off-ball linebacker, and to his credit he’s a fine player and contributor for defensive coordinator Chris Shula. Overall, he had a good game against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, flashing numerous times throughout the game. However, his limitations were also on display, such as on a long run by Bills quarterback Josh Allen in overtime when Landman was manning the middle of the field. Josh Allen GASHES the Rams defense AGAIN! 🔥 Another HUGE run for the Bills QB! pic.twitter.com/eyViuM6khl — J💥S Sports (@JordanOnSports1) October 13, 2026 He needs help, and the Rams need better depth when Landman isn’t on the field at all. That doesn’t happen often, considering all that’s currently asked of Landman (he played 89% of this week’s defensive snaps), but this would allow Shula to be more flexible with his personnel. CEDRIC GRAY For Gray’s part in this, it’s surprising that someone who was so productive just a season ago could now be on the trade block as some outlets have suggested . After all, he set the Titans’ franchise record for tackles in a single season last year with 164 stops, a bright spot in an otherwise miserable year for that franchise. A new coaching regime in Nashville has led to a much different story in 2026, however. Under the new Titans brain trust of coach Robert Saleh and defensive coordinator Gus Bradley, Gray has only played 44% of the Titans snaps in the four games he’s played. He’s also only been a starter in two of the four games after starting 16 a year ago. Saleh was asked about Gray’s playing time last week, and it didn’t make the playing time situation any clearer for the third-year pro. As of now, Cedric does a good job in the run game and pass game. Cody [Barton] is also a very good linebacker, really good communicator. When you look at nickel defense with Cody and Anthony [Hill Jr.], it has been a good combination for us. We’ve been going more dime, so only one linebacker is on the field on third down, so that’s bringing all the snap counts down also. So there’s a combination of different things. We’re doing a lot of different things personnel-wise. We’re playing with five D-linemen on the field several times a game. So, there’s certain things that are bringing both our snap counts down, but overall percentage-wise, it’s going to be similar. Something worth noting: Saleh and co. didn’t draft Gray. They did draft Hill. These things matter in the NFL. they should count this as two tackles for Cedric Gray pic.twitter.com/GYwaTaz9XI — Stoney Keeley (@StoneyKeeley) November 4, 2025 RAMS LINEBACKER OPTIONS The Rams also play a lot of dime and don’t need tons of linebackers all on the field at once. What they do need, however, is an influx of talent at the position. It also doesn’t quite match up that Gray can’t play as the dime linebacker if, in Saleh’s own words, Gray is good in both the run and pass games. We don’t need to oversell the caliber of player here. This isn’t a potential trade for a Fred Warner clone, or prime Brian Urlacher or anything like that. But it would be a talent upgrade at a position of need. The Rams want to keep up in the NFC arms race after an admittedly disappointing start to the season. The Titans have been brutal to start the year and there’s no light at the end of the tunnel for them for now. If they’re taking on calls on a player like Cedric Gray, it only makes sense for Los Angeles to keep going all in.

full_text: Nate Landman forces a lot of fumbles at the NFL level. He’s tied with TJ Watt for the most forced fumbled since 2024, and Landman darn near added to his fumble forcing legacy further last Monday night. Instead, the Rams lost, so maybe he didn’t add to any legacy, but Landman still did force a fumble and Landman almost put his team in a position to win the game. Legacy can be subjective. Landman said after the game he would’ve liked to have made a few more plays, but he also made a play that could’ve led to a win for his team. He’s done it more than once. Rams LB Nate Landman tied for NFL lead in this category since 2024 (ramswire) “ Los Angeles Rams linebacker Nate Landman has a nose for the football, and his “peanut punch” has jarred the ball loose from players’ hands time and time again. Monday night was no different, as Landman forced two fumbles on All-Pro running back James Cook, one of which was recovered by Aaron Donald. While the team was unable to jump on another loose ball, Landman’s prevalent skill has him with 10 forced fumbles since 2024. According to Sumer Sports , that’s tied with Pittsburgh Steelers star TJ Watt for the most in that span.“ Rams Signing Kicker Blake Grupe Is a Necessary Change That Was Long Overdue (sports.yahoo) “Through the first five weeks of the season, the Rams have had problems on special teams, primarily with the kicking operation. Heading into Monday’s game, Mevis was still just 5-for-7 and had a miss from 48 yards last week against the Eagles. In Monday night’s loss, Mevis missed from 50 yards and also had a potential game-winning kick blocked in overtime. While Mevis brought some stability to the kicking operation last season, there were always questions about his range. Mevis had been perfect with extra points and 19-for-20 inside of 45 yards. However, beyond 45 yards is where Mevis lacked consistency , and in today’s NFL, teams need a kicker who can hit from range when called upon.“ Sources: Rams release kicker Mevis after miscues in loss, sign Grupe from Jets (espn.com) “In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough,” McVay said. “It cost us the game tonight.” The Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL, according to ESPN Research. Los Angeles has had 81 missed or blocked kicks under McVay (since 2017, including playoffs), which is third most in the league.“ Rams OT Alaric Jackson Suspended 2 Games for Punching Bills Star (sports.yahoo) “Just in: Rams LT Alaric Jackson has been suspended 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb after their game on Monday night,” The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. “LA won’t have Jackson in Week 6 vs. Arizona and Week 7 vs Las Vegas.” “NFL punishes Rams’ Alaric Jackson for two games for punching Bills’ Bradley Chubb after the game ended as Chubb walked away, an ‘aggressive, non-football act entirely unwarranted, league informed Jackson in a disciplinary letter, per a source. Suspension ends after Rams Oct. 25 game vs. Raiders,” NFL reporter Aaron Wilson wrote on his official X account on Tuesday.“ Alaric Jackson suspended for striking Bradley Chubb after loss to Bills (nfl.com) “Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson is suspended for two games without pay after hitting Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb.” NFL Power Rankings, Week 6: Vikings, Patriots enter top 10; Eagles, Saints in free fall (nfl.com) “Five weeks into the 2026 NFL campaign, three teams remain undefeated and three squads have yet to log a win. Not sure many folks envisioned the Vikings being 5-0 or the Chargers being 0-5, but here we are. Every season brings surprises — that’s basically the key to this league’s popularity — and Week 5 certainly provided unexpected developments, including a few inexplicable finishes. So, how does the NFL hierarchy shake out after a week full of road wins? That’s the job in these here parts, and it’s a gig that demands viewing each situation in the micro and the macro before ultimately making decisions with conviction. Kind of like managing a football game. We saw some head coaches fail in that undertaking over the past few days. Hopefully, I acquit myself better here.“ Rams’ Sean McVay erupts over kicking unit after OT Collapse (sports.yahoo) “Buffalo capitalized on the extra possession, with Tyler Bass connecting on a 45-yard field goal of his own to finally end it. “In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough,” McVay said . “It cost us the game tonight.” He went further, second-guessing his own fourth-quarter decision-making as well. “I wish I would have had a better play call and gone for it, got it tighter,” he added, referring to a conservative third-down call that set up the eventual blocked attempt rather than pushing for better field position first.“ First Look: Rams host Cardinals at SoFi Stadium in Week 6 (therams.com) “ Hired former Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur as their new head coach on Feb. 1: A familiar name for Rams fans from the previous three seasons, LaFleur agreed to a five-year contract with Arizona to become the franchise’s next head coach after it moved on from Jonathan Gannon on Jan. 5. Selected former Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love with the No. 4 overall pick in this year’s draft: While Love has shared carries with veteran Tyler Allegeier – Love said last week the Cardinals’ coaches are managing his workload – he’s still the team’s leading rusher with 67 carries for 245 yards, with one rushing touchdown on the season.“ Rams Power Rankings: Week 6 (therams.com) “ Each week, TheRams.com will be taking an aggregate look at where the team ranks across different outlets in the sports media landscape. Here are the power rankings for the Rams heading into Week 6: “ Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis, sign K Blake Grupe off Jets’ practice squad (nfl.com) “His first miss was on a 50-yarder during the Rams’ opening drive, which allowed the Bills to keep a 3-0 lead. Mevis connected on his next four extra-point attempts, but disaster struck again when Buffalo’s Gregory Rousseau blocked his 48-yard game-winning try in overtime. That kicking misadventure was as much on Los Angeles’ linemen letting Rousseau surge through as it was on Mevis, but the ball’s trajectory did appear a bit low and to the left. Grupe, 27, was claimed off waivers by New York following August’s roster cutdown day, but was moved to the practice squad and did not kick for the Jets this season. He previously played for the Saints and Colts, and sports an 81.9 field-goal percentage with 98.0% accuracy on extra points over three seasons. The responsibility now falls to him to help rectify Los Angeles’ kicking woes.“ Comment(s) of the Day: “This disaster/joke of a year can’t end any sooner. This has been the worst season of football I’ve seen so far. I realistically gave up on the super bowl happening like most fans, this season appears already over. Losses like yesterday sink a season, the team is going to be demoralized. Seems McVay is starting to lose the locker room.” -STLRAMFAN27 “I don’t get why teams are so cheap with kickers. Think of how many games are won or lost by a missed or made FG, yet teams will spend draft capital and money on some rotation DL and cheap out on kickers. A good kicker is worth his weight in gold but the prevailing attitude is that teams can just pick up some scrub kicker off the waiver wire, or off the street, and he’ll kick well. In his prime, Justin Tucker was a huge advantage for the Ravens. You would think teams would gladly use a high round pick to get a great kicker, and pay him what that’s worth, but it doesn’t often work that way and we have seen how costly that has been for the Rams.” -KyrenW Feed post of the Day:

full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier Wednesday, ESPN reported that the Las Vegas Raiders are considering giving starting running back Ashton Jeanty a week off to help him recover from ankle and foot injuries. Later Wednesday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak swiftly shut down that notion. “He’s playing,” Kubiak said when asked about that idea. Kubiak also said Jeanty is “starting to feel a lot of better.” Kubiak suggested that Jeanty will practice fully this week as the Raiders prepare to host the 4-1 Buffalo Bills on Sunday as they try to snap a two-game losing streak. UPDATE: Jeanty practiced fully and the ankle injury was taken off the injury report. Jeanty was a game-day decision Sunday at New England after he missed practice time last week with a foot injury. He suffered an ankle injury in training camp. He has not missed any playing time this season. Meanwhile, as expected, starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway won’t practice Wednesday because he’s in the concussion protocol. His status for Sunday’s game is in question. Kubiak said the team hopes wide receiver Jalen Nailor returns to practice Thursday with hopes of playing Sunday. He missed the New England game due to a concussion. Also, the team opened the 21-day window to return from the injured reserve for deep backup tight end Carter Runyon. He has been out since early in training camp. Rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn returned to practice in a limited fashion after missing Week 5 with a knee injury.

title: Will Klint Kubiak finally unleash Mike Washington Jr?
summary: Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak held himself accountable for Mike Washington Jr.’s lack of playing time in the loss to the New England Patriots in his Monday afternoon press conference. full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak held himself accountable for Mike Washington Jr.’s lack of playing time in the loss to the New England Patriots in his Monday afternoon press conference. Initially, in the postgame presser on Sunday, Kubiak made some contradictory statements about the running game. However, the lack of a run game has become an issue that he must address. Washington ran all over the place in the preseason against the 2s, 3s, and 4s. With 25 regular-season carries, he has produced 125 yards and a touchdown. Averaged 5.0 yards per carry and owns the longest run of the season, 35 yards. What should earn him more touches is the 2.3 yards before contact and 2.7 yards after contact he is averaging per rush; both are team highs. Klint Kubiak said “it’s on me” to make sure that Mike Washington Jr. gets more reps moving forward after getting one carry against New England. The rookie running back has the #Raiders lone rushing touchdown this season and leading the team in yards per carry with five. — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) October 12, 2026 Ashton Jeanty is hurt. Jeanty may continue to display toughness and a willingness to fight through the pain. But at some point, his lack of production can’t continue to hold the team back. This season, Jeanty has carried the ball 88 times for 291 yards and is averaging 3.3 yards per carry. His pass-blocking ability, meshed with 215 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 22 catches, would indicate more of a third-down back or complementary role. Is Washington in the doghouse? Klint Kubiak said Dylan Laube’s uptick in usage is due to his ability to pass protect, saying the running back is a “reliable” player. #Raiders — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) October 12, 2026 Kubiak complimented Dylan Laube for his pass protection abilities. In doing so it seemed as though he was chiding Washington about his. Given the fact Kubiak has had to employ 7-man protection (max-protect) during passing attempts, it would make sense as to why Washington’s role was phased out in game. Raiders ran gap/power on 38% of their runs on Sunday which is their highest all season by far. Surprised they didn't use Washington Jr more with this gameplan. You can tell how natural he looks in a gap scheme on his only carry of the game. pic.twitter.com/wuVGc6E7uK — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) October 12, 2026 Regardless, the Raiders need fresh legs and ankles to make the offense less one-dimensional. Laube’s 2-yd score paired with Washington’s run against the New Orleans Saints remain the only rushing touchdowns in five weeks. That has to change. Washington is a big play waiting to happen and it’s up to Kubiak to take the leash off and let the big dog run.

title: 3 things about the Bills
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to be break a two-game losing streak against the Buffalo Bills at home Sunday. full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to be break a two-game losing streak against the Buffalo Bills at home Sunday. Here are three things to know about the 4-1 Bills: Josh Allen is a monster: The Bills’ quarterback could be on his way to another MVP season. He has thrown seven touchdown passes and has run for eight more this season. He leads all NFL players in rushing touchdowns. A week after getting shredded by Drake Maye in New England, the Raiders now have to deal with Allen. Not fun. James Cook is also dangerous: Cook has ran for, at least, 111 yards in three of the Bills’ five games. The Raiders have had issues stopping the run at times this season. While Allen is the centerpiece, the Raiders most focus on stopping Cook as well. Cook does have some ball-security issues as he fumbled twice in a Week 5 win over the Rams. The Raiders have had success forcing fumbles this season. They will go after Cook. Defense is struggling: Yes, the Bills can score in bunches, but they need it. The Buffalo defense has had big trouble under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Buffalo has allowed, at least, 29 points in four of their five games. Rams’ star receiver Puka Nacua had 17 catches for 138 yards in Week 5. Brock Bowers could go off.

summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Buffalo Bills: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 53 percent of the snaps at […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Buffalo Bills: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 53 percent of the snaps at New England as he was playing through foot and ankle injuries. He continued to struggle as he had 27 rushing yards on 10 carries. He also continued to have trouble holding onto the ball as a receiver. Perhaps he will have better health Sunday as he tries to regain his Week 1 form. Jack Bech: The second-round pick is on the injured reserve with a fractured forearm and will likely be out for several more weeks. Darien Porter: The third-round pick played 50 defensive snaps after playing just three in Week 4. He took over the primary outside cornerbacks role over rookie Zeke Masses, who took Porter’s job earlier in the season. Porter has a chance to get the majority of the snaps against the high-powered Bills’ offense Sunday. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick was back on the bench with starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson back in the lineup after being out with a groin injury. Rogers did play four snaps on special teams. However, perhaps he will be in the mix at left guard if the team benches the struggling Spencer Burford. Coach Klint Kubiak said this week there could be competition to help the struggling line. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual, but he did log four snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, is in the 21-day practice window to return from the injured reserve. Thornton is coming back from a hamstring injury and helps he could be activated this week. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick suffered a concussion at New England and his status for Sunday may be in jeopardy. He is the leading snap getter at defensive tackle so the Raiders will miss Hemingway if he can’t play Sunday. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was inactive for the fourth time in five games. He was active in Week 4. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 17 snaps on special teams.

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: What Moves Should The Vikings Make?
summary: The Vikings have a bye this week as you all know. I believe the team always does self scouting and probably is looking for ways to improve the roster. The team has clearly had its fair share of injury already. Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver being out for the season really stinks but the show […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Byron Murphy Jr. #7 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts after an interception against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings have a bye this week as you all know. I believe the team always does self scouting and probably is looking for ways to improve the roster. The team has clearly had its fair share of injury already. Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver being out for the season really stinks but the show must go on. Not having Mason for the last few weeks and having Addison miss the last game after Jefferson missed the previous two sure makes it difficult to build chemistry. It also makes it tough to self scout because you have yet to see your hoped for starting offensive unit even play one full game together. What can they scout? How not to get injured? Obviously they will want to get the pre-snap penalties cleaned up. They will want to get Kyler deeper into the offense to that he will know the plays really well. I do not know what happens with a QB but I imagine he is just thinking of his progressions and maybe not intuitively knowing where the other receivers are on a given play. I am sure they know but do they really truly automatically and instinctively go to the next options quickly? Regardless of Kyler Murray staying here longer than this season, the team needs to have one QB in the system for at least 3 to 4 years. Is that too much to ask? Kyler did not see Jennings wide open for a TD and it is perplexing because the way he was throwing it, it seemed like an easy completion. What did KOC say? Time on task right? That is what the offense needs the most. In fact, Kyler echoed that exact same phrase word-for-word after the Saints win. When he was asked why the offense finally looked sharper, he flat out said it came down to “time on task, getting more comfortable in this offense with Kevin.” Self scouting the defense is tougher. A lot tougher. What can they possibly want to get better at? I would say pressures. The blitz rate and success has helped to mask the pressure from the interior. Maybe that is by design because of the youths? Either way, we need to up the ante and get even more out of the front. With the trade deadline approaching, are there any moves that make sense? We all would love to get another interior lineman but they are hard to come by during the season due to injuries. They might be able to get a tight end from another team. Maybe? The Bengals and Rams come to mind. Running back is a popular choice but Mason should be returning after the bye. I am thinking Edge rusher. How about this trade with the Chiefs … Jauan Jennings plus a 2027 7th for Felix Anudike-Uzomah and a 2026 6th The question is why would the Chiefs move on from FAU? Well, he was injured in 2025 and they did not pick up his fifth year option. He is a free agent next year just like Jennings. FAU has maybe been miscast in their scheme. Bringing him here and allowing him to stand up and rush the passer could be beneficial. Another idea that could be already out there is a trade with the Dolphins … A 2027 conditional 6th for Josh Uche. … Uche is a free agent next year and the Dolphins are winless. They signed him to a minimum level deal and while they might want to keep him next year, it could prove tough if he sours on their environment. at the same time, he is playing well for them and opposite Chop Robinson. Having a starting spot and a likely massive increase in pay next year is reason for him to stay and for the Dolphins to not move him. I like this one but I doubt it gets done. Are there any moves you can dream up? Minnesota Vikings News and Links NFL Power Rankings: 5-0 Start Helps Vikings Reach Top 5 https://www.vikings.com/news/nfl-power-rankings-week-5-undefeated-start-top-5 No. 7 (up 4 spots): Nick Shook – NFL.com I know the Vikings have a truly special defense. I’d been wondering whether their offense would ever show up. We saw signs of it in the second half against the Saints, a stretch in which Kyler Murray dropped a pass over three defenders into Justin Jefferson’s bucket for a touchdown and led an attack that scored 17 points in the final two quarters. There are still plenty of kinks to work out, but Murray is beginning to look more comfortable in Kevin O’Connell’s system. … No. 3 (up 3 spots): Kris Knox – Bleacher Report The Minnesota Vikings moved to 5-0 on Sunday, and for the first time this season, things seemed to be clicking in all phases. Having Justin Jefferson back in the lineup was huge, and it helped Kyler Murray deliver his best performance as a Viking so far. Aaron Jones, Sr., returned from a first-quarter knee injury and ran for 113 yards, while Minnesota’s defense held the New Orleans Saints to a mere 142 total yards. The Vikings defense has looked championship-caliber all season. If Murray and the offense can continue to make positive strides after next week’s bye, this team could remain undefeated for the foreseeable future. … No. 3 (no change): Pete Prisco – CBS Sports [The Vikings] just keep on winning with their defense. But the offense showed some life with Kyler Murray in the victory over the Saints. … No. 4 (up 2 spots): Vinnie Iyer – Sporting News The Vikings are getting it done where it counts, even though they might not seem to be so clean from game to game. They are up to 10 takeaways in five games and now rank second in time of possession (33:37) after having the ball for almost 40 minutes vs. the Saints. Kevin O’Connell on Evolution of Vikings Offense, Roster Depth Demonstrated Against Saints https://www.vikings.com/news/kevin-oconnell-evolution-of-offense-roster-depth-against-saints Aaron Jones, Sr., continued to be a warrior in the run game, and Kyler Murray “spit completions” all afternoon while extending plays with his legs. “I do feel like we’re growing and we’re creating space in the run game. We’re running it at a high clip,” said O’Connell, noting the team’s ability “to impose our will late in the game.” “It’s very positive,” he said. “I think we’ll continue to see the evolution of how we put it all together, the impact of Kyler throwing a bunch of completions. I think he’s [completed] 40 of his [past] 48 pass attempts. We’ve really seen him click into a comfort [level] playing the position — using his athleticism, being a factor with his legs and protecting himself while doing it. “I’m excited about what’s coming for us offensively,” O’Connell added. “I’ve kind of envisioned it being like that from the beginning of the season, and we’ve been able to win football games as we progress, but ultimately to maximize who we want to be as a team, where our offense is going to be a big part of that.” No 1. Mobility from Murray Sunday’s game against the Saints felt a little “vintage Kyler Murray” in the number of ways he implemented his mobility. O’Connell explained it’s “not an every-down thing, and we don’t really want to put parameters too much of ‘Here’s when you do it, here’s when you don’t.’ ” Having the ability to call on Murray’s athleticism, though, is hugely valuable. “To me, it’s the fundamentals of it. It’s the progression,” O’Connell said. “Obviously some elite-level throws like the touchdown to Justin [Jefferson] and some other plays kind of off-schedule where he kept his eyes up and found some people. summary: It’s Wednesday, which must mean that it’s time for another member of the Minnesota Vikings to be recognized by the league with another award of some sort. This time, however, it isn’t a member of the league’s best special teams unit. It’s a member of the league’s best defense instead. The league has just announced […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Byron Murphy Jr. #7 of the Minnesota Vikings makes an interception during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Wednesday, which must mean that it’s time for another member of the Minnesota Vikings to be recognized by the league with another award of some sort. This time, however, it isn’t a member of the league’s best special teams unit. It’s a member of the league’s best defense instead. MURPH! @byronmurphy has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after his 2-INT performance in New Orleans. 📰: https://t.co/MMez61Nttp pic.twitter.com/rdaLBLKrXu — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) October 14, 2026 The league has just announced that Vikings cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. has been named the NFC’s Defensive Player of the Week for his performance against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. Murphy intercepted Saints’ quarterback Tyler Shough twice in the Vikings’ 23-13 win in New Orleans this past Sunday, with both of them coming in the second half. That made him the first Viking to record multiple interceptions in a game since Camryn Bynum did it in Week 7 of the 2023 season against San Francisco. He’s also the first Vikings player to have two interceptions in a game and at least one tackle for a loss since Harrison Smith did so in Week 16 of the 2017 season in Green Bay. Murphy is currently tied for the NFL lead in interceptions with three, and has played a role in the Vikings’ defense as a team putting up ten turnovers this season, tied for the second-most in the NFL. This is the fourth consecutive week that a member of the Vikings has brought home a weekly award. Members of the Vikings brought home Special Teams Player of the Week honors in Weeks 2, 3, and 4 of this season, but this is the first Defensive Player of the Week Award for the team this year. Unfortunately, the Vikings won’t get an opportunity to run their streak to five weeks in a row, as they’ll be taking Week 6 off to rest for their bye week. We’ll see if they pick up where they left off when they host the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7. Congratulations to Byron Murphy Jr. on being named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season!

title: What A.J. Brown returning to practice means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots returned to the practice fields on Wednesday, and so did A.J. Brown. Exactly five weeks after suffering a high ankle sprain in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, the star wide receiver made his comeback. While only participating on a limited basis, Brown’s return is an encouraging step forward for […]
full_text: The New England Patriots returned to the practice fields on Wednesday, and so did A.J. Brown . Exactly five weeks after suffering a high ankle sprain in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, the star wide receiver made his comeback. While only participating on a limited basis , Brown’s return is an encouraging step forward for both him and the team alike. Let’s assess what else it means from a big-picture perspective. Clock starts ticking Brown returning to practice and getting designated to come back off of injured reserve means that he is now officially eligible to play in this week’s game against the New York Jets. Whether he actually will be activated for the contest remains to be seen. “He hasn’t been out there for four weeks, so we’ll get him back out there practicing and see if he’s ready to go in a couple days,” said head coach Mike Vrabel. “If not, then we have a 21-day window, and we’ll go from there.” As Vrabel mentioned, the team is in no rush: it has 21 days to make that call before the return window shuts close again and he would revert back to IR to end his season. That, of course, is an outcome not expected to happen. In fact, it seems more likely that Brown will be back on the 53-man roster sooner rather than later. Much-needed boost The Patriots offense has suffered some more losses since initially seeing Brown go down with his sprained ankle in Week 1. Wide receiver Mack Hollins, fullback Reggie Gilliam and right guard Mike Onwenu plus his replacement, Greg Van Roten, have all since joined him on injured reserve. In the meantime, tight end Eli Raridon also missed time due to injury, while left tackle Will Campbell and running back TreVeyon Henderson are facing unclear outlooks after sustaining knee and ankle injuries during the Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The Patriots offense has had to take its hits over the last month, so getting somebody back — especially of the quality of Brown — should be a natural boost for the unit. At the very least, it adds more depth at a receiver position that has performed admirably recently but still became relatively thinned-out after Hollins was injured. Tip of the iceberg Brown’s return to practice was not the only good news coming out of Foxborough on Wednesday. The Patriots also saw offensive tackle Marcus Bryant make his own comeback after he started the season on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In addition, cornerback Christian Gonzalez returned after missing the last two weeks with a shoulder injury; the Pro Bowler classifies himself as “ready to go” this week against the Jets. Furthermore, there were two surprising participants at practice on Wednesday. The aforementioned Will Campbell was part of the session as a limited participant, despite his status reportedly being “week to week” — a distinction he changed to “day by day” when talking to the media in the locker room. Also on the field was TreVeyon Henderson, who reportedly is set to “miss multiple weeks” but did take the field. Long story short, in a season marred by injuries so far, Wednesday was a definitive positive. Another return spot taken NFL teams are allowed to bring up to eight players back from injured reserve during the season, under the condition that they were either sent to the list after the league’s roster cutdown deadline or labeled as “designated to return” right away when sent to IR on cutdown day itself. This means that the Patriots have now made use of two of those spots. The first was used on Marcus Bryant when he was sent to IR ahead of the late-August roster cuts. Now, a second spot has been taken by Brown and his return to practice. This leaves the Patriots with six available return spots, regardless of whether or not Brown or Bryant actually do get activated to the 53-man roster. Players eligible to fill those openings on the return list include FB Reggie Gilliam, WR Mack Hollins, RG Mike Onwenu, OL Greg Van Roten, ED Quintayvious Hutchins, LB Khalil Jacobs, S Dell Pettus and P Bryce Baringer — which means that at least two of them won’t be brought back.

Brown (ankle — IR return) OT Will Campbell (knee) OT Morgan Moses (foot) OT Marcus Bryant (ankle — IR return) LB Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder) LB Christian Elliss (chest) CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) CB Marcus Jones (ankle) CB Charles Woods (shoulder) CB Channing Canada (hamstring) S Kevin Byard III (chest) S Craig Woodson (shoulder) Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle — IR return) TE Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) S Dane Belton (knee) A total of 13 Patriots practiced in a partial capacity on Wednesday. Gonzalez was among four corners in that tier. But after being downgraded from questionable to out last weekend, the initial two selections in the franchise’s 2025 draft class were notably present. title: Patriots open A.J. Brown’s 21-day window to return from injured reserve
summary: The New England Patriots set sights on the New York Jets with reinforcements from injured reserve. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced during his Wednesday press conference that the organization has opened the practice windows for wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant. Both now have a 21-day runway to be activated back to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots set sights on the New York Jets with reinforcements from injured reserve. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced during his Wednesday press conference that the organization has opened the practice windows for wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant. Both now have a 21-day runway to be activated back to the 53-man roster. Brown, 29, sustained a high ankle sprain in the season opener versus the Seattle Seahawks and spent the past four games on injured reserve before becoming eligible to return this week. The June trade acquisition from the Philadelphia Eagles caught three passes for 26 yards during his brief 2026 debut. He headed to the locker room in the third quarter of what became a 13-10 loss at Lumen Field. Now, with fellow veteran receiver Mack Hollins landing on IR due to a calf injury , the rest of the active depth chart includes Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. “I think his routine was really good, ability to be around guys in the meetings was good, and then also focus on his rehab,” Vrabel said of Brown, whom his former Tennessee Titans selected in the second round of the 2019 NFL draft at No. 51 overall. “Just treated everything as a pro, be where he’s supposed to be and work hard to get back.” Landing in Foxborough in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder, Brown’s career spans three Pro Bowls, three All-Pros as well as a Super Bowl LIX ring. The 6-foot-1, 226-pound Ole Miss product has amassed 527 receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns across 106 games and 98 starts out wide. “He hasn’t been out there for four weeks,” added Vrabel, “so we’ll get him back out there practicing and see if he’s ready to go in a couple days. And if not, 21-day window and we’ll go from there.” The same goes for the swing tackle that had been designated for return as clubs around the league reduced from 90-plus active players in August. Bryant, 24, started New England’s preseason opener at left tackle and got the nod at right tackle the following week, as well. Yet on the offense’s first drive of that exhibition, the 6-foot-7, 320-pounder got rolled up on and headed from the blue medical tent to the locker room. He had remained sidelined since then despite being eligible to resume practicing last week. Selected in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL draft at No. 220 overall, Bryant outlasted the 53-man deadline as a rookie. The former transfer from Southern Methodist to Missouri went on to appear in 12 games last regular season, handling 19 snaps on offense and 56 snaps on special teams. His practice window opens only days after starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a right knee injury against the Las Vegas Raiders and was replaced by rookie No. 28 overall pick Caleb Lomu on the blindside. The 3-2 Patriots currently carry one open spot on the active roster and a full practice squad after recently adding running back Hassan Haskins and cornerback D’Shawn Jamison. Sunday’s AFC East kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots vs. Raiders snap counts from Week 5
summary: Missing Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada, the New England Patriots were depleted at cornerback entering their Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Add the fact that Charles Woods was questionable before the game with a shoulder injury, and you get a situation that can best be described as dire. […]
full_text: Missing Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada, the New England Patriots were depleted at cornerback entering their Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Add the fact that Charles Woods was questionable before the game with a shoulder injury, and you get a situation that can best be described as dire. In order to provide some depth and still maintain a level of flexibility, the Patriots promoted Kindle Vildor from the practice squad to the 53-man roster leading up to the contest. And they then immediately threw him into the fire: playing 44 of 60 defensive snaps, he ended the game second among New England’s cornerbacks behind only Marcus jones. His impact went beyond his playing time. The March signing also had four tackles, a pass breakup and a forced fumble. “He gets a PBU, gets a big punch out there, changes the momentum, helps us get the drive stopped,” said head coach Mike Vrabel on Monday. “I think one of the coaches was talking and said, ‘Well, he had a mental error on the play, but he also had an extra effort.’ And so, I think that really defines what we want our identity to be, the ability to have an error or a mistake, but also the ability to go finish, still impact the play and know that a mental error doesn’t have to necessarily mean that the play is over or a mistake. It certainly doesn’t limit our ability to finish.” Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 45-17 win . Offense Total snaps: 75 | Time on the field: 33:38 | * denotes starter QB Drake Maye* (75; 100%), LG Alijah Vera-Tucker* (75; 100%), C Jared Wilson* (75; 100%), RG Ben Brown* (75; 100%), RT Morgan Moses* (75; 100%), WR Romeo Doubs* (62; 83%), WR Efton Chism III* (57; 76%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (53; 71%), LT/TE Caleb Lomu (49; 65%), TE Hunter Henry* (48; 64%), TE Eli Raridon* (43; 57%), WR DeMario Douglas (37; 49%), LT Will Campbell* (28; 37%), WR Kyle Williams (27; 36%), RB Corey Kiner (15; 20%), TE/FB Tanner Arkin (15; 20%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (12; 16%), TE Cameron Latu (4; 5%) Despite the game’s blowout nature, the Patriots kept their starters in the game to the final whistle. This meant that quarterback Drake Maye and four fifths of the offensive line went wire-to-wire. The lone exception was left tackle Will Campbell, who exited the game with a knee injury in the second quarter and is considered “week to week.” In his place, first-round rookie Caleb Lomu saw playing time at left tackle for the first time in his NFL career. Campbell was not the only prominent player to depart and not return. TreVeyon Henderson got banged up on the end of an 11-yard carry in the second quarter, and he is expected to be out “multiple weeks” due to the high ankle sprain he sustained on the play. Third-stringer Corey Kiner saw increased snaps with Henderson absent; he finished with 52 yards and a fumble on six carries. The Patriots also had to replace some other injured players. Mack Hollins’ role in the offense was filled by Efton Chism, who finished tied for the team lead with five catches. Fullback Reggie Gilliam’s role, meanwhile, transferred to tight end Tanner Arkin. Defense Total snaps: 60 | Time on the field: 24:10 | * denotes starter LB Robert Spillane* (50; 83%), LB Christian Elliss* (50; 83%), C B Marcus Jones* (50; 83%), S Craig Woodson* (50; 83%), S Kevin Byard III* (50; 83%), CB Kindle Vildor (44; 73%), DT Milton Williams* (42; 70%), ED Gabe Jacas (39; 65%), ED Elijah Ponder* (36; 60%), CB Charles Woods* (36; 60%), ED Dre’Mont Jones* (34; 57%), DT Christian Barmore (27; 45%), S Jaylen Reed (22; 37%), S Mike Brown (22; 37%), DT DaQuan Jones (21; 35%), DT Cory Durden* (16; 27%), DT Joshua Farmer* (15; 25%), DT Leonard Taylor III (11; 18%), LB Darius Muasau (11; 18%), LB Namdi Obiazor (10; 17%), S Brenden Schooler (10; 17%), S Elliott Davison (10; 17%), LB Erick Hunter (4; 7%) Besides the aforementioned Kindle Vildor, the Patriots relied on Marcus Jones and Charles Woods at cornerback. Together with safeties Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard, who both played all 50 relatively meaningful snaps on Sunday, they formed the foundation of New England’s secondary against the Raiders. Safeties Jaylen Reed and Mike Brown also were given a relatively high number of snaps, with the former coming on as a nickel back to help defend Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Up front, the Patriots again relied heavily on young edges Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder. Dre’Mont Jones also was part of the mix, but he exited the game in the early fourth quarter and did not return. In the middle, Leonard Taylor notched a sack in his 11 snaps. The blowout nature of the game also allowed New England to give some of its backup defenders some extended reps, with linebackers Darius Muasau, Namdi Obiazor and Erick Hunter, and safeties Brenden Schooler and Elliott Davison all seeing action late. Special teams Total snaps: 29 | Time on the field: 2:12 | * denotes starter TE Cameron Latu (24; 83%), S Brenden Schooler (22; 76%), LB Namdi Obiazor (21, 72%), S/PP Mike Brown (21, 72%), LB Darius Muasau (20; 69%), S Jaylen Reed (19; 66%), S Elliott Davison (19; 66%), LB Erick Hunter (16; 55%), K Andy Borregales (15; 52%), RB Corey Kiner (14; 48%), LB K.J. Britt (14; 48%), DT Cory Durden (11; 38%), P/H Mitch Wishnowsky (9; 31%), LS Julian Ashby (9; 31%), OT Caleb Lomu (7; 24%), OL Alijah Vera-Tucker (7; 24%), OL Ben Brown (7; 24%), DT Leonard Taylor III (7; 24%), ED Gabe Jacas (7; 24%), ED Elijah Ponder (7; 24%), OL Matt Pryor (7; 24%), OL Walter Rouse (7; 24%), CB/PR Marcus Jones (5; 17%), DT Milton Williams (5; 17%), DT DaQuan Jones (5; 17%), WR/KR Kyle Williams (3; 10%), TE Tanner Arkin (3; 10%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (1; 3%), WR Romeo Doubs (1; 3%), TE Hunter Henry (1; 3%), LB Robert Spillane (1; 3%), LB Christian Elliss (1; 3%), S Kevin Byard III (1; 3%), DT Joshua Farmer (1; 3%) Brenden Schooler made his return after starting the season on the non-football injury list, and he immediately resumes his role as a core special teamer: Schooler played on all four of the punt and kickoff teams, including as a gunner on the punt coverage team. Despite his return, however, Erick Hunter continued playing gunner as well. Besides those two, the other core-four special teamers included Cameron Latu, Namdi Obiazor, Mike Brown and Elliott Davison. Meanwhile, K.J. Britt effectively replaces Reggie Gilliam in the kicking game after being elevated from the practice squad. Did not play QB Tommy DeVito Even though the Patriots won by 28 points, Mike Vrabel decided against pulling Drake Maye from the contest. His season-long snap count therefore stays at 12, with all of them coming in a Week 3 loss in Jacksonville. Inactive QB3 Behren Morton, OT Dametrious Crownover, CB Christian Gonzalez, CB Carlton Davis III, CB Channing Canada, CB Karon Prunty Besides the aforementioned four cornerbacks, including starters Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis, the Patriots’ list of inactives featured two healthy scratches. Neither Behren Morton nor Dametrious Crownover have roles beyond emergency status at this point in their respective careers.

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Jets ahead of Week 6
summary: Some familiar faces will meet again at Gillette Stadium. Here’s a glance through the list of former Patriots and former Jets ahead […]
full_text: Some familiar faces will meet again at Gillette Stadium. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, seven players in the fold for Sunday’s AFC East matchup have been both New England Patriots and New York Jets during their NFL careers. Here’s a glance through the list of former Patriots and former Jets ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff. NEW YORK Andrew Beck, fullback — Entering the NFL as part of the 2019 undrafted class in Foxborough, Beck was waived by the Patriots at the 53-man roster deadline following his rookie training camp. The Texas Longhorns product was claimed by the Denver Broncos that Labor Day weekend and has since taken the field for 92 games, including 24 starts. A past recipient of the NFL’s Salute to Service Award, his career includes 31 receptions for 259 yards and five touchdowns. The 30-year-old fullback has also lent a hand with one rushing touchdown. Beck made his way back to the AFC East as a futures signing in 2025 after stints with the Green Bay Packers and Houston Texans. Chukwuma Okorafor, offensive tackle — Eleven months into a one-year deal, the Patriots released Okorafor before waiting for the 2025 league year to open. The offensive tackle played 12 snaps on the blindside in his lone New England start before being replaced and placed on the left squad list. He reverted to the reserves for the remainder of that 4-13 campaign after the club’s roster exemption expired. Okorafor has gone on to sign consecutive one-year pacts with the Jets. He has appeared in 19 games during his time in Florham Park, with 62 of his 63 downs coming in the kicking game. The 29-year-old originally entered the league with the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third round of the 2018 draft at No. 92 overall. A Western Michigan alum, his run spans 97 games and 60 starts. NEW ENGLAND Morgan Moses, offensive tackle — Voted a team captain out of training camp, Moses has played 1,349 offensive snaps for the Patriots since arriving on a three-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. The 35-year-old right tackle has started all 22 games in the regular season over that span. Entering the NFL out of Virginia in the third round of the 2014 draft at No. 66 overall, Moses finds himself with 188 appearances and 180 starts on his odometer. He made previous stops with the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens. And he’s been a Jet twice, as well, beginning in 2021 and circling back in 2024 via trade. A total of 30 starts were notched during his previous tours in the division. Alijah Vera-Tucker, guard — The Patriots landed Vera-Tucker on a three-year agreement as NFL free agency kicked off in March. The veteran addition has started all five contests at left guard this fall and stayed in for 100 perfect of the workload for the offensive line. He finds himself the team’s last ironman at this point in October. Selected by the Jets in the first round of the 2021 draft class at No. 14 overall, Vera-Tucker appeared in 43 out of a possible 85 games with his previous employer. The past PFWA All-Rookie honoree from USC sustained a torn triceps in 2022, a torn Achilles in 2023 and a torn triceps in 2025. When healthy, the 27-year-old has started every game he’s appeared in during his time in the league. Greg Van Roten, guard — Van Roten was placed on New England’s injured reserve at the end of September after suffering a thigh injury during his first start of the year at right guard. He had been called upon there after tenured incumbent Mike Onwenu landed on injured reserve due to a fractured ankle. The 36-year-old Van Roten visited Gillette Stadium during training camp and soon returned to a sign a one-year deal. A veteran of 147 games, including 106 starts, the former All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn began his career as an undrafted rookie in 2012. He has been a member of nine different NFL organizations in addition to the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts over the years since then. Count the Jets among the previous. Van Roten started 23 of his 30 games before being released in the spring of 2022 with one year left on a three-year pact. Xavier Newman-Johnson, guard — After being hosted by the Patriots as a free agent midway through September, Newman-Johnson signed to the practice squad. The 27-year-old interior offensive lineman had been released from the Jets’ practice squad before headed to Foxborough. He stands 25 games into his run in the NFL and with a handful of starts. Originally entering the league with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022, the Baylor product spent parts of two campaigns with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former team before heading to the AFC East. Newman-Johnson, who resided between the practice squad, 53-man roster and injured reserve while in Florham Park, has seen 338 snaps on offense and 68 snaps on special teams. Leonard Taylor III, defensive tackle — The Patriots added Taylor to the practice squad one October ago after he cleared waivers via the Jets. The 27-year-old defensive tackle went on to become a seven-time standard elevation on the journey to Super Bowl LX and reached a futures contract in February. Nine tackles and a blocked field goal in the AFC title game had been registered by then. Taylor worked his way onto the initial 53-man roster entering 2026. He got the first sack of his stay with the defending division winners last Sunday. The 2024 undrafted free agent by way of the Miami Hurricanes checked into 16 games while with New York, tallying 27 tackles, 2.5 sacks and a pair of batted passes.

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants
summary: I want to start this week’s report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don’t disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I want to start this week’s report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don’t disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn’t lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it’s not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson’s injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he’s back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn’t perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it’s clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough’s development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it’s also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn’t great when he came in. I don’t think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn’t be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price’s release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson
